articleTitle: Protocol conversion technology based on edge computing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This research develops a protocol mediation framework demonstrating three critical advancements in IoT interoperability: multi-protocol adaptability, throughputoptimized conversion, and modular extensibility. The methodology employs a canonical intermediate data representation during bidirectional translation processes, successfully validating operational efficacy across MQTT, HTTP, and MODBUS standards. Experimental evaluations confirm negligible throughput impairment compared to native protocol handling, while maintaining linear implementation complexity growth when integrating new protocols. Current limitations stem from configuration verbosity in mapping rule specifications, necessitating future development of enhanced declarative syntax to streamline conversion rule definitions.

articleTitle: The research on rehabilitation evaluation algorithm for frozen shoulder based on kinect
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Shoulder disorders, such as frozen shoulder, cause significant upper limb dysfunction, severely affecting patients’ quality of life. Existing rehabilitation systems are costly and offer limited interactivity. This paper proposes a DTW algorithm with a relaxed endpoint diamond constraint band and time derivative sequence matching to improve evaluation and training efficiency. Using Kinect 2.0 for data acquisition and joint angles and distances as matching features, the algorithm was tested on a custom dataset in a Unity3D evaluation environment. The algorithm achieved a recognition accuracy of $96.79 \%$, with an average execution time of 1.114 s. The results show that the proposed algorithm efficiently assesses shoulder rehabilitation and is appropriate for patient training.

articleTitle: A Trajectory Unified Framework for Deep Neural Network Training in Imbalanced Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optimization method designed to address the challenges of training deep neural networks on imbalanced datasets. The main contributions include the proposal of a novel trajectory-unified method based on the influence balance factor, which adaptively reweights samples to alleviate the overfitting of decision boundaries to the majority class. In this paper a rigorous theoretical framework is presented that validates the stability and convergence properties of the proposed method. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this method outperforms cutting-edge techniques in handling class imbalance issues. In summary, this approach effectively tackles the challenges posed by imbalanced data distribution, providing a systematically enhanced solution to the class imbalance problem in advanced deep learning models.

articleTitle: A Transfer Learning and Time-Frequency Fusion Framework for Few-Shot Modulation Classification in LEO Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the challenge of low classification accuracy in small sample scenarios encountered by automatic modulation classification (AMC) in low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems, this paper proposes a multiscale encoder framework based on transfer learning. First, by combining continuous wavelet transform to extract time-frequency features and fusing signal I/Q data, the feature robustness under large Doppler effects is enhanced. Then the model adopts a source domain pre-training and target domain fine-tuning strategy, designs a data adaptation module to solve the difference in cross-domain data length, and combines local convolutional encoders with global attention mechanisms to achieve multi-scale feature fusion. Experiments show that under limited training samples, the classification accuracy of the model is significantly better than the benchmark models, especially in distinguishing QAM, PSK and APSK signals, which verifies the effectiveness of transfer learning and multi-scale feature fusion.

articleTitle: Joint Entity and Relation Extraction Based on Large Language Model and Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Joint extraction of entity and relation from unstructured text is a critical task in information extraction. Although current methods have achieved considerable performance, they still suffer from inherent limitations such as imbalanced label distribution in datasets, insufficient consideration of the complex structural features of entity relationships. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel approach by proposing a joint entity and relation extraction framework based on Large Language Model (LLM) and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN). Specifically, the model employs a strategy that enhances data using LLM, assisting the expansion of corpora with fewer labels. Subsequently, a GCN component is designed to fully explore the complex structural features of entity and relation within sentences. Finally, a biaffine classification component is developed to align entity and relation into matrix form, making it easier to capture triples. A wide range of experiments was carried out on two datasets, namely The New York Times (NYT) and Web Natural Language Generation (WebNLG). The results of the experiments show that this approach reaches state-of-the-art performance, maintaining stable extraction capabilities while capturing more entity pairs, further validating its effectiveness in addressing the overlapping triples problem.

Author Keywords: joint extraction of entities and relations

articleTitle: Predicting Olympic Medal Counts: A Random Forest Regression with Monte Carlo Simulation Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: At every Olympic Games, the medal tally is often the focal point of global attention. In this paper, we take a different approach by leveraging regression analysis on historical data features to predict medal counts. We built a feature-enhanced random forest regression model incorporating Monte Carlo simulation, and Monte Carlo simulation is used to provide uncertainty intervals for the prediction. MSE and $R 2$ of gold medals prediction model is 5.08 and 0.856, and total medals prediction model is 39.85 and 0.842, which indicates our model fits well. We analyze the feature importance in the random forest model to get our original insights as well as recommendations to the Olympic Committee. Additionally, we performed sensitivity analysis to explore the impact of input variations on the model. One of the feature variables went up and down by $10 \%$ when the data went up and down by $13 \%$, reflecting excellent model sensitivity.

articleTitle: Research on Network Public Opinion Prediction Based on Exponential Smoothing Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the problems of rapid dissemination of online public opinion, significant social impact, and susceptibility to major emergencies, this article conducts research on the pre calculation method of online public opinion. Firstly, based on the process of online public opinion dissemination, clarify the lifecycle process and characteristics of online public opinion; Secondly, starting from the influence weight of public opinion dissemination, the core variables of online public opinion information dissemination were established, and on this basis, a network public opinion evolution model was constructed; Furthermore, considering the high volatility of online public opinion during the diffusion period, a network public opinion prediction method based on exponential smoothing is proposed; Finally, the effectiveness of the prediction method was verified through case data analysis.

articleTitle: Dual Attention Mechanisms-Embedded Deep Learning Method for Video Subtle Motion Magnification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Video subtle motion magnification technology is widely used in engineering monitoring, but deep learning methods often suffer from quality degradation at high magnifications. This paper proposes a dual-attention mechanism (coordinate attention + self-attention) for video motion magnification. It enhances texture representation and reduces artifacts. Experiments show a 3.5dB PSNR and 0.026 SSIM improvement on the Baby video.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy-PI Kalman time synchronization for wireless local area network systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: High - precision time synchronization is critically important for applications in wireless local area networks (WLANs). In practical scenarios, time synchronization is sensitive to tempera-ture variations. Moreover, as the WLAN experiences fluctuations, the time synchronization exhibits low accuracy and poor robustness due to the severe jitter of the uncertain delays during the synchronization process. This paper establishes the time model and time skew model of the real-time system in WLANs, and proposes the Fuzzy-PI temperature compensation Kalman (Fuzzy-PI TCK) algorithm to track and compensate for the time synchronization errors. In scenarios where the WLAN endures high-bandwidth operations and long-distance data transmission, while simultaneously being plagued by multiple co-frequency interferences, and the temperature of the system undergoes fluctuations, the experimental results demonstrate that the time synchronization accuracy is better than $1 \mu$ s and remains stable. Furthermore, the parameters of the Kalman filter and PI controller can be adaptively adjusted online, demonstrating excellent adaptability to diverse operating conditions.

articleTitle: Multi-Text-Reading References Recommendation Method of Learning Traditional Chinese Literary Using Large Language Model AI Assistant
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) based AI assistants are being widely applied in the academic field of education. This article aims to address the difficulties encountered by vocational college students in learning classical Chinese literature, for they may easily lose their interest and motivation while dealing with such difficult grammar and semantics. Considering of our teaching objectives and educational intentions, based on the cultural and Interesting characteristics of classical Chinese historical biographical literature works, and exploiting advantages of multi-text-reading teaching and learning instructions, we use the ChatGPT-like LLM AI assistants’ abilities of natural language understanding, logical reasoning, and content generation to design variables, rules, and algorithms for a multi-text-reading reading literature recommendation model for teaching and learning of classical Chinese historical biographical literature works from seven dimensions. A chain prompt engineering template is also designed for the ChatGPT-like LLMs. The experimental results show that the recommendation model and template we designed have a high degree of fit with our teaching objectives.

articleTitle: Analysis of The Effect of Multiple False Target Jamming Based on CFAR Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Multiple false target jamming interferes with radar devices by generating false target signals to mask the echo signals of the true target. It can be seen from the principle of jamming that the false target interval is the key parameter that determines its interference effect. In this paper, the influence of the change of false target interval on the interference effect is deeply analysed through theoretical derivation and simulation verification, combined with the radar constant false alarm rate detection method. The results show that the false target interval determines the number of false targets in the reference cells of the constant false alarm rate detector. By setting different values, it affects the change in the constant false alarm rate detection threshold, thereby enabling effective interference with the radar.

articleTitle: Research on Artifact Removal in Brain-Computer Interfaces Based on Deep Learning Fusion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As an emerging human-machine interaction technology, brain-computer interface (BCI) has broad application prospects. However, various artifacts existing in electroencephalogram (EEG) signals seriously affect the performance of BCI systems. This paper proposes a method based on a deep learning fusion algorithm to remove artifacts from EEG signals. This method combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), adopts a fusion strategy with a channel attention mechanism, and constructs a deep learning fusion model. Compared with traditional methods, the fusion algorithm proposed in this paper can effectively remove artifacts from EEG signals, providing a new solution for improving the accuracy and reliability of BCI systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Economic Distribution in Electric Power Systems Utilizing an Adaptive Immune Cloning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to establish a balanced distribution of power and minimize generation costs within the power system, we propose an adaptive immune clone algorithm grounded in a mathematical model for economic load allocation. This algorithm incorporates concepts such as scaling transformation, elite clone mutation, heuristic clone crossover, and clone selection, which theoretically improve solution diversity. Simulations conducted on a power system consisting of three machines and six buses produced results that validate the algorithm’s effectiveness. When compared to genetic algorithms, the enhanced algorithm demonstrates superior global search capabilities, a diminished likelihood of converging on local optima, and a quicker convergence rate.

articleTitle: Research on the Application Framework of AR Technology in Engineering Sites
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In view of the problems such as the complexity of the construction site, numerous potential safety hazards, and low efficiency of manual supervision in engineering projects, this paper proposes an engineering site management and control framework based on AR technology. The hardware platform of the construction site monitoring system is adopted, and the on - site construction monitoring data of each terminal is transmitted through the monitoring center. A data storage algorithm is introduced to completely AR - reconstruct the on - site construction data. The experimental results show that the system proposed in this paper has low data transmission pressure, low latency, smooth operation without freezing, and further enhances the immersion of monitoring.

articleTitle: Research on a Spindle Speed-Based Periodic Segmentation Regression Method for Rotor Vibration Data in Aircraft Engines
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the operation of rotating machinery, the analysis and evaluation of vibration signals are crucial for condition monitoring and fault diagnosis. Due to the complex structure and harsh working environment of aero-engines, challenges such as insufficient fault identification samples and vibration data loss are common. Traditional methods for handling missing data often fail to fully restore the hidden information in the original signals, resulting in suboptimal signal reconstruction. In recent years, deep learning techniques, especially Transformer models, have shown good performance in time-series data analysis. However, they still face limitations such as fixed input lengths and high computational complexity. To address these issues, we proposes an RPMTST network based on spindle speed periodic segmentation, aiming to effectively predict and reconstruct missing vibration signals, particularly capturing local variations in the signal. Experimental validation using public datasets demonstrates that the proposed model significantly improves the accuracy of signal reconstruction and fault prediction. This provides more reliable support for condition monitoring and fault detection in aero-engines, contributing to the safe and stable operation of mechanical systems.

articleTitle: SPONGE: A Scalable Heterogeneous Chiplet Accelerator Architecture for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With advancements in packaging and die-to-die interconnect technologies, multi-chip modules (MCMs) offer a viable approach to building systems ranging from edge devices to data-center scales using fine-grained DNN chiplets. This approach significantly reduces both fabrication and design costs. However, there is currently no Chiplet accelerator specifically designed for autonomous driving scenarios. Thus, in this work, we propose a Scalable Heterogeneous Chiplet Accelerator architecture for Autonomous Driving, which consists of compute chiplets and a dual-functional IO chiplet. The compute chiplets include a global buffer, a computing engine, and a network communication engine. The dual-functional IO chiplet integrates interface IPs at its edge, with SRAM filling the central unused area enlarged by the edge IPs. These two types of chiplets can be freely combined to form various accelerator configurations. In addition, we propose a pipeline mapping strategy to efficiently utilize these compute and storage units. Overall, Sponge’s hardware and software optimizations reduce latency by $\mathbf{7 8. 2 \%}$ on average and reduce energy consumption by $53.6 \%$ compared to a baseline system using the state-of-the-art Tangram mapping strategy, optimized by us, across a wide range of DNNs.

articleTitle: Study on the effectiveness of brain dynamic network clustering with standardized distances in space-time constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the traditional clustering method in dynamic functional connection (DFC) analysis is sensitive to data distribution and ignores the continuity of time series, this paper proposes an improved clustering effectiveness evaluation framework based on spatiotemporal characteristics. Firstly, the Standardized Corrected Distance (NCD) was designed to replace the Euclidean measure, and the distance weight was dynamically adjusted by the standard deviation of the feature dimension to solve the problem of BOLD signal scale difference in multiple brain regions. Secondly, the penalty term for state transition between sliding windows was introduced to construct the spatiotemporal joint optimization objective function to constrain the physiological rationality of state switching in the brain network. The reconstruction of the evaluation function is further integrated to improve the stability of the optimal clustering number selection. In the SimTB simulation data test, the accuracy of the proposed method in the three-classification and five-classification tasks reaches $84 \%$ and $80 \%$, which is improved compared with the traditional method, and the variance of state dwell time variation is reduced. Empirical studies based on ASD autism dataset show that the accuracy of health and disease classification is higher when the optimal cluster number $\text{k}=4$. This method provides a more reliable dynamic connectivity quantification tool for the study of brain disease heterogeneity, and shows potential application value in the analysis of dynamic functional connectivity in the diagnosis of brain diseases.

articleTitle: Contrast Sample Pre-selection for Augmentation-Free Graph Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, contrastive learning has become a dominant approach in graph self-supervised learning. However, most existing graph contrastive learning methods rely on the homophily assumption, leading to poor performance on heterophilic graphs. Developing contrastive learning methods that are effective for both homophilic and heterophilic graphs remains an important challenge. Among these methods, augmentation-free contrastive learning has gained attention due to its simplicity. However, existing approaches typically select positive samples based on similarity in the representation space, making them heavily dependent on the quality of node representations produced by the graph encoder in the early training stages. In this paper, we propose a contrastive learning method that directly determines positive sample pairs from raw graph data, avoiding the reliance on unstable early-stage sample selection. We leverage feature similarity and neighborhood similarity in the original graph data to select positive samples. Through different model parameter initialization strategies, we demonstrate that our method mitigates the adverse effects of low-quality node representations during training. Extensive experiments on various datasets further validate the effectiveness and generalizability of our method across both homophilic and heterophilic graphs.

articleTitle: Network Intrusion Detection System Based on BERT-MLP Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: A Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) is a tool designed to identify potential cyber threats. In recent years, leveraging machine learning algorithms to develop NIDS has emerged as an effective solution for intrusion detection. However, traditional machine learning-based algorithms, due to their limited adaptability, have not been widely adopted in NIDS. This paper proposes a BERT-MLP-based NIDS model. To address the class imbalance issue in power information system datasets, a Classifier Generative Adversarial Network (ACGAN) is employed. Network traffic data is converted into natural language-like sequences through feature encoding, and the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) is innovatively introduced to extract contextual features from the traffic. A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is then integrated to construct an end-to-end classification model, which outputs the probability of traffic classification. The proposed method was tested on a power information system dataset, with results demonstrating superior performance in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. These findings validate the model’ s ability to effectively capture spatiotemporal correlation features in traffic sequences, significantly enhance robustness in detecting novel attacks, and provide a new technical pathway for safeguarding power information systems.

articleTitle: Research on Performance Optimization of Embedded Microcontrollers Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the performance optimization of embedded microcontrollers using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). With the continuous development of the Internet of Things and edge - computing technologies, embedded microcontrollers are required to handle complex tasks such as image and signal processing. CNNs, renowned for their outstanding performance in feature extraction and pattern recognition, offer a promising solution for enhancing the capabilities of embedded microcontrollers. This research first reviews the basic principles of CNNs and embedded microcontrollers. Then, it delves into the challenges of integrating CNNs into embedded microcontrollers, including limited computing resources and power consumption constraints. Through in - depth experimental studies, real - world data is collected and analyzed to evaluate the impact of different optimization strategies on the performance of embedded microcontrollers. The results show that through appropriate optimization methods, the performance of embedded microcontrollers in tasks related to CNN - based processing can be significantly improved, which has important practical significance for promoting the application of CNNs in the field of embedded systems.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Allocation of Educational Resources Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the problem of unequal distribution of education in some regions, a model for the allocation of learning resources based on the difference evolution algorithm is proposed. Using actual data and textbook resource allocation examples from teachers in six districts and cities, this study compares and analyzes the learning outcomes of resource allocation using simulation simulation. The results show that compared to the learning resource allocation model based on the combined model, this model has a similar work distribution, and at the same time, it is not easy, and it allows for effective learning resource allocation and educational management decision making.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fusion Strategies and Feature Extractors for Improved Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In multimodal sentiment analysis, the combination of fusion models and feature extractors is crucial, and there is significant room for improvement in feature extractors to achieve higher accuracy. Most existing image feature extractors do not use Attention mechanisms, which have shown great success in text processing. In this paper, I first tested various fusion models on the MVSA-single dataset, and then selected the optimal fusion medels to test different text feature extraction pre-trained models. Next, based on the previous steps, I tested several different image feature extraction pre-trained models. Finally, under the optimal combination of fusion strategy and text feature extractor, I improved a single image model by adding various Attention mechanisms and tested their impact. Based on this, the same improvements were applied to multiple image feature extractors. For different image feature extractors, the accuracy increased by $1 \%$ to $5 \%$ compared to the baseline.

articleTitle: A Denoising Method for Event Streams with Graph Attention and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Event cameras enable high dynamic range and low latency for 3D reconstruction, but indoor noise degrades accuracy. Traditional methods are limited by static thresholds or high computation costs. We propose a GAT-Transformer denoising method that retains event characteristics via spatio-temporal sampling, extracts features with GAT, and classifies events using Transformer. Experiments show lower noise retention and higher signal preservation compared to existing methods, enhancing indoor 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: Contextual Parameters’ Impact on Sentiment Polarity Determination
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study proposes a deep learning-based sentiment analysis framework integrated with Halliday’s contextual theory, constructing a context-aware model by deconstructing three-dimensional parameters of field, tenor, and mode. We develop a Contextual Configuration Matrix to quantify domain-specific term density (NI), social power gradient (PG), and rhetorical structure (RST), while designing an attention mechanism for dynamic fusion of contextual features and semantic sentiment. Experiments on dual-domain datasets (2,800 medical consultations and 3,500 e-commerce reviews) demonstrate that introducing contextual parameters improves sentiment classification F1-scores by 14.2% (medical: 0.82 $\rightarrow 0.89$; ecommerce: $0.76 \rightarrow 0.84$) and effectively resolves $23.7 \%$ of domaindependent sentiment ambiguities (e.g., “flexible” shows $61 \%$ negative polarity in medical contexts vs. $89 \%$ positive in ecommerce). This work validates Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL) as an interpretable pathway for contextual modeling in sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Dangerous Driving Behavior Monitoring System based on Raspberry PI 5
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: According to the domestic and foreign highway traffic safety accident reports, driver fatigue driving and distracted driving are the main causes of traffic safety accidents, and the concealment and severity of accidents are much higher than others. Therefore, vehicle driving behavior monitoring plays an important role in reducing traffic accidents. This paper proposes a method based on image processing technology to detect fatigue driving and distracted driving. For the former, this paper uses the 68-aspect feature point detection algorithm encapsulated in the Dlib library, and extracts facial fatigue information through the shape detector of Dlib for face recognition and eye and mouth location tracking. For the latter, this paper proposes a driving behavior recognition method based on YOLOv5-Lite, a lightweight object detection model, which still has a good detection effect while reducing the calculation amount, so that it can be easily deployed to edge devices. The Python Flask micro framework and FRP (Fast Reverse Proxy) Intranet penetration tool are used to realize remote real-time web monitoring of drivers, complete the overall function of the system, and can effectively reduce road traffic safety accidents.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation for EEG-based SSVEP Decoding
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)based neural decoding (BCIs) play a crucial role in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). However, traditional machine learning algorithms often face SSVEP decoding stability challenges due to the inherent multi-class small-sample pattern recognition, along with external factors such as noise interference or subject fatigue, resulting in unsatisfied performance. To solve this limitation, a data augmented decoding algorithm is proposed by applying Gaussian noise to SSVEP signals to enhance the robustness of traditional machine learning-based SSVEP decoding algorithms. This method was evaluated on selected subjects with initially low decoding accuracy in the public SSVEP dataset, showing significant performance improvement, with an average accuracy increase of $8.33 \%$. The proposed approach effectively improves the robustness of SSVEP decoding with a straightforward manner and facilitates the broader application of SSVEP in practical BCIs.

articleTitle: YOLO-lite: A novel lightweight model for underwater object detection using large model and graph structure
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Underwater object detection is essential for ocean exploration but presents significant challenges, including poor performance in detecting small objects, environmental complexity, and high computational demands that hinder deployment on underwater robots. To tackle these issues, this study enhances YOLOv5 by introducing a graph-based multiscale feature fusion mechanism, which improves feature integration across layers. Additionally, an auxiliary training branch is incorporated, utilizing semantic segmentation images as supervision signals to enhance small object detection accuracy without increasing inference complexity. To facilitate deployment on edge devices, the model is lightweighted by pruning 70% of its parameters using a Batch Normalization (BN) layer pruning method, achieving a substantial reduction in size and a boost in inference speed with minimal accuracy loss. The optimized model achieves a 3.1 mAP improvement, runs at 100 fps (frames per second) on the Jetson Nano edge device, and satisfies real-time underwater detection requirements. This approach demonstrates potential applicability to other small object detection tasks and edge deployment scenarios.

articleTitle: Utility of Knowledge Graphs in Enhancing Cloud-Based LLMs: A Meta-Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the growing complexity of tasks requiring factual accuracy, multi-hop reasoning, and domain-specific knowledge, knowledge graphs (KGs) have emerged as a valuable complement to large language models (LLMs). However, as tasks and experimental setups vary due to different objectives, some studies report improved question answering performance through combination, while others report only negligible effects. Therefore, in this article, we review and synthesize findings from a range of studies that explore various methods for integrating KGs with LLMs, focusing on their impact on model performance. Our analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of current integration strategies, identifies emerging trends in KG-LLM research, and suggests areas for further investigation. This paper also examines how KGs contribute to overcoming the inherent challenges faced by LLMs, such as hallucination and inefficiency, and explores the potential for further advancements in combining structured knowledge with LLMs to achieve more reliable, scalable, and interpretable systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of RFID-based Student Management System for Higher Education Students
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an RFID-based student management system for higher education institutions. The system adopts a B/S architecture integrating RFID technology, cloud database, and web platform to achieve automated student attendance tracking and access management. Through functional and performance testing with 500 simulated users, the system demonstrated high reliability with over $98 \%$ success rate in data collection and attendance management, maintaining response times under 280 ms at peak loads. The results indicate that RFID technology significantly improves automation efficiency and management accuracy in campus environments, providing a practical solution for intelligent student management.

articleTitle: Improved Steger Line Laser Stripe Centerline Extraction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The extraction of the central line of laser stripes is a crucial technique in three-dimensional measurement. To overcome the limitations of existing algorithms for central line extraction, particularly in terms of speed and accuracy, this paper proposes an enhanced version of the Steger algorithm that incorporates parallel-accelerated Gaussian filtering and adaptive Gaussian templates. Initially, an adaptive Gaussian template is utilized, wherein the width of the light stripe at various positions is estimated to generate the Gaussian template. Subsequently, Gaussian filtering is applied to improve the accuracy of central line extraction. This method effectively mitigates the impact of surface contamination and reflection artifacts. Furthermore, the algorithm enhances processing speed through parallel execution. Experimental results indicate that the enhanced algorithm extracts central lines that are smoother, more coherent, and more accurate. By computing the standard deviation of central line extraction across various image types, it is observed that the error in the enhanced Steger algorithm has decreased by $16.6 \%$ on average.

articleTitle: On Clustering Algorithms for Cognitive Diagnosis Based on Item Responses
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Cognitive diagnosis in education and psychology reveals students’ knowledge grasp, aiding in personalized learning and targeted interventions. As it evolves, researchers are increasingly focusing on nonparametric methods like clustering, which traditionally groups subjects into unlabeled clusters based on similarity. The novel proposed clustering average distance algorithm(C-ADA) is used to label the estimated clustering results based on the subjects’ observed response patterns. At the same time, the corresponding proof is given. It serves as a supportive tool for future clustering in this field. Simulation studies show that the C-ADA resolves the unlabeled problem. The effectiveness and applicability of this method are also investigated.

articleTitle: A Feature-Based Method for Evaluating the Quality of Heterogeneous Image Matching
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Image matching is a critical area of research in computer vision, with widespread applications in scene matching, image retrieval, and autonomous driving. However, accurately evaluating image matching quality without ground truth data remains a significant challenge. This paper presents a novel image matching quality evaluation method based on the Enhanced Generalized Dual-Bootstrap Iterative Closest Point (E-GDB-ICP) algorithm. The method begins by using GDB features for robust image representation, followed by feature point selection and determination of the image’s orientation based on the principal direction of the feature points. Finally, a matching evaluation function is employed to score the image matching quality. The method is extensively validated across various image datasets, including heterogeneous remote sensing and building images, and compared with traditional image matching evaluation methods. Results show that the proposed method not only accurately assesses matching quality for these images but also demonstrates superior robustness and adaptability in complex scenarios. These findings confirm the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method for evaluating image matching quality in the absence of ground truth data.

articleTitle: Research on the Quantitative Evaluation System for Simulation Training Effects
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To enhance the objectivity and real-time nature of simulation training effect evaluation, this paper constructs a multilevel quantitative evaluation model by integrating the fuzzy theory and big data technology. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is employed to determine the weights of evaluation indicators. The fuzzy theory is utilized to quantify the uncertainties in the evaluation process, and big data technology is introduced to optimize the data collection, storage, and analysis processes. A distributed computing framework is used to process massive training data, machine learning algorithms are combined to optimize the weight allocation, and dynamic evaluation results are generated through real-time data flow analysis. Taking the redblue formation confrontation training as an example, an evaluation system based on big data is designed to achieve multidimensional analysis and visualization of training effects.

articleTitle: Design of Automatic Test Platform for 400G QSFP112G Optical Module
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the accelerated intelligent transformation of the manufacturing industry, the demand for high-speed optical modules is growing rapidly. The 400 G optical module with QSFP112 package form gradually replaces the low-speed optical module as the mainstream product in the market, but there is no complete set of automatic test platform and corresponding test software in the market, which causes the difference in the quality of the module performance validation and product testing due to the difference in the manual operation, validation process, and test equipment, so the purpose of this thesis is to design an automatic test platform for 400 G QSFP112 optical module that meets the QSFP112 MSA and Multi-source Protocol standards. Multisource protocol standards of 400 G QSFP112G optical module automatic test platform. The core objective of this system is to construct an efficient and reliable automatic test platform by analyzing the working principle of optical modules in depth, and starting from three perspectives: hardware equipment construction of the test platform, design of the test board, and software development. The test results show that the automatic test platform can meet the performance test of 400 G QSFP112 optical modules and the results meet the IEEE 400GBASE-DR4 standard.

articleTitle: Research on PCB Defect Detection Based on YOLOv8n-DDS
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the challenges of insufficient detection accuracy, real-time performance, and lightweight design caused by the diversity of PCB defect features, varying shapes, and sizes, this study proposes an improved algorithm based on YOLOv8n, named YOLOv8n-DDS. First, the Deformable Convolutional Network v2 (DCNv2) module is integrated into the first and second C2F modules of the backbone network. This module dynamically adjusts sampling positions and weights, enabling the model to better capture geometric deformations and complex features of targets. Second, the Dilated Widthwise Residual (DWR) module is introduced into the third and fourth C2F modules of the backbone network. This module employs dilated convolutions to expand the receptive field without increasing parameter count or computational complexity. Finally, the SEAM attention mechanism is incorporated into the detection head (Head) to enhance the model’s focus on critical features and improve recognition capability. Experimental results on a PCB defect dataset demonstrate that the YOLOv8n-DDS model achieves improvements of $26.3 \%, 12.4 \%, 19.4 \%$, and $27.6 \%$ in precision (P), recall (R), mean average precision (mAP) and frames per second (FPS), respectively, while reducing GFLOPs and model size by $13.6 \%$ and $7.7 \%$. compared to the baseline YOLOv8n. These results validate the superior comprehensive performance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: An Optimized RDMA Scheme for Efficient VM Synchronization in QEMU Checkpoints
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In virtualization, ensuring high availability and reliability for critical business applications can be achieved through Fault Tolerance (FT) solutions. QEMU, a popular open-source virtualization platform, employs Coarse-grained lock-stepping (COLO) to maintain high availability by synchronizing states of the Primary Virtual Machine (PVM) and the Secondary Virtual Machine (SVM). The high-speed synchronization process of COLO checkpoints involves efficient data transfer, which is crucial for service continuity. In Ethernet-based virtual machine data transmission, Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) offers superior performance in reducing latency and increasing throughput compared to TCP/UDP. However, the original RDMA implementation in QEMU’s COLO process is limited, constraining its efficiency. This paper proposes an improved RDMA scheme for QEMU FT, based on the compressed transmission of dirty pages, enhancing COLO checkpoint synchronization in bandwidth-constrained environments. In experimental evaluations conducted in a 10 Gbps network environment, our scheme achieved a $5.26 \%$ to $14.09 \%$ improvement in Oracle tests, and a $\mathbf{1. 7 7 \%}$ to $\mathbf{3 1. 0 3 \%}$ improvement across various tests in MySQL. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our scheme in enhancing FT performance under different database workloads, further validating its potential for widespread application in cloud data center virtualization environments.

articleTitle: Design of Analog Neuron Circuit with ReLU Activation Function
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative analog neuron circuit design, subtly implementing ReLU activation function. This analogy neuron mainly consists of two parts. The first part is about linear processing, which responses for weighted summation of input signals. In our design, with the use of hardware circuit, it is able to assign desired weight to signals from different inputs. The other part is activation function circuit. In this part, we designed four different circuits. Proteus simulation results indicate that all four circuits can implement ReLU function well. With precision rectifier circuit selected, the output voltage has a strong ReLU relationship with the input, while the other circuits have their advantages and disadvantages. Additionally, the diode clamp circuit realizes ELU function approximately, which provides a new idea for the design of analog neurons.

articleTitle: Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation Based on Multi-Strategy Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Fully-supervised semantic segmentation has advanced notably with deep learning, yet its dependence on large amounts of precisely pixel-level annotated data brings high costs, hampering wide application. Weakly-supervised semantic segmentation helps reduce this burden, but current methods still lack in fully covering the target regions and utilizing contextual information. This paper proposes a weakly-supervised semantic segmentation method via multi-strategy collaboration. By combining regional feature expansion, contextual awareness, and feature enhancement fusion, it improves the model’s target recognition and segmentation accuracy. Experiments show that our method surpasses existing techniques on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 datasets, offering an effective solution for weakly-supervised semantic segmentation.

articleTitle: Drone Assisted Freight Transport in Highway Logistics Coordinated Scheduling and Route Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study aims to improve the drone-highway collaborative transport model to enhance efficiency and reduce operational costs. A multi-objective optimization model was developed using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) combined with the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. Based on empirical data from the Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway (G42), the effectiveness of the drone-assisted transport model was analyzed across different scenarios. The results show that drone collaboration effectively alleviates peak-hour congestion, enhances long-distance transport efficiency and performs particularly well in tasks ranging from 100 to 400 km. The findings indicate that during peak hours (8:00–10:00, 18:00–20:00), the drone-assisted model maintains transport efficiency above $82 \%$. For long-distance transport, travel time is reduced by $14 \%-18 \%$, while perunit operating costs decrease by $9.5 \%-18 \%$. Additionally, the study finds that improving drone scheduling requires balancing transport demand and resource allocation. The most significant time savings occur when scheduling falls between 5 and 15 times, with diminishing returns beyond 15. Further analysis highlights that well-developed intelligent transport infrastructure plays a key role in enhancing drone delivery performance. In particular, a well-planned layout of takeoff and landing sites with V2X communication support can improve scheduling accuracy and reduce transport uncertainties. This study provides theoretical support for integrating drones into highway logistics and offers recommendations for improving drone endurance, refining smart scheduling algorithms, strengthening regulatory frameworks and advancing infrastructure development to foster the growth of low-altitude economy in smart logistics.

articleTitle: Improved EO fusion DWA for sand fixation robot path planning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To achieve autonomous navigation of sand fixing robot in a dynamic environment, improved EO fusion DWA is proposed for sand fixing robot path planning. In global path planning, covariance learning is proposed for the initiating concentration of the traditional EO algorithm to establish the connection between initial concentrations, which is easy to jump out of the local optimum; sinusoidal adjustment factors are proposed for the exponential term coefficients to balance the exploration and mining ability of the algorithm; and a new fitness function is added to measure the superiority or inferiority of the global path. Use quadratic path optimization to improve path smoothing. Incorporate DWA algorithm for local path planning. Simulation results show that the algorithm in this paper can not only effectively shorten the path distance but also effectively avoid obstacles in complex environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cross-Domain Graph Classification with Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Graph classification, as one of the core issues in graph data analysis, demonstrates significant application value in scenarios such as chemical molecular property prediction and protein function analysis. Given that graph data contains both domain-specific feature knowledge and structural knowledge with lower domain dependency, transferring and integrating structural knowledge across heterogeneous graph models from different domains is a viable approach to enhancing graph classification performance in each domain. Motivated by this, we propose a multi-teacher knowledge distillation framework tailored for heterogeneous cross-domain graph data. Under the federated learning setting, this framework effectively utilizes and transfers the structural knowledge embedded in different domain-specific graph models through knowledge distillation. Specifically, the framework employs a knowledge separation model to separate structural knowledge from feature knowledge, where the structural knowledge module takes domain-independent node structural vectors as input, while the feature knowledge module retains local personalized training. Furthermore, the framework incorporates a multi-teacher knowledge distillation mechanism within the federated graph learning setting to fully transfer structural features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods in various cross-domain settings for graph classification.

articleTitle: AGCL: Attention Aggregation Contrastive Learning for Multimodal Emotion Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to predict the emotions in videos, which requires integrating heterogeneous information from the visual, auditory, and textual modalities and achieving effective feature fusion. Fusion methods based on attention mechanisms have gained widespread attention due to their outstanding performance and strong robustness. However, recent research indicates that these methods heavily rely on good feature representations in multimodal data. To address this issue, we propose the AGCL model, which uses an attention aggregation mechanism to fuse the visual and auditory modalities, enhancing semantic richness and bridging the gap in information density with the textual modality, ensuring the quality of modality information. Subsequently, hierarchical contrastive learning is implemented via attention mechanisms, which effectively decompose heterogeneous information into similar and dissimilar features, further enhancing the feature representation between the visual-auditory and textual modalities. Finally, we conducted extensive experiments on the CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and IEMOCAP datasets to evaluate various state-of-the-art multimodal sentiment analysis methods. The experimental results demonstrate that AGCL outperforms all baseline methods across various metrics on these datasets.

articleTitle: CEET: Time-Series Casual Effect Estimation via Transformer Based Representation Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurately estimating causal effects in time series holds significant value across various fields, including healthcare and finance. Existing estimation methods often perform poorly under complex original distributions and struggle to capture the intricate long-range dependencies among confounding factors. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Transformer-based representation learning model for time series causal effect estimation, named Causal Effect Estimation Transformer (CEET). The model is built on the Transformer architecture and employs an encoder-decoder framework. The encoder captures complex dependencies in historical data and generates balanced representations using Multi-Head Self-Attention. The decoder leverages these representations, combined with Self-Attention and Cross-Attention mechanisms, to predict counterfactual outcomes for causal effect estimation. Additionally, the model incorporates relative position encoding to enhance its ability to capture long-range dependencies in sequences. Furthermore, CEET utilizes a generative adversarial network to filter out confounding information, thereby reducing the influence of confounding factors and further improving the model’s performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior performance on multiple benchmark datasets, validating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Fusion Low Illumination Image Enhancement Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Existing image enhancement algorithms operate at the same scale, do not consider the effect of sensory field size on image enhancement performance, the network deep downsampling or upsampling is prone to lose the object contour texture information, and most of them are difficult to balance multiple enhancement goals, such as brightness enhancement, detail restoration and noise suppression. Aiming at these problems, this paper proposes a multiscale multi-stage image enhancement network that incorporates the attention mechanism. The network uses the hybrid attention mechanism in each stage to provide illumination a priori information, mines multi-level features through different scale network branches, and uses denoising network to suppress the noise and color difference of the enhanced image.

articleTitle: Spectrum and Power Allocation Using DRL in Cooperative Spectrum Sharing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper delves into optimizing joint spectrum and power allocation between a matched primary and secondary link pair in cooperative spectrum sharing. Weighted sum energy efficiency (WSEE) is adopted as the objective function to address the challenges of green communication. We propose a scheme based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to address this nonconvex spectrum and power allocation problem. Leveraging DRL, the spectrum and power allocation problem is autonomously optimized by only utilizing local information. Simulation results reveal that it achieves near-optimal performance and significantly enhances the network convergence speed with low computational overheads.

articleTitle: Controlling Multi-Magnetic Levitation Network System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: By integrating the linearized magnetic levitation system with network topology, we develop a novel multi-magnetic levitation network system. In this system, there is an independent magnetic levitation unit inside each node, and the interaction between these units is governed by the underlying network topology. To determine the minimum number of driver nodes required for system control, we apply the exact controllability theory. Extensive simulations of both the model and real networks reveal that as the proportion of original nodes replaced by independent magnetic levitation units increases, the required number of driver nodes for global control decreases. It is observed that denser and more homogeneous network systems are more easily controlled. Furthermore, we find that in dense network systems, the edge weight influences controllability; however, this effect diminishes as a greater number of original nodes are replaced by independent magnetic levitation units.

articleTitle: Formal Security Analysis and Innovative Application of Blockchain-based 5G AKA Protocol in Service Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a blockchain architecture to address the challenges posed by the inadequate integration of technology and the absence of security analysis in the context of 5G communication and blockchain technology. The architecture integrates a blockchain-based 5G AKA protocol, a novel design that utilizes the tamper-proof characteristics of blockchain to enhance the security performance of the conventional protocol. The Tamarin-prover tool is applied to model and analyze the blockchain-based 5G AKA protocol, and the results indicate that the new protocol satisfies 7 of the 10 unsatisfied security authentication properties of the traditional 5G AKA protocol, improving security by $60 \%$. This provides an effective strategy for enhancing 5 G communication security.

articleTitle: Research on Medical Image Segmentation Method Based on Semi Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a key task in medical image analysis, which is widely used in tumor detection, organ segmentation and other fields. However, the annotation of medical image data is costly and time-consuming, which limits the application of traditional supervised learning methods. In this paper, we first introduce the concepts of image segmentation and semi-supervised learning. Secondly, the FPS-Net based on semi-supervised learning is designed. The network combines the feature pyramid module (FPM) and the cross-attention module (CSA) to improve the segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Finally, through experiments on liver CT image dataset and skin lesion dataset, the effectiveness of the proposed method in the semi-supervised learning environment is verified, and the performance of the segmentation model is further improved.

articleTitle: DNS Fuzz Testing Technique Based on Multi-Indicator Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the Internet scale, the domain name system, as the key infrastructure of the Internet, is of great significance in terms of its operational stability and security. Existing fuzz testing techniques have a single evaluation index for test cases, and there is a bottleneck in the efficiency of test case generation, which is difficult to meet the needs of the increasingly complex DNS security testing. In view of this, we designed a fuzz testing method based on the fusion of multiple indicators for domain name system software testing. On the basis of AFLGO, we first introduce update region, vulnerability update region, new region, three new test case evaluation criteria, and then combined with the multi-indicator fusion algorithm to construct an energy allocation model, which accurately allocates the energy to different test cases, so that the test cases are more targeted to cover the key basic blocks of the domain name system. Experiments show that our designed method outperforms traditional methods in generating use cases efficiently and provides a more efficient fuzz testing technique for software testing of domain name system.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Deep Feature Fusion GAN for SAR and Visible Images via Cross-Modal Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This research proposes a Hierarchical Deep Feature Fusion GAN based on cross-modal enhancement for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and visible image fusion. Through deep learning techniques, the network addresses the challenging fusion task between visible and SAR images caused by their distinct imaging mechanisms, achieving high-quality fusion with rich detail preservation. Initially, the network leverages the bidirectional generative capabilities of CycleGAN for modal enhancement to mitigate issues related to training data scarcity and quality. In the feature extraction phase, the ResNet-50 serves as the backbone network to extract hierarchically refined deep features from both SAR and visible images. During the feature fusion phase, lightweight attention mechanism modules are employed to fuse deep features at corresponding hierarchical levels. Finally, we designed a hierarchical nested connection architecture to reconstruct the fused image from multi-level fused deep features. Experimental results demonstrate that our method exhibits superior image fusion performance in both visual perception and objective metrics. Keywords- synthetic aperture radar (SAR); visible images; crossmodal enhancement; hierarchically refined deep feature

articleTitle: MMFN: Multi-Scale Mask Fusion Network For Remote Sensing Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of CNN and Transformer network architectures has played a pivotal role in the field of change detection in remote sensing. The most recent research has showcased remarkable advancements. However, we have encountered several challenges concurrently. Traditional methodologies predominantly rely on conventional semantic segmentation approaches, overlooking the inherent geometric features unique to the task of change detection, particularly those related to buildings. Secondly, the extensive use of convolutional operations can mask the inherent spatiotemporal characteristics of the data. Addressing the aforementioned issues, this paper introduces a multi-scale fusion method named MMFNet, designed to extract features at different levels.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Task Assignment Based on Improved VPPSO
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Task assignment is a critical factor for multi-UAVs to efficiently accomplish missions. In this paper, two task assignment models are established under different optimization objectives. Based on the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, a particle encoding scheme that satisfies model constraints is designed. To address the issue of PSO easily falling into local optima, improvements are made by revising the particle velocity update strategy, introducing chaotic initialization for particle positions, and incorporating hill-climbing mutation operations to enhance the algorithm’s search capability. An improved velocity pausing particle swarm optimization algorithm (VPPSO) is proposed to solve multi-UAV task assignment problems. Simulation validations using two case studies demonstrate that the algorithm achieves accurate and stable solutions, with faster convergence and stronger optimization capabilities compared to the basic PSO algorithm, indicating better practicality.

articleTitle: Based on TDNN-BiLSTM and Multi-head Attention for Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Effective fusion of local spectral features and global contextual information remains a challenging task in automatic speech recognition (ASR). This paper proposes a hybrid neural network architecture based on time-delay neural networks (TDNN), bidirectional long short-term memory networks (BiLSTM), and multi-head attention mechanisms to improve phoneme sequence prediction accuracy. The model first extracts local acoustic features using TDNN, captures bidirectional temporal dependencies via BiLSTM, and dynamically integrates contextual information through multi-head attention. Experimental results show that the phoneme recognition accuracy of the model is 82.2% and 92.5%, and the word error rate (WER) is 30.9% and 14.1% on the TIMIT and Switchboard test sets, which are 19.3% and 16.5% higher than the traditional TDNN model, and the WER reduction is increased by 23.4% and 33.8%. At the same time, compared with multiple models such as CTC-Transformer, the key role of multi-head attention in modeling long-term dependencies is verified, and the generalization ability of the model for ASR tasks is highlighted.

articleTitle: Design of a Power Flow Convergence Discriminator Based on Physical Information Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As the structure of power systems becomes increasingly complex, the number of possible operating modes in power systems increases, leading to a sharp rise in the difficulty and computational load of traditional power flow calculations. Meanwhile, the application of artificial intelligence technology in new power systems still lacks rationality, making it challenging to apply in real grid operations. This paper proposes a power flow convergence discriminator based on a physical information model, utilizing a multi-Layer Perceptron network to implement a voltage predictor that satisfies the equality constraints of power flow calculations. Through power flow networks and residual calculations, it meets the inequality constraints to ensure the feasibility of actual operations. Simulations were conducted on the IEEE 30-bus system, and the results indicate that the power flow discriminator can accurately distinguish five types of power flow samples, achieving a testing accuracy of $96 \%$.

articleTitle: A Flow Field Prediction Method Based on the Transformer for Enhancing Local Sensitivity of Irregular Geometries
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: engineering significance in aerospace, meteorology, and renewable energy systems. While traditional CFD methods face computational inefficiency due to mesh generation and Navier-Stokes equation solving, current deep learning approaches encounter dual challenges with unstructured meshes: voxelization struggles with complex geometries, and PointNet-based methods exhibit limited local feature extraction. To address these, we propose PointTransformerCFD, integrating attention mechanisms to establish learnable local feature aggregation, enhancing physical feature capture in critical regions (e.g., boundary layer separation). Experiments confirm its high accuracy in airfoil flow field prediction.

articleTitle: A Research on Virtualization Technology for Computing Center
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Current naval shipboard information systems use distributed system architecture. This architecture takes large space, while its resource utilization is poor. These cannot satisfy the requirements of next generation naval shipboard information systems. Computing center architecture with virtualization technology can reorganize the physic resource of the computers into virtual resource pool, which can significantly improve the resource utilization and meet the needs of the new shipboard information systems. In this paper, we carried out an in-depth research of virtualization technologies. We proposed a virtualization system evaluation method, and took a comprehensive evaluation of the three virtualization systems. In result, we gave several suggestions for virtualization system deployment. These can solve the problems of poor resource utilization and fault tolerance performance in current naval shipboard information systems. This project can provide a solid foundation for the application of the computing oriented virtualization technologies to the new naval shipboard information systems.

articleTitle: Research on Urban Waterlogging Risk Analysis Method Based on InfoWorks ICM and Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study employs InfoWorks ICM data and the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to assess urban waterlogging risk. The risk factors considered in the evaluation encompass three aspects: natural factors, engineering factors, and management factors. These are further broken down into nine specific indicators: rainfall intensity, terrain slope, historical water accumulation, completeness of pipeline systems, compliance of pipeline design return periods, stormwater pumping capacity, flood embankment management, integrated management of waterlogging and pollution, and emergency response management. When using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) for risk assessment of these indicators, experts can prioritize InfoWorks ICM simulation data to make precise judgments on engineering factors. Additionally, historical data, field surveys, and questionnaire surveys are integrated to ensure the scientific rigor and accuracy of the evaluation results. Practical case studies demonstrate that this method is feasible and yields effective outcomes.

articleTitle: Fliter Bank Convolution Neural Network Based on Transformer for SSVEP Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Deep learning is increasingly being applied in Steady-State Visual Evoked Potential (SSVEP) Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) systems, particularly models based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This paper introduces a novel method named Conv-Trans2, which integrates the temporal characteristics of SSVEP data and channel features by utilizing the multi-head attention mechanism from the Transformer architecture to process time-domain data directly. Furthermore, to enhance harmonic learning, an extension based on a filter bank (FB-Conv-Trans2) is proposed, further improving classification accuracy. Experiments were conducted on two publicly available datasets (Dataset 1: 35 subjects, 40 targets; Dataset 2: 70 subjects, 40 targets). The results demonstrate that FB-Conv-Trans2 outperforms other baseline methods across different time windows, achieving significant improvements in both classification accuracy and information transfer rate. The study also investigates the impact of varying data lengths on inter-individual differences.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Standing Long Jump Distance Measurement Based on Improved YOLOv11 and Lightweight Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a vision-based algorithm for automated standing long jump (SLJ) measurement, addressing the inefficiency and inaccuracy of traditional manual methods. By integrating an enhanced YOLOv11 detector with lightweight pose estimation, the system achieves real-time performance on edge devices. Key innovations include: A FocalModulation-enhanced YOLOv11 model for precise athlete detection, improving accuracy by $1.68 \%$; A biomechanical phase recognition mechanism combining spatial-temporal analysis of heel trajectories with adaptive thresholds to identify takeoff, airborne, and landing phases; A dual-state logic control system to filter measurement noise and ensure reliable jump counting. Experimental results on 220 real-world videos demonstrate $99.44 \%$ accuracy in standard jumps, comparable to infrared systems, while outperforming conventional algorithms in complex scenarios. The system requires only smartphone cameras, eliminating dependency on specialized sensors. This work provides a cost-effective, portable solution for intelligent physical education assessment, advancing the standardization of sports training and public health monitoring.

articleTitle: Steel Defect Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Steel, a crucial material in construction and machinery, demands high surface quality. This paper presents an enhanced YOLOv8 for steel surface defect detection. To detect small defects better, the original C2f module is replaced with the new DBBNCSPELAN4 module, improving small - defect detection accuracy. For better feature fusion, the traditional Concat module in the Neck network is swapped with the ContextGuideFusionModule, enhancing fusion and reducing computational complexity. To address overlapping defect issues, the WaveletPool module is added to certain convolutional layers in the Backbone and Neck, strengthening the model’s robustness and multi - scale feature extraction. Experiments show that, though with increased inference time and complexity, the model improves Precision by $5.3 \%$, Recall by $2.0 \%$, and mAP50 by $3.0 \%$, significantly enhancing steel defect detection accuracy, especially for tiny defects.

articleTitle: Design of Network Security Situation Assessment Method and Application of Data Mining in the Tobacco Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The existing network security situational awareness technologies and evaluation schemes in tobacco enterprises lack accuracy in calculating and evaluating the network security operational situation index, which prevents relevant departments from comprehensively understanding the network security situation in the tobacco industry. To address this issue, this paper proposes a data mining-based network security situational awareness and evaluation method for the tobacco industry. Specifically, it uses the stability degree of data mining to identify and extract network security situational awareness features in the tobacco industry; calculates the network operational situation index and generates an operational situation matrix; mines common data within the matrix to generate the final result. The experiment shows that this method has certain advantages and can accurately perceive the network security situation in the tobacco industry.

articleTitle: The migrativity of grouping functions over fuzzy implications from generator functions
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The migrativity of aggregation functions holds significant importance in fuzzy logic systems, and it has been found that migrativity is a worthwhile research issue both in application and theory. In the past few decades, the migrativity of some aggregation functions has been documented. However, the relationship between the generator fuzzy implications and grouping functions is still an open question. This paper aims to explore the migrativity of grouping functions with respect to fuzzy implications derived from generator functions. To be specific, we examine the migrativity of grouping functions over several particular generator fuzzy implications. From this novel perspective, we will present a multitude of new findings.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Switched-Capacitor RF Receiver for Low-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel RF receiver architecture that combines specific harmonic rejection, switched-capacitor filtering, and current-reuse techniques to achieve high performance with low power consumption. The proposed receiver utilizes a reconfigurable switched-capacitor filter to selectively reject undesired harmonics generated by the local oscillator, thereby improving signal integrity and reducing interference. The filter’s programmability allows for dynamic adaptation to varying RF environments, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. Current-reuse techniques are employed to enhance the receiver’s noise figure without significantly increasing power consumption. The proposed architecture is implemented in a standard CMOS process, and simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving high linearity, low noise, and good harmonic rejection while maintaining low power consumption. The combination of reconfigurability, low power, and robustness makes this receiver an attractive solution for next-generation wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Hybrid wired-wireless service access system based on optical frequency comb.
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This research focuses on a hybrid wired-wireless service transmission system. Using the multi-wavelength feature of the optical frequency comb light source, wired and wireless data are co-transmitted in one optical fiber. At the base station, the central carrier can be extracted from the multi-carrier optical signal for the uplink transmission link’s light source, simplifying the base station’s structure.
