Moreover, an optimization scheme to enhance the system’s transmission efficiency is proposed from the modulation methods perspective.

articleTitle: Design of FPGA Timing Processing Module in Radar System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In view of the strict requirements of radar systems on timing control and processing accuracy during high-speed data processing, FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) as an efficient hardware platform has become one of the key technologies in the design of timing processing modules. In order to meet the real-time and high-precision requirements of the radar system, this study cites a timing processing module design based on FPGA. First, through an in-depth analysis of the radar signal processing process, the requirements and performance indicators of each timing control are clarified, and a module architecture suitable for FPGA is designed. Then, VHDL language is used to describe the hardware of the module, and the parallel processing characteristics of FPGA are used to realize real-time processing of high-speed timing data. Finally, to ensure timing accuracy, precise clock synchronization and signal delay compensation technology are used, and a custom timing control algorithm is used to optimize the data transmission and storage process. Experimental results show that the designed FPGA timing processing module performs excellently in timing accuracy, data throughput and multi-target signal detection capability. The timing error is controlled within ±0.8 nanoseconds, the processing speed reaches 50,000 to 66,667 pulses per second, and the maximum throughput is $0.1 \mathrm{~GB} / \mathrm{s}$. At the same time, the module can still stably detect target signals in complex noise environments and high load conditions, fully meeting the radar system’s requirements for high precision, high efficiency and high stability.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis of Olympic medal table based on multiple features
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Predicting Olympic medal counts holds significant value for strategic planning by National Olympic Committees. This paper presents a comprehensive modeling approach for predicting medal distribution across countries at future Olympic Games. We developed a stacked integration learning framework incorporating multiple machine learning algorithms: LR, LASSO, SVM, and Catboost in the first layer as base learners, and RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM in the second layer as meta-learners. This approach effectively quantifies medal fluctuations based on multiple country characteristics and their correlation patterns. The model was used to predict medal standings for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and identify countries likely to improve or decline in performance. Additionally, we constructed specialized evaluation models for countries without previous medals by parameterizing scarce data and adjusting association ratios. To analyze the relationship between sports types and national medal counts, we employed a neural network algorithm that determined sport-specific impact parameters for each country. Furthermore, we examined the “great coach” effect on medal stability using the DBSCAN clustering algorithm and UMAP hierarchical analysis, identifying optimal coach-sport pairings for six selected countries. Our modeling approach provides valuable insights for National Olympic Committees to optimize resource allocation and strategic planning for future Olympic competitions.

articleTitle: User-Centric Bandwidth Allocation in Network Slicing via Dueling DRL
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Network slicing plays a pivotal role in 5 G and next-generation communication systems to support diversified service requirements. This paper investigates bandwidth allocation in a multi-base station, multi-user network where users probabilistically request network slicing services. We formulate a dynamic resource optimization problem to maximize user satisfaction, accounting for stochastic service demands and heterogeneous quality-of-service requirements. An Adaptive Hierarchical Dueling Deep Q-Network (AH-Dueling DQN) algorithm is proposed to address the NP-hard mixed-integer programming nature of this problem, leveraging deep reinforcement learning to handle high-dimensional state-action spaces. Simulation results demonstrate the algorithm’s effectiveness in reducing users’ latency while improving the throughput.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Redis-Based Data Hot-Table Caching Mode
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of social informatization and intelligence, the volume of data in information systems has grown exponentially. Traditional relational databases have become the mainstream storage medium due to their unified operational standards and stable, reliable characteristics. However, high-concurrency read and write scenarios pose significant challenges to relational databases. Relational databases store data on disks, and each data read or write operation requires interaction with the disk. Frequent I/O operations severely affect the availability and stability of the system. To address the I/O performance bottleneck of relational databases in high-concurrency scenarios, a Redis-based data hot-table caching mode is proposed(RHTCM). This pattern designs an integrated exponential smoothing prediction algorithm to achieve real-time heat prediction for accessed tables in the system. It utilizes a modulo-based approach to enable efficient data pagination extraction and processing. Additionally, a table-object mapping storage migration mode is adopted to achieve efficient data migration. Experimental results show that by leveraging Redis’s exceptionally high read and write performance, the frequency of disk interactions is significantly reduced, greatly enhancing the real-time response capability of the database system.

articleTitle: A YOLOv5-based Model Enhanced by Dynamic Convolution for Accurate Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The object detection algorithm based on YOLO has been widely used in many fields, but there are still some shortcomings. As for the classic YOLOv5, it is easy to miss or misdetect when dealing with small objects, resulting in inaccurate detection results. In order to improve the accuracy of object detection, this paper proposes an improved object detection model YOLOv5-DDN. This model replaces the original convolution module in YOLOv5 with dynamic convolution, which enhances the adaptability and representation ability of the model to different input features. In addition, YOLOv5-DDN adopts the DIoU-based non-maximum suppression (DIoU-NMS) technology, which not only considers the overlapping area of the bounding box, but also introduces the distance between the center points of the bounding box as an additional penalty term, so as to more accurately evaluate the similarity between the bounding boxes and avoid the problems of false suppression and repeated detection. We verify the YOLOv5-DDN model on the public dataset GC10-DET. Experimental results show that YOLOv5-DDN outperforms the current state-of-the-art models in terms of detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Radar Parameter Estimation Algorithm for Small UAV Targets
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a typical radar point target, small UAVs have poor target estimation accuracy when traditional weighted methods are used. It is impossible to accurately estimate the target’s range and velocity, and under high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, the estimation results are not asymptotically consistent with the parameters to be measured. To improve the detection accuracy of radar for small UAVs, this paper deeply analyzes the radar signal processing process of small UAV targets, proposes a parameter estimation algorithm based on the joint calculation of the highest point and its adjacent points, and correspondingly presents an iterative solution method for transcendental functions encountered in the solution process. Simulation results show that this algorithm can obtain rangeDoppler estimation results close to the theoretical accuracy, and the computational complexity of the algorithm is controllable.

articleTitle: Design of Automatic Control Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Traditional robotic arms are manipulated in realtime through remote control technology. However, they not only have a mechanical feel that differs from the human body structure, which fails to meet the more meticulous operational requirements of technicians in complex environments, but also suffer from the issue of a single control mode. In order to address the problem of the limited control mode in traditional manipulators and better meet the diverse needs of complex operations, this project has investigated the structure of the human hand and natural - motion - based simulation control technologies. By combining the advantages of various technologies, a manipulator with multiple control methods has been designed. The design uses the STM32F103C8T6 single-chip microcomputer as the main control board, and it can be controlled in multiple ways, such as through a somatosensory glove, a mobile phone, or a gamepad. The structure of the manipulator is driven by servos. In the somatosensory glove, the HC-12 chip is used as the data transmission module. Coupled with the high-precision potentiometers installed on each finger cot, analog signals can be stably and quickly converted into digital signals for transmission. The Bluetooth module or PS2 receiver on the robotic palm can receive control information from mobile phones or gamepads. Moreover, the W25Q64 chip on the manipulator can store preset action groups, enabling the manipulator to perform preset actions.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Floating-Point Operations: Optimizing Division in 2PC Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized floating-point division protocol to address the issues of high communication overhead and computational complexity in existing protocols, while ensuring accuracy and security. The proposed method improves the mantissa computation process, significantly reducing data transmission volume and interaction rounds. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed protocol outperforms existing mainstream methods in terms of runtime, communication overhead, and efficiency, thus optimizes complex nonlinear functions such as Sigmoid, Tanh, and Softmax. This research provides new insights into optimizing floating-point operations and establishes a solid foundation for the application of privacy-preserving computation in high-precision scenarios.

articleTitle: Architecture Design Based on Big Data Storage Technology for Launch Vehicle Test Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, the test data of launch vehicle shows the characteristics such as large data volumes, numerous files, complex data types and rapid growth rates. Traditional relational databases are inadequate to meet the requirements for the storage and application of massive data produced by launch vehicle test due to the relatively low query efficiency for large volume data, lack of data backup and poor scalability. A storage and application architecture based on big data technology including HDFS, HBase, SeaweedFS, Elasticsearch and Hive is designed for massive launch vehicle test data. Practical engineering application has demonstrated that this architecture shows good reliability and scalability, and can meet the storage and query demands of launch vehicle test data effectively.

articleTitle: Field automatic warning network based on LoRa
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at problems such as insufficient communication coverage, high power consumption and complex deployment, a low- power wide-area monitoring network architecture based on LoRa technology is proposed in this paper. The network adopts the dual-star hybrid topology, combines the dynamic spread factor allocation and time division multiplexing mechanism, and realizes the balance between low power consumption and long distance communication by optimizing the configuration of LoRa parameters (bandwidth, spread factor, coding rate).Regarding hardware design, the STM32 series microcontroller and SX1268 RF module are used to build terminal nodes, which support multi-sensor access and power partition management. At the software level, an adaptive anti-collision algorithm is proposed, which combines signal enhancement and collision decoding technology to improve network reliability.

Author Keywords: low power wide area monitoring network

articleTitle: A Framework for Adaptive Learning and Context-Aware Knowledge Enhancement: An Art Education System Based on DeepSeek
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Digital platforms have overtaken galleries in art dissemination, yet static formats limit personalization and engagement across diverse audiences. This paper presents an DeepSeek-based conversational system integrating dynamic user profiling and knowledge-enhanced dialogue generation. It features a profile extraction module for real-time interest tracking via multimodal fusion and an LLM-driven (DeepSeek-driven) module balancing personalization and fidelity through dual-constraint optimization. Employing neural differential equations, hierarchical attention, and three-phase joint training, the system fosters bidirectional cognitive interaction, surpassing traditional recommendation logic. Experiments on the Art_GenEvalGPT dataset (13,870 dialogues) show superior performance (BLEU-4: 0.38 vs. 0.31, session turns: 9.4 vs. 5.8, p $\lt 0.01$). A $1,260-$ participant study confirms enhanced engagement ($83 \%$ report deeper thinking) and adaptability (profile matching: 0.82). This framework transforms art dissemination into active meaningmaking, supporting digital cultural preservation, though “information cocoons” and young user challenges suggest future refinements.

articleTitle: SREQ: A Structured Approach to Safety Requirements Modeling for ADS under ISO 26262
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Automated Driving Systems (ADS) are safety-critical systems with components such as perception, planning and execution. As these systems become increasingly sophisticated, ensuring their safety in the design phase remains a crucial challenge. However, requirement modeling for ADS, particularly with a focus on safety, remains complex. This calls for a more refined requirement modeling methodology specifically designed for ADS. Thus, we propose SREQ, a structured approach to modeling safety requirements in ADS. Our approach integrates safety-related concepts from ISO 26262 with the requirement diagram from SysML. The feasibility of our approach has been validated through an overtaking scenario.

articleTitle: Lightweight Network based on Depth-separable Convolution for 5G Indoor Positioning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The importance of 5G positioning lies in its ability to provide high-precision location accuracy, impacting network optimization, emergency response and safety, augmented reality and virtual reality, and commercial applications. 5G positioning offers accurate location information, fostering innovation and improving user experience and quality of life. The importance of 5G CSI fingerprint positioning for machine learning-based methods has led to rapid development in recent years. However, existing models from computer vision and natural language processing lack adaptation to the physical meaning of 5G CSI, resulting in suboptimal performance. In this paper, we propose a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) based 5G positioning method that considers spatial and frequency domain modeling. The method utilizes interpretable CNN weights to explore dependencies on frequency domain information across different base stations. Performance validation is conducted on three real-world 5G positioning datasets with varying signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: BiLSTM Model Based on Bayesian Optimization for Network Security Situation Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of network scale and the gradual deepening of complexity, network attack techniques are also in the process of dynamic evolution. As a core hot spot in the field of network security, network security situation prediction is receiving more and more widespread attention. Traditional network security situation prediction methods have many limitations, such as single approach, poor prediction accuracy, insufficient generalization ability, and high time cost. In this paper, we take the bidirectional long and short-term memory network (BiLSTM) as the main research object, optimize the BiLSTM with the help of Bayesian optimization algorithm (BO) and attention mechanism. Then propose and construct a new forecasting model BO - BiLSTM - ATT (BBLA), and carry out the relevant experimental research. Through simulation experiments on the UNSW-NB15 network traffic dataset, the predicted situation values of the optimized BiLSTM are highly consistent with the actual posture values, which fully verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: GSNet: Multimodal Deep Learning for Predicting Molecular Metabolic Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular metabolic stability is considered to be of significant practical value in the field of drug development, particularly in ensuring the safety and efficacy of drugs. The metabolic stability of drugs has been effectively predicted by existing deep learning methods through the analysis of the structural features of drug molecules. However, the propagation of molecular graph information is primarily focused on by most of the current methods, with limited consideration given to molecular sequence data. The Graph-Seq Network (GSNet) model, which is proposed in this paper, is aimed at predicting the metabolic stability of compounds. A deep learning framework has been designed to integrate the SMILES representation of compounds and molecular graph data for the extraction of molecular features. Specifically, for molecular sequence information, a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) is utilized to capture the context of symbols and to learn the sequence representation of molecules. For molecular graph data, a graph encoder is introduced, through which the graph structure representation is learned by capturing the consistency between global and local structural information. Finally, the sequence and structural information are combined by the model through fully connected layers for model training. It is demonstrated by experimental results that, in comparison to alternative methods, the GSNet model performs more effectively across a range of public datasets. The importance of both the sequence encoder and the graph encoder in the model is also confirmed by ablation studies.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Natural Language Processing in Automatic English Composition Scoring
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence technology, the application of natural language processing in the field of education continues to deepen. A natural language processing based automatic scoring system for English compositions has been designed to address issues such as strong subjectivity, inconsistent scoring criteria, and time-consuming and laborious processes. The system achieves multi-dimensional automatic evaluation of composition content, language expression, and discourse structure through core technologies such as text preprocessing, feature extraction, semantic analysis, and machine learning. The experimental results show that the system has achieved the expected goals in terms of scoring accuracy, consistency, and efficiency. The scoring results are highly consistent with manual scoring, providing an effective intelligent auxiliary tool for English teaching.

articleTitle: Optimizing Image Classification Models for Cloud Infrastructure with Elastic Scaling
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Advances in image classification have led to significant improvements in various applications, yet challenges remain in optimizing these models for cloud infrastructures. Fluctuating workloads and the need for efficient resource allocation complicate the deployment of high-performing models. We propose a novel framework that enhances image classification performance specifically within cloud environments through Elastic Scaling. This approach leverages a modular architecture, facilitating real-time adjustments to computing resources based on demand and complexity of the models being utilized. Our methodology incorporates diverse data preprocessing techniques and evaluates multiple model architectures to strike a balance between accuracy and operational efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted across various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our solution, showcasing considerable enhancements in classification performance and substantial reductions in operational costs tied to cloud infrastructure. The findings highlight improvements in response times and resource utilization, creating an adaptive framework that effectively addresses differing image processing requirements. This work offers a comprehensive solution aimed at optimizing cloud-based image classification tasks while maximizing performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: PPDM:Pansharpening based on conditionally guided diffusion modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Pansharpening technique is an important technique in the field of remote sensing imagery, aiming at fusing a pair of low-resolution multispectral maps(LRMS) and high-resolution panchromatic maps(PAN) to obtain high-resolution multispectral images.(HRMS) The most dominant current method is based on deep learning, which is mainly based on learning the mapping of the input image to the fusion result. We propose a novel Pansharpening method based on a conditionally guided diffusion model, which processes LRMS and PAN images from a new perspective, learns the difference between the input image data and the output image, and implements the previous complex image fusion process using a multi-step Markov process. To ensure the fidelity of image information required in the field of Pansharpening, we designed a multi-scale concurrent convolutional reconstruction module to encode the feature information contained in LRMS and PAN into the diffusion model inverse process, which is implemented by a denoising U-Net network. Experiments are conducted on the mainstream datasets GauFen-2, QuickBird, and WorldView-3, and results are obtained in both qualitative and quantitative analyses that achieve results that are not inferior to those of the current mainstream Pansharpening methods.

articleTitle: A Deep Text Mining-Based Cosmetics Consumer Sentiment Analysis Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, consumer reviews have become crucial channels for businesses to obtain market insights and user feedback. In this study, we propose a sentiment analysis method based on deep text mining, targeting cosmetic product reviews from the JD.com platform. Firstly, comments are preprocessed using Jieba segmentation and TF-IDF feature extraction combined with N -gram models, along with class-weight adjustment to address class imbalance. Experiments involve traditional machine learning methods, with Logistic Regression achieving an initial class- 0 F1-score of 0.8135. We further compare the influence of different stopword strategies, including generic stopwords, Chinese sentiment-specific stopwords, and a customized stopword list constructed based on word frequency and N-gram analysis. Results show the updated stopword list performs similarly to not using any stopwords in Random Forest. Additionally, deep learning models (LSTM and CNN) achieve initial class-0 F1-scores of 0.8331 and 0.8271, respectively, improving to 0.8598 and 0.8521 after Bayesian optimization, while Logistic Regression slightly improves to $\mathbf{0. 8 1 3 9}$. Overall, results indicate that TF-IDF text representation combined with deep learning and Bayesian optimization significantly improves negative sentiment prediction, offering valuable insights for future large-scale, cross-domain sentiment analysis research.

articleTitle: Physics-Constrained ST-GNNs for High-Performance PM2.5 Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: PM2.5 pollution is a serious global health problem. This paper introduces PIST-GNN, a new model for predicting PM2.5 levels in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region that performs very well. Unlike typical machine learning methods, PIST-GNN considers real-world physics. It directly incorporates equations that describe how air particles move into its design as a spatio-temporal graph neural network. The model uses Graph Convolutional Networks to understand relationships between locations and to estimate how PM2.5 moves based on these physics equations. This allows for more accurate predictions over multiple time steps, guided by physical principles. Our experiments demonstrate that PIST-GNN is significantly better. It reduces the prediction error (RMSE) by 47.5% for one-step predictions and by $23.23 \pm 0.32$ for 8-step predictions. These results highlight PIST-GNN’s strong capability for highly accurate PM2.5 forecasting.

articleTitle: Research on Abnormal Behavior Detection Method Based on User Access Sequence Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of enterprise informatization, traditional perimeter security protection technologies have gradually exposed their limitations in dealing with unknown threats. In response to this issue, this article proposes an anomaly behavior detection method based on user access sequence analysis. This method constructs a multi-level and multi-dimensional adaptive baseline model through deep data modeling and machine learning algorithms. By introducing sequence correlation analysis and spatiotemporal distribution feature analysis, comprehensive modeling was conducted from three dimensions: individual-level behavior patterns, position-level behavior patterns, and group-level behavior patterns, significantly improving the perception ability of covert network threats. The experimental results indicate that the multidimensional sequence baseline weighted scoring mechanism proposed in this study can effectively identify potential abnormal access behaviors. This provides a new technological support method for enterprise network security protection system.

articleTitle: Research on Calibration Method and Uncertainty Evaluation of Pacemaker Analyzers
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: External pacemakers, also known as temporary pacemakers, have been widely used in clinical settings, significantly reducing patient mortality rates. Pacemaker analyzers are utilized to measure the parameters of pacemakers, ensuring their accuracy, as these parameters are critical to patient safety. Regular calibration is essential since pacemaker analyzers have been widely used. However, measurement institutions and published measurement standards rarely focus on the calibration of pacemaker analyzers. This paper designs a calibration method that uses a digital multimeter and a waveform generator to calibrate parameters such as internal resistance, current amplitude, pulse width, rate, and energy of the pacemaker analyzer. A program by C# in Visual Studio is developed to control the calibration instruments, therefore improving measurement efficiency. At the end of the paper, uncertainty evaluation of the calibration results is conducted.

articleTitle: Formalizing the Semantics of a Classical-Quantum Imperative Language in Maude
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Recent advancements in quantum computing have exhibited substantial promise across domains such as formal verification and quantum communication. However, formal verification of hybrid quantum-classical programs remains challenging due to the complex interactions between classical control logic and quantum operations. In this paper, we propose an executable operational semantics for the Classical-Quantum Imperative Language (QIMP), implemented using the Maude system. Our framework employs rewrite rules to precisely capture classical-quantum interactions, particularly the probabilistic branching induced by quantum measurements. Experimental validation using representative algorithms, such as Quantum Teleportation and the BB84 protocol, demonstrates the capability of our semantics to accurately simulate quantum behaviors including state evolution, collapse, and classical state updates, highlighting its applicability and scalability in formal verification tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Composite shoreline detection based on U-Net
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Sea-land segmentation, as one of the core tasks in intelligent interpretation of remote sensing imagery, directly impacts the effectiveness of marine applications such as coastline change monitoring and intertidal zone resource surveys. To address issues like blurred boundaries and misclassification of small features in existing deep learning methods when processing complex shoreline scenarios, this paper proposes an improved U-Net model incorporating a boundary-aware attention mechanism. The model adopts ResNet50 as its backbone network and introduces a Boundary-Aware Attention Mechanism in the encoder to enhance feature representation in key regions and improve the model’s focus on weak boundaries. During the decoding phase, skip connections are employed to compensate for information loss, while deconvolution layers and Softmax are used for refined segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional U-Net, SegNet, and DeepLabV3, the proposed model achieves superior performance across metrics including mIoU, mPA, and F1-Score. Particularly in complex mixed shoreline environments, it effectively prevents boundary blurring and misclassification, thereby improving both the accuracy and robustness of land-sea segmentation.

Index Terms: Islands In The South China Sea

articleTitle: A 3D Simulation Platform for Gas Source Localization with Quadrotor
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The turbulent airflow introduces chaotic and random characteristics to gas plume dispersion processes, rendering gas source localization experiments hardly reproducible in outdoor environments. To address this challenge, this paper develops a 3D gas source localization simulation platform integrated with Hector rotorcrafts. Built upon a simulator named GADEN and adopting the ROS modular development framework, this platform enables validation of gas source localization algorithms for single/multiple UAVs or mobile robots. Furthermore, to enhance 3D data visualization capabilities, the simulator incorporates a customized octree mapping component derived from OctoMap for displaying user-defined 3D occupancy grid maps. This work also establishes an organizational framework for gas source localization strategies. Simulation validation through UAV gas source search and gas concentration mapping processe demonstrates the practical applicability of the developed simulation platform.

articleTitle: Image Generation Network Combining High-efficiency Residual and Self-conditioning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the field of image generation, deep - learning methods based on diffusion models have achieved remarkable progress. However, when dealing with images of Thangka ritual implements, which have fine textures and unique shapes, existing models suffer from slow inference speed, as well as deficiencies in texture clarity and pattern integrity.To address these issues, based on the DDIM, we propose an image - generation network that combines the high - efficiency residual and self - conditioning. This network utilizes the ConvNext v2 Block to enhance the ability to extract and utilize image features. Meanwhile, the self conditioning is introduced to enable the model to better utilize its own existing information during the generation process.Experimental results show that, on the Thangka ritual implement dataset, compared with the original DDIM, the method proposed in this paper reduces the FID by 1.169, increases the IS by 0.23, and improves the subjective evaluation score by 6.2%.

articleTitle: Research on Cultural Gene Inheritance and Design of Qinghai Tu Circle Embroidery Based Based on Hierarchical Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Combine them with modern design activities, explore the cultural gene inheritance and innovation of Qinghai Tu circle embroidery, and promote the organic combination of this traditional non-heritage art and modern aesthetics, so as to give it a new vitality. To extract the cultural factors of the Qinghai Tu circle embroidery, we collect data from the composition, pattern, color and semantics of the Qinghai Tu circle embroidery to establish the cultural gene mapping; secondly, we use the hierarchical analysis method to calculate the weights of the cultural factors and sort them; finally, we use the shape grammar to reorganize the design of the factors with larger weights to verify the possibility of this method. After the above research, is one of the paths for the integration of the modern design forms of the Qinghai Tu circle embroidery, the creative transformation into the modern design and application of the products.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Low-altitude Flight Dynamic Monitoring and Management Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper constructs a low-altitude flight dynamic monitoring and management platform to address the problem of monitoring blind spots and data loss in continuous tracking of lowaltitude cooperative targets using a single ADS-B or BeiDou surveillance source. The platform parses the raw surveillance data from ADS-B and BeiDou short messages, interpolate and predict missing data from both ADS-B and BeiDou surveillance sources based on the least squares method, then persistent stores and forwards the fused data, and designs a flight dynamic monitoring and management platform based on this, ultimately achieving continuous tracking of low-altitude cooperative targets.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Breast Ultrasound Images Based on CBAM-Extended Residual U-Net
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Breast cancer has a high malignancy rate and poses a serious threat to women’s health. In China, ultrasound imaging is the primary method for breast cancer screening, and precise lesion segmentation is crucial for diagnosing benign and malignant cases. The traditional U-Net model concatenates feature maps from the encoder and decoder, which introduces redundant information, and its skip connections struggle to transmit longrange contextual information. This study proposes a U-Net model based on attention mechanisms and extended residual convolution to address these issues. The extended residual convolution replaces traditional convolution modules to expand the receptive field and capture multi-scale features. An improved CBAM attention module is added to the skip connections to enhance the combination of shallow and deep features. Additionally, the DiceIoULoss function is used to balance the Dice and IoU coefficients. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the original U-Net model, with improvements of 8.6%, $23.7 \%, 5.6 \%$, and $5.1 \%$ in IoU, Dice, Recall, and F1-score, respectively. These results demonstrate the model’s effectiveness in breast nodule lesion segmentation.

articleTitle: Verification of AMBA-based Flash Controllers
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Based on the actual IoT chip project, this paper designs a feature-rich and compatible Flash controller, which greatly facilitates the communication between the chip and the external memory. In this paper, we first designed the interface module of the flash controller, which supports APB/AHB/AXIAMBA bus protocols, and realised that the external flash can normally handle the read/write requests from the SOC bus. Through the request sent by the interface module, the register configuration module is designed to achieve the correct read/write and address. The flash controller designed in this paper supports the mainstream 4-wire serial flash in the market. For the serial transmission, the control module is designed to achieve the control of the flash state, instruction set and data flow, and it is optimised in the control module to support all the regular flash operations through the firmware, and to support the XIP function, which greatly facilitates the application of flash in the chip system.

articleTitle: Lightweight vit depression facial image detection with integrated attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of limited ability of extracting local information and excessive parameters in the diagnosis model of major depression (MDD), an image depression recognition algorithm based on the lightweight CNN+Transformer model of transfer learning (attn_ConvNeXt _MobileVit) was proposed to evaluate depression from facial images. The model adopts CASIA WebFace pre training model to improve the generalization ability of the model on small data sets; CA attention mechanism and ConvNeXt convolution module optimized by SimAm are used to enhance the extraction of local information; The lightweight mobile ViT module combined with global local information is used to maintain a low parameter amount while improving the depression recognition ability of the model. The experimental analysis of the public dataset AVEC2014 shows that compared with other methods, the predicted results of depression scores of subjects are better, with RMSE of 8.37 and MAE of 6.28, which verifies the effectiveness of the model and algorithm.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Drill Pipe Communication Approach Based on VMSK Modulation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the trade-off between communication rate and transmission distance in intelligent drill pipe systems, this paper proposes a novel communication scheme based on VMSK (Very Minimum Shift Keying) technology. The VMSK technique modulates carrier waves with distinct positive and negative half-cycle waveforms, enabling the differentiation of binary information (0 and 1) through the analysis of waveform variations between these half-cycles. This innovative approach allows the representation of one bit of information within a single carrier cycle, significantly enhancing data transmission rates. Moreover, we develop a specialized VMSK-based communication scheme, which conducts comprehensive simulation analysis of VMSK’s time-domain waveforms and frequency spectrum characteristics, and combines with the unique single-resonance-frequency transmission properties of intelligent drill pipes The proposed approach has been experimentally validated in an intelligent drill pipe simulation system, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of the VMSK communication approach.

articleTitle: Perturbation Analysis of Statistical Feature-based Evidence
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In complex equipment, the evidence reasoning method based on statistical feature extraction can realize health assessment under high dimensional correlation data. However, in the actual operation of the equipment, affected by environmental factors and operation modes, the monitoring data will be disturbed, which will lead to changes in the extracted features and affect the evaluation results. In order to analyze the influence of perturbation on the evaluation results, a perturbation analysis method for statistical feature-based evidence is proposed. By introducing perturbations into statistical evidence reasoning models, we analyze the effects of perturbations from variables to features to evidence construction and output results. Then, the relative utility variation factor is defined to judge the degree of perturbation influence on the evaluation results and the acceptable range of the model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the perturbation analysis experiment of the inertial measurement unit.

articleTitle: Speculative Inference with vLLM: Optimizing Heterogeneous Computing in Training-Inference Integrated Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become central to advancements in AI, but their deployment in heterogeneous computing environments poses significant challenges in terms of performance and resource utilization. In this paper, we present a dual-model speculative inference framework based on the vLLM architecture that optimizes LLM inference between CPU-GPU systems. The framework uses dynamic collaboration, adaptive resource scheduling, and memory-aware techniques to address CPU resource underutilization, GPU inefficiency, and bottlenecks in highly concurrent scenarios. Extensive experiments show that our enhanced vLLM improves throughput by a factor of 86.3x in GPU-only settings and 56.3x enhancement in speculative inference compared to traditional Transformer-based systems. Speculative inference in vLLM improves performance by up to 70%, especially for small batches and long input-output sequences. We also investigate the impact of batch size, input length, and memory management on performance. The framework provides a scalable solution for optimizing LLM inference, with future work focusing on hardware scalability, adaptive scheduling, and extension to multilingual and multimodal models.

articleTitle: FPGA Acceleration and ARM Collaborative Optimization Testing of Multi Task Scheduling Algorithm Based on Zynq SoC
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Existing multi-task scheduling algorithms face challenges in resource utilization and real-time performance. How to efficiently implement task scheduling to optimize system performance has become an urgent problem to be solved. First, a multi-task scheduling framework is designed to divide tasks into different priorities. Then, hardware acceleration of the scheduling algorithm is implemented on the FPGA, and pipeline processing and parallel computing are used to improve throughput. Next, the ARM processor is used for task management and scheduling control, a time-slice-based scheduling strategy is adopted, and dynamic priority adjustment is implemented. Finally, real-time communication between FPGA and ARM is established through an efficient data transfer mechanism (DMA). The experimental result in the paper shows a resource utilization of 74% achieved by the Method in 20 tasks, which far exceeded the 57% attained by the traditional methods. The multi-task scheduling algorithm based on Zynq SoC can boost scheduling efficiency dramatically, and in this way, provide individualized solutions for future embedded system designs.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of Trusted Boot Architecture Based on Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper delves into the optimized design of the trusted boot architecture for embedded devices. In an era where embedded devices are ubiquitously integrated into various aspects of modern life, safeguarding the security of their boot processes has become a critical concern. We commence with a comprehensive analysis of existing trusted boot architectures, highlighting their inherent limitations. Subsequently, an innovative optimized design is put forward, which incorporates state - of - the - art techniques such as refined measurement models, fortified key management strategies, and enhanced authentication protocols. Rigorous experiments are conducted to assess the performance and security of the proposed architecture. The experimental data convincingly demonstrates substantial improvements in boot - up time, attack resistance, and overall system integrity, thus offering a reliable solution for ensuring the secure boot of embedded devices.

articleTitle: Research on AI Model Invocation Framework and Integration Platform for Plasma Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The increasing depth of nuclear fusion research and the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) applications have heightened the demand for intelligent plasma control systems. Currently, a new plasma control system is under development, which requires the integration of AI algorithms to enhance decision-making capabilities. To address this, this study has developed a comprehensive AI model invocation and integration solution tailored for plasma control systems.On one hand, an AI model invocation framework has been designed to enable the system to quickly call and execute models, facilitating real-time inference tasks. On the other hand, an AI model integration platform has been developed, which can automatically integrate models provided by developers into the system. This eliminates the need for users to deal with the intricate details of algorithm integration, thereby reducing unnecessary time consumption. Finally, the effectiveness of the invocation framework and integration platform has been demonstrated through a set of comparative experiments and an MHD mode recognition model integration case study.

articleTitle: Implementation of Optimized Resource Allocation Algorithm in Grid Computing System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In this paper, a grid computing system based on resource optimization allocation algorithm is proposed. The system consists of four modules: grid user, grid administrator, grid resource and grid information service center. The resource allocation of the system includes two aspects: one is resource allocation on the user side, and the other is request ordering on the resource side. The two-stage optimization allows the requirements to be assigned to the most appropriate resource based on the user’s requirements. The main implementation methods of cloud computing service layer and the design of mobile Agent in the system are discussed in detail. This system can fully concentrate high-quality education resources in urban and rural areas. And through the cloud server for automatic management, to achieve the maximum degree of resource sharing. This is of great significance for improving the distribution of educational resources and public services in rural areas of China. In addition, the intelligent segmentation algorithm based on mobile agent is used to improve the intelligence of the system. Personalized learning service for users and real-time update of teaching resources are realized. The methods proposed in this paper are compared from three aspects: request completion success rate, completion time and average delay. The results fully illustrate the advantages of this system.

articleTitle: A multi-scale feature fusion facial emotion recognition method based on dynamic attention guidance
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel deep neural network, DynamicEmoteNet, is proposed for solving face emotion recognition tasks in complex scenes. It combines convolution, channel attention, spatial attention mechanism and multi-scale residual network. The Dynamic Channel Spatial Attention module adaptively enhances the feature expression of the key region of face emotion and suppresses the background interference through the dynamically generated channel weights and spatial weights. The Multi-Scale Residual Block module, on the other hand, simultaneously captures global expression structure and local detail features through parallel multi-scale convolutional branching, and utilizes a dynamic attention fusion mechanism to filter cross-scale valid information and enhance the robustness of the model to expression intensity, illumination changes, and facial occlusion. We conducted systematic experiments on three public datasets: AffectNet-7, FER2013 and RAF-DB, and the method proposed in this paper shows different degrees of performance improvement on each dataset compared to mainstream methods.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Optimization Method for High Slope Monitoring Points Based on Coupled EXDBSCAN-ATTCNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: High slope stability monitoring is critical for infrastructure safety, yet traditional methods face challenges in adaptability and precision. This study proposes a novel dynamic optimization framework integrating Extended Density-Based Spatial Clustering (EXDBSCAN), Attention-based Convolutional Neural Networks (ATTCNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The method enhances monitoring point layout by (1) fusing multi-source data (displacement, stress, geological parameters), (2) dynamically partitioning slope deformation zones via EXDBSCAN, and (3) optimizing monitoring points using a hybrid deep learning model. Validated through a decade-long case study of a large-scale slope along the Yellow River, the approach improved prediction accuracy from 87% to 91% after optimization, demonstrating significant advancements in spatialtemporal feature extraction, adaptive resource allocation, and early risk identification.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO-OTFS Satellite Communication Channel Estimation Based on Improved 3D-SOMP
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issues of low estimation accuracy and high computational complexity caused by the high-dimensional characteristics of three-dimensional (3D) channels and dynamic Doppler spread in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite massive MIMO- OTFS systems, this paper proposes an improved 3D structured orthogonal matching pursuit (3D-SOMP) algorithm. By exploiting the joint sparsity in the delay-Doppler-spatial domain, a dynamic 3D redundant dictionary is designed to mitigate the fixed grid mismatch problem. Leveraging prior knowledge of satellite channel coherence time, an adaptive atom search step size strategy is constructed to optimize atom matching paths. Furthermore, a residual energy variation rate threshold mechanism is introduced to dynamically control the iteration count. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to the traditional 3D-SOMP algorithm, the proposed method achieves an improvement of 1.8 dB in normalized mean square error (NMSE), along with reduced computational complexity and pilot overhead.

articleTitle: Non-contact Vital Signs Detection in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate phase demodulation is essential for vital sign detection using millimeter wave radar. The time-varying DC offsets and phase imbalance in complex scenarios can seriously interfere with the performance of demodulation. This letter proposes a novel DC offset calibration algorithm as well as a Hilbert and differential cross-multiply (HADCM) demodulation algorithm to solve the time-varying imbalance terms. It works by estimating the time-varying DC offsets from neighboring peaks and valleys, and uses the differential form as well as the Hilbert transform of the $I / Q$ channel signals to obtain the vital sign signal. Simulations and experiments have verified the effectiveness of the novel algorithm under low signal-to-noise ratio. Compared with the existing demodulation algorithms, the proposed algorithm can not only recover the original signal in complex environments more accurately, but also reduce the interference of noise on the signal.

Author Keywords: Hilbert and differential cross multiply demodulation algorithm

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Multi-Angle Gas Leak Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Hazardous chemicals play a crucial role in advancing industrial development; however, during storage, the potential risk of leaks presents a serious threat to both human health and the environment. To ensure effective management and monitoring of hazardous chemical storage, this paper proposes a gas leak detection method tailored for dynamic viewpoints. A Dynamic Foreground Extraction Module (DFEM) is designed to efficiently extract gas foreground images. Additionally, the Leakage Gas Detection Network (LGDNet) is optimized: initially, raw and foreground images are input in parallel to integrate the strengths of different layers, enhancing feature extraction. Furthermore, multi-scale feature fusion and an attention mechanism are incorporated to enable the model to adapt to leak scenarios at varying scales and focus on critical regions, ensuring accurate gas detection. Experimental results show that the LGDNet model with two blocks performs optimally. On the custom dataset, the LGDNet model achieved an accuracy of $99.42 \%$ and an F1 score of $99.31 \%$, offering a better balance between lightweight design and performance, surpassing mainstream deep convolutional networks. Additionally, tests on the GasVid dataset demonstrate that its accuracy exceeds that of the GasNet model by 2 percentage points, showcasing robust detection performance and adaptability.

articleTitle: Study on Neural Network-Based Prediction Methods for Ship Mooring Forces
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: LNG vessels are significantly affected by external environmental conditions during mooring operations, and there are risks such as mooring line failure in severe sea states. In order to solve this problem, this study employs back propagation neural network (BP), long short-term memory network (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) to predict the mooring force of LNG vessels. Comparative analysis of the models shows that GRU outperforms the BP and LSTM models, achieving lower mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), while obtaining higher coefficient of determination ($\mathrm{R}^{2}$). These results indicate that the GRU model provides higher prediction accuracy and reliability in predicting mooring forces. In addition, the GRU model exhibits excellent performance in terms of prediction accuracy, convergence speed and generalization ability. The experimental results highlight that the GRU model is able to effectively capture the nonlinear dynamic characteristics of mooring force time series data and significantly reduce the prediction error compared to other models.

articleTitle: Honeypot-Driven Decoy Block Vulnerability Obfuscation: A Structured Framework for Software Protection Against Symbolic Execution Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Symbolic execution, a powerful program analysis technique, poses a significant threat to software security by efficiently exploring program paths and exposing vulnerabilities. To address this challenge, we propose a novel Honeypot-Driven Decoy Block Vulnerability Obfuscation (HD-DBVO) framework, which integrates opaque predicates and decoy vulnerabilities to mislead symbolic execution tools. Our approach embeds strategically designed decoy vulnerabilities behind opaque predicates resistant to symbolic execution, thereby diverting analysis tools toward false paths while ensuring the integrity of the actual program logic. Experimental evaluation reveals that our technique increases symbolic execution time by 4.58 times, expands the number of explored paths by 32 times, and achieves an 83.7% false positive rate for decoy vulnerabilities, with a negligible runtime overhead of 6.3% and a 21.9% increase in code size. These results demonstrate that HD-DBVO effectively mitigates the impact of symbolic execution attacks, offering a promising avenue for enhancing software security.

articleTitle: Dynamic Edge Caching Strategy Integrating Deep Learning and Swarm Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that cache strategies are difficult to adapt to changeable factors in complex and dynamic edge caching environments, this study proposes a novel cache decision-making framework that deeply integrates deep learning prediction, user preference mining, and hybrid intelligent optimization. By constructing a user request prediction model and combining it with an improved collaborative filtering recommendation mechanism, a personalized cache candidate set is generated. Based on the prediction results, a hybrid optimization strategy that integrates the discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm and the genetic algorithm is designed to effectively avoid the trap of local optimality. Finally, a dynamic adaptive update mechanism is established. By monitoring the change rate of content popularity through a sliding window, the real-time evolution of the cache strategy is achieved. Simulation experiments show that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional strategies in key indicators such as cache hit rate and user request latency, verifying the effectiveness of the algorithm in dynamic and complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual-Branch Graph Attention Model for Rumor Understanding and Propagation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the widespread use of social media, although it has brought many conveniences, it has also intensified the spread of rumors. In recent years, graph neural networks have made significant progress in identifying the structural features of rumor propagation. However, more and more rumors adopt disguise strategies to evade the detection of the model. Inspired by the graph attention mechanism, this paper proposes a dual-branch graph attention model for rumor understanding and propagation, which integrates the characteristics of text content and propagation structure. The text content part constructs a graph network representation through the idea of self-supervised learning to capture the potential information in the text; while the propagation structure part adopts graph attention network modeling to fully explore the relationship between nodes and reveal the law of rumor propagation. In order to enhance the robustness of the model, we introduce the FGSM adversarial attack module in the training process to simulate the attack scenarios in practical applications, thereby improving the model’s ability to deal with various disguise strategies. Experimental results show that the proposed dual-branch graph attention model significantly outperforms the existing state-of-the-art rumor detection methods in experiments on two public datasets, showing stronger robustness and higher accuracy.

articleTitle: A Simple and Precise Segmentation Framework for Drone Swarm via SAM Proposals and Group Similarity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Intelligent swarm drone recognition methods are becoming more and more important with the advancing of drone techniques. Most current methods treat drone segmentation independently, neglecting the usage of inner-swarm group similarity characteristics. This paper tackles the task of infrared-domain swarm drone segmentation in remote sensing images from the aspect of group similarity analysis. We use the state-of-the-art segmentation algorithm as an initial module, and incorporate the segment anything model (SAM) to generate high-quality proposals, after which a specially designed candidate selection module carries out the group similarity analysis among swarmed drones to produce a finer segmentation mask. Experimental results on the Swarm Drone Detection dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art performance for the proposed method, and validate the effectiveness of introducing group similarity into swarm drone tasks.

articleTitle: Application of Cloud Computing Technology Based on FusionCompute in Data Sharing Center
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Cloud computing is a technology that virtualizes physical resources such as computing resources, storage resources, and network resources through virtualization technology to form multiple cloud host servers that can operate independently and without interference. It can effectively solve problems such as low utilization of infrastructure resources, large investment in funds, and lack of operation and maintenance management. This paper analyzes the current situation of infrastructure resources of the Hydrogeological Environmental Geological Survey Center of CGS (hereafter referred to HEGS Center), and builds Huawei FusionCompute cloud computing platform based on virtualization technology, which is applied to the data sharing center. The result shows that this technology can improve the utilization rate of infrastructure resources, reduce the energy consumption of human, financial and material resources, and has a good practical effect in the sharing of infrastructure resources.

articleTitle: Cross-Time Domain Dynamic Human Detection Based on WIFI-CSI Feature Weighted Voting
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To date, numerous studies have been conducted on passive sensing techniques for WiFi-CSI, yet the application of these methods to real-world scenarios still faces challenges across both temporal and spatial domains. For dynamic human body detection across the time domain, this paper proposes a featureweighted voting (FWV) algorithm, which integrates the prediction results of various features to achieve a comprehensive prediction. First, the collected CSI data is processed by calculating the amplitude and applying denoising techniques. Based on this, five CSI features are extracted, each characterizing different aspects of the dynamic human body’s CSI data. Then, the trained model is used to predict the validation set and the weights of each feature are calculated based on the prediction results of the validation set. Finally, by combining the feature weights with the respective prediction results, a comprehensive decision is made to determine the presence of a dynamic human body. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of over $99 \%$ in dynamic human body detection, validating the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Compute KV First: Scaling up Time Series Model with Cross-Retention-only Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Transformers have significantly advanced time series forecasting, but still face challenges such as quadratic time complexity, high memory consumption, and lack of positional priors. While recent research has explored Cross-Attention-only architectures that outperform complex Transformer models, the quadratic complexity of vanilla attention remains a bottleneck for scaling time series Transformers. With the rapid development of large language models, research in the NLP field has focused on addressing the quadratic complexity issue of attention mechanisms. Inspired by the recent Retentive Network (RetNet) in the field of NLP, we propose CKVF, a Cross-Retention-only Time Series Transformer that achieves linear complexity by computing key-value (KV) representations first, yet retains global attention capability. Building on RetNet’s retention mechanism, we introduce Cross-Retention, an adaptation of RetNet’s retention mechanism. Cross-Retention avoiding the high complexity introduced by attention matrices. Furthermore, we incorporate a self-adaptive adjacency matrix within Cross-Retention to capture dependencies between variables more effectively. Extensive experiments thoroughly validate that CKVF achieves state-of-the-art performance across various benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: A novel hybrid system for wind speed forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate wind speed prediction is vital to enhance wind energy utilization efficiency and maintaining the stability of societal structures. In this paper, the primordial wind speed data is decomposed via variational mode decomposition (VMD) into sub-sequences spanning low to high frequency components. The low-frequency sequences are then predicted using a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), while the high-frequency sequences are forecasted using an extreme learning machine (ELM). This paper introduces a novel method that employs cosine similarity (CS) to determine the length of the input in a deep learning model, which is termed lookback. Finally, the individual predictions are effectively integrated to produce the final forecasts. This hybrid system is referred to as VMD-CS-BiGRU-ELM. Predictions based on real wind speed data and different error criteria indicate that the proposed system performs well.

articleTitle: Exploration of rice disease data sharing scheme based on blockchain and federal learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Rice diseases severely impact rice yield and quality, posing threats to food security and agricultural economies. Traditional manual identification of rice diseases exhibits multiple limitations, while deep learning, despite its potential, faces challenges in agricultural applications such as insufficient data volume, uneven data distribution, and data privacy-security concerns. This study proposes a rice disease data sharing and privacy protection scheme by integrating blockchain technology with a federated learning framework. Leveraging blockchain’s decentralized and tamper-proof features to replace traditional federated learning’s centralized servers, the approach employs smart contracts for global model aggregation. A differential privacy mechanism is introduced to process model parameters, ensuring data privacy protection. Experimental results demonstrate that this solution effectively safeguards data privacy without compromising federated learning accuracy, while enhancing data utilization efficiency and sharing effectiveness, thereby providing robust technical support for the advancement of smart agriculture.

articleTitle: Obstacle Geometric Features based Map Segmentation for Architectural Coating Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Traditional global path planning struggles with large-scale and dynamic structures. To reduce planning complexity, map segmentation methods are developed to dividing a global region into sub-regions. Current research integrates geometric and semantic data, edge-cloud collaboration and construction metrics. In this paper, a novel map segmentation method based on obstacle geometric features is proposed to stress the complexity of coating robots path planning.

articleTitle: Rock image recognition method based on ECAResNet50 transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Intelligent rock recognition is crucial for geological research and engineering applications. In this paper, we propose an ECA-ResNet50 model that incorporates the ECA attention mechanism and migration learning. The model is validated and evaluated on a rock image dataset. Experiments show that the model achieves an accuracy of 95.4%, which significantly improves the rock image recognition capability.

articleTitle: Coal mine roadway deformation analysis based on 3D laser point cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, coal mine roadway safety monitoring faces higher accuracy requirements. In this paper, we propose a method to quantify the deformation of the roadway based on 3D laser point cloud: we construct a global point cloud model of the roadway, preprocess and optimize the point cloud data by pixel raster downsampling, radius outlier removal, etc. Secondly, we construct a quasi-uniform NURBS curve model to extract the point cloud set along the normal section, and finally, we carry out the accuracy experiments. The results show that the error of this method is within 1 cm, which has important engineering application value.

articleTitle: MobileViT-Based Dog Breed Classification and AI Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As urbanization accelerates, dog ownership is becoming more common, impacting public safety and community well-being. This paper proposes a MobileVit-based deep learning model for accurate dog breed classification, integrated with a GPT component for behavioral analysis and risk assessment. The system provides real-time risk alerts to administrators, security personnel, and pet owners, helping implement preventive measures. Additionally, it supports intelligent pet management, promotes harmonious human-pet coexistence, and contributes to urban pet regulation development.

articleTitle: Dynamic Detection and Analysis Strategy of Students’ Abnormal Behaviors Based on LOF-GMM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study focuses on the field of vocational education and aims to use the LOF-GMM algorithm to achieve dynamic detection of students’ abnormal behaviors. Based on the detection results, effective analysis strategies are proposed. By collecting multi-dimensional data of students, this algorithm is utilized to accurately identify the abnormal points in learning behaviors and performances. Furthermore, an in-depth analysis of the causes behind the abnormal behaviors is conducted, providing a powerful basis for personalized education, optimization of teaching content, construction of decision support systems, etc. This is intended to promote the improvement of students’ comprehensive qualities and contribute to the highquality development of vocational education.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Prediction Model Based on GBDT-RF
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Heart disease affects the quality of life and even the safety of countless people. Exploring a model that can predict heart disease is significant for prevention and policy formulation. In this paper, a feature extraction model based on gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) was established after preprocessing the data from the cardiac database of the University of California. The results showed that cholesterol level, thalassemia status and ST segment depression had the greatest contribution to the diagnosis of heart disease, and the characteristic contribution was $19.70 \%, 13.91 \%$ and $12.80 \%$, respectively. Subsequently, based on the gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) features, the random forest (RF) heart disease prediction model is established, and four machine learning models, including BP neural network, random forest model, decision tree model and logistic regression model, are established for comparison. $A_{c c}=0.833, A R=0.820, A P=0.872$, F1-score $=0.845$, AUC $=0.862$, which indicates that the RF heart disease prediction model based on GBDT feature extraction can effectively predict the diagnosis of heart disease.

articleTitle: Multiscale Strip Module and Aspect Ratio Sensitive Loss for Remote Sensing Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The aspect ratio and orientation sensitivity of objects in remote sensing images make object detection under the traditional framework face great challenges. To address these issues, we propose two methods: multiscale strip module (MSM) and aspect ratio sensitive angle loss (ARS Loss). MSM uses parallel strip convolutions with different receptive fields to enhance long-range feature extraction of slender objects, while ARS Loss dynamically adjusts the angle regression penalty according to the target aspect ratio to alleviate the IoU degradation caused by angular bias. Experiments on DIOR-R dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, which achieves 69.75% of the highest mAP under single-scale training. Compared with the baseline model, the proposed framework improves the detection accuracy of slender objects (such as bridges and harbors) by up to 1.57%, while maintaining robustness to near-square objects. This work provides a comprehensive solution for dealing with different geometric targets in remote sensing scenes.

articleTitle: Hybrid Parameter Estimation for Multi-Carrier Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate estimation of unknown signal parameters, such as carrier frequency offset, timing offset, and channel state information, is crucial for reliable communication in multicarrier systems. This paper proposes a novel hybrid approach that combines the strengths of traditional signal processing and deep learning techniques to enhance parameter estimation accuracy and robustness. We leverage signal processing methods to extract informative features from the received multi-carrier signal, which are then fed into a deep neural network for parameter estimation. This hybrid strategy allows us to exploit the inherent strengths of each approach. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method through simulations and over-the-air experiments, showcasing its superior performance compared to conventional signal processing and deep learningonly methods. Our findings highlight the potential of hybrid approaches to significantly improve parameter estimation accuracy and robustness in multicarrier systems, paving the way for more efficient and reliable wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Mask Optimization Method for Automated Vulnerability Repair
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, automated vulnerability repair methods, particularly those based on Transformer models, have been increasingly applied to address software security challenges. These methods often employ masking techniques to focus on attack-prone code areas. Inspired by Vision Transformers in object detection, this paper introduces a mask optimization solution. It integrates masks into the decoder’s cross-attention mechanism, allowing the model to focus on key vulnerability segments. Additionally, the mask is applied to the encoder’s self-attention, enhancing feature representation. The proposed method demonstrates improvements over approaches such as VulRepair and VQM.

articleTitle: The smart contract vulnerability detection based on pre-trained model feature fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the widespread application of blockchain technology across various fields, the security of smart contracts has become increasingly important. In the field of anomaly detection, particularly in smart contract vulnerability detection, pre-trained models have demonstrated tremendous potential, improving the accuracy and efficiency of vulnerability detection. However, these models typically focus on a single modality, which limits their applicability.
