While integrating multiple models can mitigate this issue, effectively fusing features from different pretrained models remains a challenge that needs to be addressed.To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a feature fusion method for smart contract vulnerability detection based on pre-trained models (PFSCV). The method uses contrastive learning (CL) to capture fine-grained relational information between smart contracts, generating sample pairs based on the relationships between contracts to guide the fine-tuning of the pre-trained model CodeBERT, enabling it to learn contextual information from the source code. At the same time, the UnixCoder model is fine-tuned to extract data flow information from the contracts. Subsequently, we introduce an att-BiLSTM (Attention-based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) model to fuse and integrate features extracted from different pre-trained models. Finally, extensive experiments on real-world smart contract datasets validate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Bi-directional Taint Flow Analysis: A High-precision Static Detection Approach for Java Deserialization Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The Java deserialization vulnerability represents a significant security threat to enterprise applications, enabling attackers to execute malicious code through crafted serialized data. Current detection approaches struggle with accurately identifying complex exploit chains and effectively capturing comprehensive data flow paths through traditional one-way taint analysis, resulting in false positives and missed vulnerabilities. Our proposed bi-directional taint flow analysis method innovatively combines forward taint propagation with reverse sensitivity analysis to precisely identify potential deserialization exploit chains through intersection analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that our SerialVulnScanner implementation achieves a 74.3% detection rate on mainstream Java components—6.9 percentage points higher than existing tools—with particular effectiveness in handling complex code structures and atypical exploit chains, thereby providing enhanced security for Java applications.

articleTitle: The Design and Implementation of the Integrative Validation Platform for Flight Test
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of avionics technology and computer networks, the complexity of the airborne test systems for flight test aircraft continues to rise, and the corresponding verification costs are also increasing day by day. This paper deeply analyzes the current verification process of airborne test systems and conducts research on the integrated verification technology of the Flight Test Instruments (FTI) system. An integrated verification platform that incorporates data acquisition, recording, real-time inspection, data analysis and anomaly data monitoring functions has been elaborately designed and successfully implemented. The practical application of this system fully demonstrates that this platform can not only precisely meet the actual work requirements, but also effectively shorten the system verification cycle and reduce verification costs. In addition, the system has great promotion value for other similar fields.

articleTitle: A U-Net Based Lightweight Semantic Segmentation Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Image segmentation is an important research hotspot in the field of computer graphics processing, and more and more scholars pay attention to it gradually. At present, semantic segmentation models not only need to have high-precision scene parsing ability, but also must meet strict real-time requirements. Therefore, it is of great theoretical significance and practical value to deeply study the balance mechanism between accuracy and speed of semantic segmentation. Based on the U-Net model, the backbone network of feature extraction is deleted to reduce the complexity of the model. At the same time, dilated convolution is introduced to increase the receptive field, so as to better capture the context information. The model further improves the ability of feature expression through the attention mechanism. In addition, a hybrid loss function is designed to accelerate the convergence of the model and enhance the ability to capture detailed features. The proposed method is verified on the CamVid dataset. Experiments show that the model achieves $80.23 \%$ and $88.06 \%$ in mIoU and mPA, which has significant performance improvement compared with other existing algorithms, verifying the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in semantic segmentation.

articleTitle: PDESpectralRefiner: Achieving More Accurate Long Rollouts with Spectral Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Generating accurate and stable long rollouts is a notorious challenge for time-dependent PDEs (Partial Differential Equations). Recently, motivated by the importance of high-frequency accuracy, a refiner model called PDERefiner utilizes diffusion models to refine outputs for every time step, since the denoising process could increase the correctness of modeling high frequency part. For 1-D Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, refiner models can degrade the amplitude of high frequency part better than not doing refinement process. However, for some other cases, the spectrum might be more complicated. For example, for a harder PDE like Navior-Stokes equation, diffusion models could over-degrade the higher frequency part. This motivates us to release the constraint that each frequency weighs the same. We enhance our refiner model with doing adjustments on spectral space, which recovers Blurring diffusion models. We developed a new v-prediction technique for Blurring diffusion models, recovering the MSE training objective on the first refinement step. We show that in this case, for different model backbones, such as U-Net and neural operators, the outputs of PDE-SpectralRefiner are more accurate for both one-step MSE loss and rollout loss.

articleTitle: Research on privacy protection mechanism based on edge computing in Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the contradiction between real-time data processing and privacy protection in edge computing of Internet of Vehicles, this paper proposes a dynamic collaborative differential privacy mechanism (DCDP). This mechanism clusters edge nodes by DBSCAN algorithm, builds a density-aware dynamic privacy budget allocation model, and realizes multi-node collaborative data aggregation by combining the improved PBFT consensus protocol. The experiment is based on the SUMO-NS-3 joint simulation platform. In the scenario of 300 m coverage radius, when the vehicle density reaches 80 vehicles $/ \mathrm{km}^{2}$, the privacy leakage rate of DCDP is only $0.078 \%$, which is $42.3 \%$ lower than that of traditional differential privacy (TDP); the root mean square error (RMSE) of traffic flow estimation is 2.15 vehicles/minute, which is $28.7 \%$ higher than that of the location-independent algorithm (PIDP). The system delay experiment shows that the average processing time of DCDP is 12.4 ms, which is $65.2 \%$ shorter than that of the blockchain-assisted solution (BCDP).

articleTitle: FSDE-net: Coarse-to-Fine Feature Separation Depth Estimation Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Towards the drawbacks of insufficient accuracy and inexplicit details in monocular depth estimation, a coarse-to-fine feature separation depth estimation network with two stages, namely FSDE-net is proposed in this paper. A feature separation network to obtain one complementary group of features as salient features and depth features for distilling depth information is dedicatedly designed in the first stage. In the second stage, coarse depth maps of multiple receptive fields are generated for further restoring the refined depth map. In addition, a long-range skip connection structure between the two stages is proposed to compensate for information loss in the long propagation of the network. Experimental results on the KITTI dataset show that our proposed method can achieve the absolute relative error of 0.090, the squared relative error of 0.701 and the linear root mean squared error of 4.365, outperforming existing representative methods.

articleTitle: The spatio-temporal evolution of provincial carbon emissions in China based on machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the increasingly severe global climate change issue, controlling carbon emissions has become a global focus. Taking the provincial carbon emission dataset of China as the research object, and combining the STIRPAT model with machine learning methods, this paper analyzes the spatio-temporal evolution characteristics and driving factors of carbon emissions in China. The research results show that there are significant regional differences in carbon emissions in different regions of China, with the eastern and northern regions having significantly higher carbon emissions than the southern and western regions. At the same time, there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between carbon emissions and economic growth, verifying the EKC hypothesis. The carbon emission prediction results using machine learning models show that if the current policy intensity is maintained, China’s carbon emissions will tend to stabilize and gradually decline in the coming years. In addition, improving energy conversion efficiency and promoting low-carbon technologies play an important role in carbon reduction. This paper provides a reference basis for the formulation of regional carbon reduction policies and low-carbon transformation in China.

articleTitle: AFSA-FL: A flexible semi-asynchronous federated learning framework
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Federated learning has attracted significant attention in recent years, providing a secure and feasible approach for cross-institutional and cross-organizational data collaboration. Synchronous federated learning offers advantages such as easier control of convergence, simpler implementation, and better interpretability. However, it suffers from long waiting times, high stability requirements, and limited scalability. Asynchronous federated learning overcomes the issue of slow nodes in synchronous federated learning, offering higher efficiency and better scalability. However, it also introduces challenges such as complex model convergence and the risk of outdated updates. Inspired by these approaches, we propose a flexible semi-asynchronous federated learning scheme AFSA-FL to address the issues of low round efficiency and slow convergence under extreme conditions. We optimize client selection and global aggregation during the training process of the global model. This approach mitigates the impact of model staleness while ensuring model convergence. Experimental simulations demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces training time per round and improves the accuracy of the global model.

articleTitle: Deep learning-driven head posture detection and real-time feedback system
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: A real-time head posture detection and feedback system was developed to address increasing cervical spine problems in office environments. The system employs a lightweight HPENet model (4.2M parameters) achieving 3.35° detection error and 23.1FPS processing speed on Jetson Nano. Incorporating visual, auditory, and data recording feedback mechanisms, it improved user posture efficiency by 47.3%. The optimized system operates at 5.7W with 4.5-hour continuous runtime. A 72-hour stability test confirmed reliable performance across various environments, offering a practical solution for protecting computer users’ posture during extended work periods.

articleTitle: Improving Generalization in Fringe Projection Profilometry Networks through Physics-Informed Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the generalization capabilities of neural networks in the fringe projection profilometry (FPP) by incorporating physical knowledge through data augmentation. Current FPP datasets primarily consist of gypsum objects, leading to performance degradation when applied to metal objects. By leveraging the physical model of FPP imaging and reflectance properties, we design a data augmentation method that simulates varying material reflectance. This approach significantly improves the model’s robustness when transferring from gypsum-based training data to metal objects. Our experimental results demonstrate an 22.8% improvement in terms of prediction MAE on metal objects compared to non-augmented models.

articleTitle: HSelect: Effective Selection of Heterogeneous Software for Common Mode Failure Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the growing risk of Common Mode Failure (CMF), N -versioning has become a key strategy for improving fault tolerance and security in software systems. While studies often assume the availability of off-the-shelf heterogeneous variants, practical N -versioning systems are typically built using different versions of the same software. Selecting heterogeneous variants is a key challenge in building robust N -versioning systems. This work introduces HSelect, a novel approach for selecting N versioning variants by measuring software heterogeneity. HSelect detects code changes at file and block levels, generating a heterogeneity matrix to select maximally diverse variants. Evaluation on eight projects shows HSelect more effectively measures heterogeneity and mitigates CMF vulnerabilities than traditional methods.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Recommendation based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The growth of the internet and AI has caused information overload, making it harder for users to find relevant content. Deep learning-based recommendation systems help by analyzing user-product latent interactions for recommendations. However, these systems have limitations, including their inability to fully capture the nuances of users’ long-term and short-term interests, as well as the persistent problem of data sparsity. This paper aims to improve recommendation systems by using graph neural networks GNNs to leverage more available information. The key contributions include the proposal of a multi-modal GNN recommendation algorithm MHGR, which models capture local user interests. The algorithm outperforms others on several datasets, showing $4.46 \%$ improvement in Recall@20 and $2.42 \%$ in NDCG@20 on the Clothing dataset compared to the second-best algorithm LGMRec.

articleTitle: HDC-YOLOv8s: An Improved YOLOv8s Algorithm for Steel Surface Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issues of low contrast and strong background interference in steel surface defect detection, which lead to high false positive and false negative rates, an improved YOLOv8s steel surface defect detection algorithm, HDCYOLOv8s, is proposed. Firstly, a lightweight backbone network based on HGNetV2 is used to replace the backbone network of YOLOv8s, enhancing feature extraction capabilities while reducing model parameters and computational load. Secondly, a hybrid dilated convolutional residual (HDCR) module is designed to replace the original C2f module in YOLOv8s’s neck, effectively integrating multi-scale information and enhancing feature representation. Furthermore, a dynamic weighted downsampling (DWD) module is introduced to adaptively adjust feature weights and reduce information loss during the feature extraction process. Lastly, a content-guided attention (CGA) feature fusion module is incorporated to adaptively aggregate low-level and high-level information through learnable spatial weights, improving detection performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8s algorithm achieves mAP50 of $81.1 \%$ and mAP50:95 of 48.1% on the NEU-DEF dataset, with improvements of $4.0 \%$ and $2.9 \%$ over the baseline algorithm, while reducing parameter count and computational load by $26.8 \%$ and $29.3 \%$ respectively.

articleTitle: A Library Implementation for DDS Packet Capture and Parsing based on Wireshark
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents an library implementation called NPGA (Network Packet Grabbing and Analysis), which serves as a comprehensive solution for packet capture and parsing in the Data Distribution Service (DDS) environment, with a particular focus on the Real-Time Publish-Subscribe (RTPS) protocol. The NPGA library is engineered with a modular architecture, integrating a customized version of the open-source Wireshark dynamic library for in-depth parsing. It offers a flexible API through a callback mechanism, enabling developers to conveniently capture and analyze DDS traffic. This library will furnish a toolkit to facilitate in-depth analysis and monitoring, thereby making it more accessible for developers to utilize and integrate into their projects.

articleTitle: Network Defense Strategy Model Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the limitations of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in modeling adversarial strategy evolution and the rigidity of evolutionary game theory in dynamic scenarios, this paper proposes a Dual-layer Cooperative Evolutionary Framework (DCEF). DCEF integrates the Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C) algorithm for real-time defense generation with an evolutionary game layer for global optimization, leveraging an incremental payoff matrix and adaptive triggering mechanisms. Experiments on the CICIDS2017 dataset demonstrate DCEF’s superiority: 86.2% defense success rate (5.6% higher than A3C), 38ms response latency, and robust adaptability to multi-stage attacks. The framework effectively balances short-term responsiveness with long-term strategic stability.

articleTitle: Epidemic Routing Optimization Algorithm Based on Node Cache Status
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the issue that the Epidemic routing algorithm in DTN generates a large number of message copies in the network, which can easily deplete network resources and even cause network congestion, we propose an optimized Epidemic routing algorithm based on node cache state, called EBNCS (Epidemic Based on Node Cache State). The EBNCS algorithm classifies nodes based on their cache status and adopts different message forwarding strategies for nodes with different cache statuses, thereby avoiding the resource waste and network congestion caused by blind flooding. Additionally, an ACK acknowledgment mechanism is introduced to delete successfully delivered message copies in the network, reducing network overhead. Simulation experiments show that the EBNCS routing algorithm significantly improves message delivery rate, network overhead, and transmission delay.

articleTitle: A method for automatically generating the Input/Output timing parameters of DDR controller
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The IO timing parameter configuration of the DDR controller can accurately control the timing of data transmission between the DRAM and the controller, ensuring that the data can be written or read at the correct time point, so as to ensure the performance and stability of the system. In view of the shortcomings of the existing methods, this paper proposes a new method to generate the IO timing parameters of DDR controllers, which obtains the delay information on the command and data transmission paths through the static timing analysis tool, and automatically outputs the IO timing parameter configuration files of the DDR controller with the help of scripts. Because this method directly calculates accurate results through timing analysis tool information and automated scripts, compared with traditional calculation methods, this method can avoid repeated manual measurement and simulation verification for many times, and improve the number of simulations and the total simulation time, which can effectively improve the efficiency of chip development and verification.

articleTitle: Exploration of automated transmission control model of communication instrumentation in the context of big data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the era of big data, with the continuous expansion of communication networks and the increasing complexity of data traffic, traditional communication instrument transmission control methods face challenges. This study aims to explore an automated transmission control model for communication instruments by integrating big data technology. A layered architecture model is designed, including data acquisition, processing, control decision - making, and application layers. A multilayer perceptron neural network - based automation control algorithm is employed. Performance tests are carried out using specific hardware and software environments. The results show that the model’s performance varies under different signal intensities, interference intensities, data types, and transmission rates. Generally, as the signal - to - noise ratio improves, the data transmission delay decreases, the bit - error rate reduces, and the system throughput increases. Different data types also affect performance due to different processing complexities.

articleTitle: Improving User Experience in E-commerce Through Intelligent Demand Forecasting and Inventory Visualization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: E-commerce has grown significantly, creating an urgent need for businesses to enhance user experience. This paper proposes innovative strategies to achieve this through intelligent demand forecasting and inventory visualization. We introduce a system that leverages historical sales data alongside current market trends to deliver more accurate demand predictions. By implementing machine learning algorithms, retailers can proactively anticipate customer needs, thereby optimizing their stock levels and minimizing the chances of stockouts. Complementing this, an interactive inventory visualization tool is presented, enabling users to track stock availability in real-time. This tool not only supports retailers in making data-driven decisions but also fosters customer satisfaction by ensuring products are accessible. Experimental results from e-commerce platforms illustrate that our approach significantly boosts customer engagement and enhances sales performance, emphasizing the critical role of advanced analytics in transforming the e-commerce environment for improved user experiences.

articleTitle: Orientation-Aware Multi-Scale Fusion Algorithm for Point Cloud Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Recently, in the field of point cloud processing, a two-stage strategy of applying pre-training followed by fine-tuning for various downstream tasks has achieved inspiring performance in tasks such as object classification and semantic segmentation. However, significant challenges remain in terms of fine-grained feature capture efficiency and representation capability in sparse regions. To address these issues, this paper proposes an orientation-aware multi-scale fusion algorithm for point cloud classification. In terms of feature extraction, we utilize orientation-aware Octant-constrained K-Nearest Neighbors (O-KNN) and enhance the feature representation of sparse regions by concatenating multi-scale point cloud patches. During pre-training and fine-tuning phases, we learn point cloud contextual representations through the Masked Point Modeling (MPM) task. Furthermore, to address feature shift and information redundancy that may arise during feature extraction, we propose a key-value subspace adaptive selection mechanism, combined with root mean square (RMS) normalization, to mitigate the impact of these issues. The overall training process utilizes a Teacher-Student architecture and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) for self-distillation learning, ensuring robust and stable results. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves promising performance on the ModelNet40 classification task and the ShapeNetPart part segmentation task, confirming the dual advantages of our approach in feature extraction and model lightweighting.

articleTitle: Enhancing Spectral Efficiency in CSS Modulation via Cumulative Encoding
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Conventional Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) modulation typically transmits one data symbol per chirp, resulting in low spectral efficiency. In this paper, we propose a novel concurrent transmission scheme, termed Cumulative Encoding-CSS (CE-CSS), that enhances spectral efficiency by allowing multiple symbols to be transmitted within a single chirp duration. In the proposed scheme, the input bit stream is first segmented into symbols and then cumulatively encoded into groups. Within each group, every cumulative sum is mapped to a distinct chirp signal, and these chirps are superimposed and transmitted concurrently. At the receiver, dechirping followed by FFT-based peak detection and differential decoding enables the recovery of multiple symbols from a single composite chirp. Simulation results demonstrate that CE-CSS can significantly improve spectral efficiency while retaining the inherent robustness and low-power advantages of traditional CSS modulation.

articleTitle: Selective Cross-City Transfer Model with Dual-Attention Graph Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Cross-city transfer learning relies on auxiliary city information (e.g., POI) to compute node features, which are then used for selective knowledge transfer. The effectiveness of this process depends on the quality of node features, but existing GNNbased methods fail to fully capture auxiliary information, leading to suboptimal feature representations. To address this, we propose DAGTrans, a Selective Cross-City Transfer Model with DualAttention Graph Feature Extraction. First, we decouple node embeddings using Node Attention (NA) and Edge Attention (EA) to separate feature representations from interference signals. Second, Dual-Channel Graph Convolution Network (DC-GCN) extracts fine-grained semantic information from the node feature graph, capturing both local and global perspectives. Third, inspired by counterfactual causal intervention, we introduce random perturbations to the interference graph and integrate it with the node feature graph, minimizing distributional shifts to improve node embedding learning. DAGTrans enhances feature expressiveness and better leverages auxiliary city information, achieving $0.89 \%$ improvement over state-of-the-art methods in cross-city traffic prediction.

articleTitle: Lightweight Semantic Communication Model Driven UAV for Intelligent Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are crucial tools for remote sensing tasks. However, UAVs face limitations in computational and communication resources. In the context of the exponential growth of remote sensing data, it is necessary that this captured information be transmitted to powerful ground servers for better processing. To accomplish this task efficiently, this paper proposes an intelligent transmission scheme based on semantic communication. An end-to-end encoder-decoder network is trained to understand the semantic features of remote sensing images, ultimately reconstructing high-quality original images, which significantly reduces channel resource overhead. Additionally, to further reduce the computational load on the transmitter to better align with practical constraints, this paper introduces a pruning method based on $l_{1}$-norm regularization, which reduce the overall computational cost of the model while maintaining performance. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to baseline models, the proposed system features a more lightweight architecture and superior performance, even under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions.

articleTitle: Demand Analysis of Daily Necessities Based on Machine Learning Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the small sample size and irregular time series data of household goods orders, this study proposes a data repair and multi-model collaborative prediction framework based on the BGCP algorithm, focusing on addressing the limitations of traditional statistical methods in terms of data missingness, feature correlation, and adaptability to multiple time granularities. Innovative proposals include: (1) employing the BGCP algorithm to construct a Bayesian tensor decomposition model with shared regional parameters, achieving anomaly correction and missing value imputation (regional average RMSE=0.482); (2) designing the MMIFS multivariate mutual information feature selction mechanism, effectively capturing nonlinear features such as holidays and promotional activities (lag feature mutual information reaches 0.95); (3) establishing a multi-model prediction system with time granularity adaptability, where the CRU model enhances daily granularity prediction accuracy through a continuous time increment module (MSE=0.643×10^7), the DeepAR model optimizes weekly granularity prediction using an autoregressive network (MSE=0.475×10^7), and the Prophet model performs best at monthly granularity prediction due to its trend decomposition capability (MSE=0.310×10^7). Experiments show that compared to traditional methods, the proposed framework reduces prediction errors at daily/weekly/monthly time granularities by 18.3%/23.6%/34.7%, respectively, verifying the adaptability of the multi-model collaborative mechanism to complex time series features. The research results provide a fine-grained demand forecasting method for supply chain management, particularly suitable for short-life-cycle products with promotional fluctuations and seasonal abrupt changes.

articleTitle: Research on Data Privacy Protection Scheme Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper conducts an in - depth study of data privacy protection methods based on consortium blockchains. With the arrival of the era of massive data, data privacy protection has become of vital importance. By adopting AES and HECC encryption algorithms, the encryption and decryption efficiency of privacy data has been effectively improved, and the security of privacy data has been strongly ensured. Verified by experiments, in the specific application scenario of data privacy protection, this scheme demonstrates excellent privacy and high feasibility. Compared with existing solutions, this scheme has significant advantages in the backup management of massive data and can better meet the actual application requirements. This indicates that the scheme provides a practical and efficient solution for data privacy protection, and is expected to be widely applied and promoted in related fields.

articleTitle: Research on the identification of electromagnetic radiation and acoustic emission precursor signals of rock burst
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In this paper, the extraction of precursor signals in acoustic emission and electromagnetic radiation and the identification of precursor signal time intervals are studied. Firstly, the auto-covariance function, Kendall standardized variables and Mann-Kendall standardized variables are selected as the trend characteristics, and the stationarity analysis and trend test are carried out. Then, the support vector machine model is established with these three precursory features as input vectors. Finally, the time interval of the precursor signal is found by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: KGCBC: Knowledge graph completion model of BERT hybrid Convolution
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a critical foundational resource supporting numerous intelligent tasks, knowledge graphs face the challenge of incomplete triples. Common Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) methods are typically divided into structural embeddingbased models and semantic comprehension-based models, which often risk partial information loss. This paper proposes KGCBC, a hybrid model integrating BERT and convolutional networks, designed to extract structural and semantic information from triples through dedicated convolutional and BERT modules. The convolutional module incorporates multi-head attention mechanisms to dynamically enhance structural features. Ablation studies validate the complementary roles of the two modules. Evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate KGCBC’s outstanding performance, surpassing state-of-the-art models on WN18RR.

articleTitle: An adaptive bitrate method based on human visual characteristics
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for optimizing panoramic video transmission by integrating human visual system (HVS) characteristics, with a focus on non-uniform bitrate allocation. We introduce a viewport prediction algorithm, HVC360, that leverages visual attention mechanisms. The bitrate allocation problem is modeled as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where the system dynamically adjusts bitrate distribution based on user viewport predictions and network conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods, improving the comprehensive QoE index and HVC score by $9 \%$, and achieving an $81 \%$ allocation to the viewport, compared to $72 \%$ in conventional methods. The model demonstrates superior performance in long-term viewport prediction and efficient bandwidth utilization, offering a robust solution for next-generation immersive media transmission.

articleTitle: Assessment of AGV Safety Perception in Smart Warehouse
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The safety perception capabilities of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) in dynamic warehouse environments are critical for collision-free operation. Existing safety assessment, however, rely heavily on fragmented manufacturer self-certification and lack standardized testing protocols, particularly for non-contact obstacle avoidance. To address this gap, this study proposes a laser point cloud-based framework for systematically assessing AGV safety perception performance across three dimensions: motion interaction, obstacle reflectivity, and spatial angle and distance perception. The methodology integrates calibrated laser point clouds with quantitative metrics to ensure reproducibility and industrial relevance. Experimental results confirmed the system’s compliance with safety application requirements in smart warehouse. AGV’s dynamic obstacle avoidance ability was assessed under varying speeds and motion modes, with minimum safe distance (MSD) as the key metric. The Obstacle reflectivity assessment quantified detection rates (DR) for objects with reflectivity ranging from $10 \%$ to $90 \%$, while spatial angle and distance experiments evaluated field-of-view (FOV) coverage and boundary recognition accuracy. The proposed methodology not only standardizes AGV safety evaluation but also provides a robust foundation for AGV safety certification processes.

articleTitle: Comparative study on automatic identification and performance of cotton pests and diseases based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Cotton yield is significantly affected by pests and diseases. This study proposes using three deep learning models—AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and ResNet18—to automatically identify cotton pests and diseases. The models were trained on a dataset containing multiple types of cotton pests and diseases, with normalization and standardization applied to the data, achieving recognition accuracies of $72.22 \%, 90.12 \%$, and 93.67%, respectively. Ablation experiments conducted on GoogLeNet and ResNet18 showed that the Inception module and residual blocks contributed 6.92% and 4.15% to the accuracy of their models, respectively. At the end of the article, an improved ResNet model was proposed, achieving a recognition accuracy of 95.68%. This study concludes that AlexNet is not well-suited for practical applications due to its lower accuracy. In contrast, the multi-scale feature extraction capabilities of GoogLeNet and the detailed feature extraction of ResNet18 render them highly effective and promising for identifying cotton pests and diseases.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sparse Trajectory-Unified method for Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks Training
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Traditional Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) lack interpretability when dealing with complex nonlinear problems, and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) provides a new solution to this problem through learnable activation functions. Nevertheless, KAN has issues with low training efficiency and high-order networks. In order to overcome significant obstacles in KAN training, this work suggests a novel technique termed Adaptive Sparse Trajectory-Unified (ASTJU). The innovation of the ASTJU method include: first, in order to achieve a more compact and efficient architecture without compromising expression ability, an Adaptive Sparse mechanism is proposed; second, the KAN training problem is transformed into a stable equilibrium point (SEP) by building a business, which makes the training process more systematic and efficient; finally, the pseudo-transient continuation (PTC) technology is used to speed up convergence and locate the local optimal solution. Experimental results show that on several datasets, such as the Feynman dataset, MNIST, and CIFAR-10, the ASTJU approach performs better than the conventional optimization method. It performs remarkably well in terms of model convergence speed and parameter utilization efficiency, in addition to greatly increasing test accuracy. In addition to offering a novel approach to KAN network training, this research offers fresh approaches to the interpretability and efficiency problems in deep learning.

articleTitle: Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification Network Based on Intermediate Feature Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Visible-infrared person re-identification (VI-ReID) aims to retrieve images of the same individual captured by visible and infrared cameras. With the advent of Vision Transformers (ViTs), existing methods have benefited from a strong global receptive field during the feature extraction stage.However, their channel attention mechanisms often lack flexibility and operate at a coarse granularity. Additionally, due to the significant modality gap between visible and infrared images, learning intermediate modality features remains a challenging task.To address these issues, we propose DFHNet, a novel network based on intermediate feature learning to facilitate effective VI-ReID. Specifically, we first employ a multi-modal feature module to extract both local and global features from visible and infrared images. Then, we introduce a cluster-guided contrastive fusion module, which leverages contrastive learning to integrate intermediate features generated from different modalities and scale sizes, effectively capturing view-common features that encapsulate both shared and complementary information.Extensive experiments on the SYSU-MM01 and RegDB datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the VI-ReID task.

articleTitle: Multi-tagged Objects Loss Detection in Unreliable Channels for Large-Scale RFID Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Missing object detection plays a crucial role in practical Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) applications. However, many existing solutions are not compatible with the EPC global Class 1 Generation 2 standard (C1G2) and are difficult to deploy in Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) RFID systems. This paper designs a scheme that supports target object detection based on object categories and batches. The scheme utilizes a selection code written into the user memory of tags, as designed by us. Additionally, we incorporate a lost weight mechanism to more flexibly address communication faults. Finally, simulation experiments verify that our proposed solution is more effective in detection compared to existing Bloom filterbased methods.

articleTitle: Enhanced Dual Control Station Protocol of UAV Swarm System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm systems have been extensively deployed in both civilian and military applications. As the command center of the swarm, the control station plays a crucial role in determining mission completion capabilities. This paper proposes enhanced dual control station protocol that employs hot standby stations operating in mutual standby mode. When anomalies occur in the primary control station, seamless switching to the standby one is immediately initiated, thereby ensuring uninterrupted working of the UAV swarm system. Furthermore, the standby control station possesses an additional function of data forwarding for error correction. When wireless communication is compromised by interference, the standby control station can forward critical commands to UAVs, thereby enhancing anti-jamming capabilities.

articleTitle: Vehicle target detection algorithm in complex environment based on hybrid attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of significant background interference, variable target scale and insufficient real-time performance in vehicle target detection in complex environments, this paper proposes an improved model based on hybrid attention mechanism and polarisation filtering (PTRDarknet-POSA). Firstly, the PTRDarknet module is embedded into the YOLOv5 backbone network<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, which adaptively enhances the channel characterisation and spatial localisation of the target critical region by fusing the SE channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms, and effectively suppresses the complex background interference. This hybrid attention mechanism enables the model to identify the target more accurately and reduce the false detection rate.Secondly, a polarised filtered feature pyramid network (POSA-FPN) is designed, and a dynamic filtering kernel is introduced to optimise the multi-scale feature fusion process, which improves the detection accuracy and efficiency. On the KITTI dataset, The model mAP@0.5 reached $88.2 \%$, a $1.6 \%$ improvement over the original model was achieved. This significant improvement verifies the superior performance of the model in complex scenarios. Experimental results show that the method significantly improves the robustness of vehicle detection in complex situations such as rain, fog, and occlusion, providing an effective solution for autonomous driving systems. This innovative design not only enhances the detection performance, but also improves the real-time response capability, making the autonomous driving technology more reliable and efficient in complex environments. By optimising the feature extraction and fusion strategies, the model demonstrates excellent adaptability and stability, laying a solid foundation for the future development of autonomous driving technology.

articleTitle: The path planning of a mobile robot based on the improved A-star algorithm combined with DWA.*
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, the significance of path planning has been increasingly recognized as a fundamental component in enabling autonomous robot navigation. This critical technology has emerged as an essential element for mobile robots to achieve self-directed movement and obstacle avoidance in complex environments. Currently, the $A^{*}$ search methodology and Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) are prominent techniques. A-algorithm is able to compute optimal global paths in static environments. However, in dynamic environments, its performance is limited, especially in real-time obstacle avoidance [1] and trajectory tracking. Comparatively, DWA focuses on local path planning and can dynamically adjust the robot speed and direction to avoid obstacles in real time. But it relies on global path planning and lacks global optimality. This study presents an innovative navigation strategy that integrates the A* search mechanism with the Dynamic Window Approach. The proposed methodology synthesizes global path optimization with local obstacle avoidance, addressing the inherent constraints of each standalone algorithm. The experiments results show that the postoptimization algorithm generates smooth paths and achieved the $19.13 \%$ reduction in search time.

articleTitle: YOLOv10 Traffic Sign Recognition Model Based on Lightweight Convolutional GSConv Improved with Multiscale Attention Mechanism MSAA
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To improve the precision and efficiency of traffic sign detection, especially in intricate traffic scenarios, we present a streamlined traffic sign detection approach utilizing an enhanced version of YOLOv10. To overcome the accuracy challenges encountered by conventional YOLOv10 in certain contexts, we initially implement a lightweight convolutional module, GSConv, replacing the traditional convolutional components in the backbone and neck layers of YOLOv10N. This modification significantly diminishes computational complexity and accelerates processing speed. Furthermore, we introduce a multiscale attention mechanism, MSAA, to refine feature fusion capabilities and bolster the model’s accuracy and robustness. Experimental findings illustrate that the optimized model attains a mean average accuracy of 83.96% on the TT100K dataset. When compared to YOLOv10-N, the model exhibits an 8.9% reduction in size, a 3.12% improvement in accuracy, and an increase in frames per second to 83.53. The enhanced model retains high accuracy even under challenging lighting conditions. This algorithm not only performs exceptionally well in the traffic sign recognition task but also exhibits significant potential for implementation on embedded devices, rendering it suitable for realworld applications.

articleTitle: Research on Battery Life Prediction Model Based on Multi-Physical Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for predicting the life of a battery based on MPF-DNN, which takes into account thermal, electric, chemical and so on. This model can accurately predict the battery life in various operating conditions based on the mathematical equation of metaphysical field coupling and deep neural network. The results show that the prediction error of MPF-DNN model is much lower than that of the conventional one. The experimental results show that MPF-DNN exceeds the traditional thermal, electrical and chemical models in terms of accuracy (MSE) and adaptability ($\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$), which is improved by more than 20%.

articleTitle: Screening of Natural Anti-Aging Compounds Based on WBDSS Algorithm and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This article addresses the challenge of traditional sampling algorithms struggling to generate representative samples of minority classes by proposing a dual-safe mixed sampling algorithm based on Wasserstein distance (WBDSS). The aim is to tackle the issue of sample imbalance in the screening of natural anti-aging compounds. WBDSS combines Wasserstein distance with a dual safety mechanism to generate high-quality minority class samples by improving the SMOTE algorithm, and fine-tunes the pre-trained TabPFN model to enhance the predictive accuracy in the screening of anti-aging compounds. Experimental results indicate that WBDSS outperforms traditional sampling algorithms across multiple evaluation metrics, and the fine-tuned TabPFN model, enhanced by WBDSS data augmentation, performs well in the task of screening natural anti-aging compounds, effectively identifying natural anti-aging agents.

articleTitle: Research on Protocol Parsing Gateway Based on Dynamic Loading Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices achieve data transmission and information interaction through various communication protocols, but protocol heterogeneity leads to difficulties in cross-device intercommunication. In response to this problem, this paper proposes a protocol parsing gateway architecture based on dynamic loading technology, which realizes the efficient parsing of multiple protocols through the offline script definition and the dynamic loading mechanism. This architecture allows the parsed data to serve devices or cloud applications directly, and supports protocol extension through extended parsing scripts, without the need to develop a parser for each protocol, significantly reducing the development complexity. Experiments show that this solution conforms to the development trend of the Internet of Things, has good extensibility and adaptability, and provides an effective solution for heterogeneous data integration.

articleTitle: The Research on College Student Employment Recommendation Method by Integrating Temporal Text and Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the limited application of recommendation systems in the education field, this paper focuses on the college student employment position recommendation and proposes a recommendation method that integrates temporal text and collaborative filtering. A time-decaying attention mechanism is introduced to model the temporal features of resume texts, capturing the dynamic trajectory of students’ project abilities. A cross-era comparison learning strategy is designed to alleviate the data sparsity issue. By adding a business rule injection layer, constraint functions are used to correct the text output based on rigid requirements such as education level and salary for job positions. Experiments on a real employment dataset evaluate the model’s performance, showing that both HR@N and recall rate results outperform baseline models. This provides valuable reference for the application of recommendation algorithms in the employment recommendation field.

articleTitle: COTKEG: A Chain-of-Thought and Knowledge Graph Enhanced Method for Medical Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) in natural language processing (NLP), their medical applications are gaining attention. LLMs can support healthcare professionals in diagnosis and treatment but face challenges such as hallucinations, limited reasoning, and constrained data. High accuracy and reliability are crucial in medicine. This paper proposes the COTKEG framework, integrating chain-of-thought reasoning and knowledge graphs to enhance LLMs’ medical accuracy. The framework includes two key modules: one deconstructs complex medical issues step by step, while the other incorporates structured knowledge to reduce hallucinations and improve reliability. Experiments on MMCUMedical and CMB-Exam datasets show that COTKEG outperforms baselines in exact match (EM), partial correct rate (PCR), and medical expertise (h1) and harmlessness (h2) scores. Future work can optimize retrieval, adapt to dynamic knowledge, and expand applications. COTKEG offers a promising approach to improving medical LLMs’ accuracy, reliability, and safety.

articleTitle: Semantic and Contextual Modeling for Malicious Comment Detection with BERT-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study aims to develop an efficient and accurate model for detecting malicious comments, addressing the increasingly severe issue of false and harmful content on social media platforms. We propose a deep learning model that combines BERT and BiLSTM. The BERT model, through pre-training, captures deep semantic features of text, while the BiLSTM network excels at processing sequential data and can further model the contextual dependencies of text. Experimental results on the Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification dataset demonstrate that the BERT+BiLSTM model achieves superior performance in malicious comment detection tasks, with a precision of 0.94, recall of 0.93, and accuracy of 0.94. This surpasses other models, including standalone BERT, TextCNN, TextRNN, and traditional machine learning algorithms using TF-IDF features. These results confirm the superiority of the BERT+BiLSTM model in handling imbalanced data and capturing deep semantic features of malicious comments, providing an effective technical means for social media content moderation and online environment purification.

articleTitle: Forest Fire Detection based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Forest fires are one of the most destructive natural disasters, causing significant ecological, economic, and social losses. Early detection and rapid response are critical for minimizing the damage caused by these fires. Traditional forest fire detection methods, such as manual monitoring and satellite imagery, often suffer from delays and inaccuracies. With the rapid advancement of computer vision and deep learning technologies, automated fire detection systems have emerged as a promising solution. This paper presents a novel forest fire detection system based on the latest object detection algorithm, which aims to provide real-time, accurate, and efficient fire detection capabilities. The proposed system leverages the YOLOv8 algorithm, which is renowned for its high detection speed and accuracy. The system processes real-time video feeds from surveillance cameras installed in forested areas to detect flames, smoke, and other fire-related indicators. We trained the YOLOv8 model using a comprehensive dataset containing annotated images of forest fires and non-fire scenes. The model was optimized for detecting small and partially obscured fires, which are common in early-stage forest fire scenarios.

articleTitle: Accurate Vital Signs Detection using SWD-VMD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate respiratory and heartbeat detection helps to monitor the physical health status of the human body in a timely manner. This paper proposed a swarm decomposition-variational mode decomposition (SWD-VMD) algorithm to accurately decompose vital sign signals into multiple modal components, addressing the difficulty in separating respiratory harmonics, noise, and heartbeat signals. Then, correlation coefficient is used to screen the relevant modal components, in order to achieve the reconstruction of respiratory and heartbeat signals. The experimental results have shown that the proposed SWD-VMD algorithm is more accurate in detecting vital signs compared to the EEMD, VMD and SSA-VMD algorithms. The experiments proved the feasibility of the proposed algorithm in detecting vital signs.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Dual-Interface Intelligent Assistant for openEuler with NLP-Powered Terminal Support
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: OpenEuler operating system has made remarkable progress in the technical level, but its complexity and rich functions also pose challenges for users in terms of learning and usage. To address this issue, this paper designs and implements an intelligent assistant tool tailored for the openEuler operating system. In terms of technology selection, the web side adopts frontend technologies such as Vue3+Element-Plus+Axios, and the backend technology stack is SpringBoot3+Mybatis+Redis, which supports multi-condition queries and CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) functions, enabling users to participate in the maintenance of the knowledge base. The tool side uses the framework of Textual, TF-IDF algorithm and cosine similarity algorithm to build a text matching system. By calculating the similarity between user-input keywords and existing texts and sorting the results, it achieves efficient and accurate text matching. Experimental results demonstrate that the tool offers high accuracy and fast response times, providing an excellent user experience. The innovation of this tool lies in its support for both web and terminal interfaces, integrating advanced natural language processing technologies to meet the complex requirements of the OpenEuler operating system. It offers users an intelligent and convenient tool that fills the gap in the field of intelligent assistant tools for OpenEuler.

articleTitle: Research on Brain-Computer Interface Classification Algorithm Supported by Motion Imagination
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, brain-computer interface, as a new way of human-computer interaction, is considered to be another important technological revolution after the Internet, mobile communication and the Internet of Things. The performance of BCI system depends on the performance of signal classification algorithm. From the perspective of classification algorithm, it is difficult for traditional signal analysis methods to be directly applied to brain-computer interface systems, so new methods need to be studied to solve the above problems. In recent years, brain-computer interface technology has been widely concerned by scholars at home and abroad. In this paper, we introduce the classical method of motion image signal analysis, and give a new classification algorithm based on fuzzy logic reasoning.

articleTitle: A Novel AI Model for Optimizing Excitation Parameters in Irregular Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: For irregular phased arrays, the failure of certain array elements due to uncontrollable factors inevitably leads to varying degrees of degradation in beam pattern performance. Restoring or improving the beam pattern performance thus becomes an unavoidable issue. The most direct approach to addressing this problem is to compensate for beam pattern defects by reasonably adjusting the excitation parameters of the remaining functional elements.Since this study considers scenarios where any array element may fail, with the goal of rapidly compensating for beam pattern performance under arbitrary failure conditions, the complexity of irregular phased array cases and the stringent real-time requirements make traditional adaptive array algorithms inadequate. Therefore, this research explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) methods, leveraging the model’s generalization capability and superior computational power, which holds promise for solving such highly real-time demanding problems.

articleTitle: Safe Path Planning in Unmanned Warehousing Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to solve the safety problem during vehicle traveling in the context of unmanned warehousing, this paper proposes an improved RRT algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (SAC-RRT). In this paper, a safety constraint module is added to the algorithm, and the deep reinforcement learning SAC algorithm is used to guide the direction of RRT expansion and dynamically adjust the sampling step size through the obstacle area ratio to improve the efficiency of vehicle transport. Experiments have proved that with this algorithm, the unmanned forklift can dynamically adjust its path, avoid areas such as cargo falling, and quickly arrive at the designated location while ensuring safety.

articleTitle: Research on DSP-based Integrated Navigation Terminal
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The GNSS/INS integrated navigation system is widely utilized in various fields due to its high precision and reliability. However, traditional multi-core architectures often face challenges such as hardware complexity, high power consumption, and large size. To address these limitations while maintaining navigation accuracy, this paper proposes an integrated navigation terminal design based on a loosely coupled GNSS/IMU algorithm, utilizing a single DSP chip as the core processing unit. By implementing timed interrupt tasks on the DSP chip, the design achieves efficient data acquisition and fusion, significantly reducing reliance on additional hardware and simplifying the system architecture. Experimental results demonstrate that the terminal achieves a positioning accuracy of less than 1 meter, a velocity error below $0.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, and a heading error within 1 degree, confirming the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Text Feature-Aware Network for Scene Text Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Scene Text Image Super-Resolution (STISR) aims to restore high-frequency details from low-resolution text images to improve scene text recognition accuracy. However, existing methods predominantly rely on character sequences predicted by recognizers for guidance, leading to imbalanced feature extraction across different characters. To address this issue, we propose an efficient framework named TFA-Net, which consists of two branches: a Semantic Guidance Branch and a Super-Resolution Reconstruction Branch. In the Semantic Guidance Branch, we design a Text Feature Enhancement (TFE) module to enhance and fuse the intermediate features extracted by the recognizer with low-resolution image features, thereby generating high-quality semantic guidance. In the Super-Resolution Reconstruction Branch, we propose a novel Efficient Attention Recurrent Residual Block (EARRB) to improve feature extraction efficiency and enhance super-resolution reconstruction capability. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that TFA-Net achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: High-Precision CBCT Scatter Correction via Monte Carlo Simulation and Physics-Constrained Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) plays a critical role in image-guided radiotherapy by enabling accurate patient positioning and adaptive treatment planning. However, its image quality is significantly degraded by scatter artifacts arising from photon-tissue interactions such as Compton and Rayleigh scattering, which compromise both soft tissue contrast and dose calculation accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates high-fidelity Monte Carlo (MC) simulation with data-driven deep learning for efficient and accurate scatter correction. The MC simulation component generates ground-truth scatter distributions under realistic clinical CBCT acquisition parameters, while a convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained to extract structural and texture priors from raw projections to estimate the scatter component rapidly and effectively. By combining the physical rigor of MC modeling with the generalization capacity of deep learning, the proposed method achieves robust and high-quality scatter estimation. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that the corrected reconstruction yields a root mean square error (RMSE) of approximately 9 HU, with a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.93 and a universal quality index (UQI) of 0. 95. These results markedly outperform both conventional anti-scatter grid techniques (SSIM:0. 82, UQI:0. 85) and pure deep learning baselines (SSIM:0. 87, UQI:0. 89). Furthermore, the framework is computationally efficient and suitable for time-sensitive clinical workflows. This hybrid approach not only improves the fidelity of CBCT images- particularly in soft tissue regions-but also supports more accurate target delineation and dose calculation. Its modular design enables future integration of advanced neural architectures and adaptation to diverse anatomical scenarios, paving the way toward artifact-free, quantitative CBCT imaging in precision radiotherapy.

articleTitle: Prediction of Mercury Removal Efficiency of Commercial Adsorbent in Natural Gas Based on PSO-BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To reduce the loss of mercury adsorbents in natural gas and achieve accurate prediction of mercury removal efficiency, the mercury removal efficiency of commercial adsorbent was predicated using various models in the present study. The mercury removal experiment of commercial adsorbent was carried out in simulated nature gas and 304 sets of experimental data were obtained. Regression prediction models including Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Ridge Regression (RR), and BP neural network (BPNN) were employed to predict the mercury removal efficiency of commercial adsorbent. The parameters of temperature, gas flow velocity, mercury adsorbent dosage, removal efficiency, and reaction duration were set as inputs, whereas the current removal efficiency was defined as output. The BPNN was the optimal model to predict the mercury removal performance of commercial adsorbent in nature gas, because of its high $R^{2}$ value (0.9219) and low RMSE (0.0445) and MAPE values (5.37%). To further improve the prediction accuracy, the particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) was introduced to optimize the hyperparameters of the BPNN. After optimization, the $R^{2}$ improved to 0.9532, while the values of RMSE and MAPE decreased to 0.0345 and $4.3 \%$, respectively. According to the above results, the PSO optimized BPNN model might prove to be a promising model to predict mercury removal efficiency of commercial adsorbent in natural gas.

articleTitle: Securing GPU Kernels with Lightweight Formal Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper reports our initial experience of applying lightweight formal method to validate the security of CUDA, the main programming language used for GPGPU programming. By “lightweight formal method”, we mean a pragmatic approach to verifying the security of CUDA programs coded by programmers. We do not aim to achieve full formal verification, but instead emphasize automation, usability, and the ability to continually ensure security as program evolve over time. Our approach first analyzes the program annotated with specification and loop invariants, and generates the corresponding verification conditions, which can be verified to ensure the security that is essential to GPU programs. Our work shows promising potentials by successfully verifying representative CUDA programs, including matrix multiplication optimized by using shared memory. Compared with some existing tools, our method exhibits better performance in CUDA programs security verification of without excessively increasing the programmer’s usage cost.

articleTitle: Rupture Disc Detection Method Based on Curve Detectors
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the automated production of bursting discs, this paper proposes a method based on a deep learning edge detection model combined with curve detector post-processing, effectively addressing the challenges of defect detection and positioning for circular blanks. The method first uses an edge detection model to extract the preliminary edge information of the workpiece, followed by a skeletonization algorithm and a segmented curvature detection algorithm to refine the extraction of single-pixel edges and calculate curvature segment by segment. By comparing curvature features, abnormal segments are identified to locate defects, while curve fitting techniques in normal regions achieve precise workpiece positioning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm ensures high accuracy while maintaining high computational efficiency, meeting the real-time requirements of automated production and significantly improving production quality and stability.

articleTitle: Analysis of key indicators based on large-scale drug testing data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The safeguard of drug security is an important prerequisite to guarantee public health and life safety. The pre-warning mechanism is an important means to monitor drug risks quickly and effectively. Based on the data mining technology, oriented to the massive data from each procedure of the drug industry chain, this paper mainly discusses how to pre-find the potential risks of the whole drug industry chain, and provides early-warning guidance via risk indicators. From the view of data modeling and technical processing, the key is how to integrate and analyze multi-source heterogeneous data (across space and time) and use the analysis of key indicators for streaming data. In specific, we first construct a distributed system and carry standardization for complex time-series data from different objects. Secondly, the potential risk of drug data is evaluated by using the key indicator analysis. At last, obtain the abnormal data objects and their fluctuating indicators of different periods. The application of the proposed method can provide potential hints or guidance for the sampling inspection of drugs, which is advantageous to improve the efficiency of the drug safety supervision department.

articleTitle: An multi-platform systematic error registration method based on Multi-criteria Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter with Singer model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Systematic error registration is a critical issue in multi-platform, multi-sensor target tracking. For noncooperative targets moving under the Singer model, this paper proposes a systematic error registration algorithm based on a multi-criteria adaptive cubature Kalman filter. By comparing the innovation obtained during the measurement update process with different decision thresholds, the algorithm selects appropriate compensation corrections to improve estimation accuracy and convergence speed. Numerical experiments reveal that the proposed methodology achieves notable improvements in parameter estimation fidelity and accelerated convergence rates compared to conventional CKF-based error registration approaches, demonstrating effective real-time compensation capabilities for systematic biases in multi-platform, multi-sensor architectures. The enhanced performance metrics confirm the algorithm’s practical applicability in operational scenarios involving distributed sensor networks.

articleTitle: SAM-MSF:A multi-scale indoor point cloud segmentation method based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of 3D data processing technology, indoor point cloud segmentation has become a critical step for tasks such as scene understanding, target detection and path planning. However, existing methods are insufficient in dealing with complex geometric structures and multi-scale feature fusion. For this reason, this paper proposes a deep learning-based multi-scale indoor point cloud segmentation method (SAM-MSF). The method firstly utilizes the SAM model to segment RGB images at multiple scales and generates nested segmentation masks; subsequently, the 2D masks are mapped to 3D space with the help of the inverse projection method, and the local point clouds are integrated through a hierarchical and iterative merging strategy to obtain the global segmentation results.

articleTitle: Decision Support Method Based on Interval-Valued Spherical Fuzzy Density Operator
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The information aggregation operator in a fuzzy environment effectively reduces information errors and enhances the accuracy of decision making. In this paper, considering the preference of decision makers (DMs) for dense distribution of evaluation information, we introduce density intermediate operators, and propose interval-valued spherical fuzzy density intermediate operator to achieve effective aggregation of information. In addition, the entropy theory in the interval-valued spherical fuzzy environment are extended. On this basis, a decision support method combining TOPSIS is proposed. Finally, an example is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, and its sensitivity analysis are carried out.

articleTitle: Northeast cold vortex detection algorithm based on reanalysis data prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The Northeast Cold Vortex (NECV) is a significant atmospheric phenomenon characterized by a large-scale, high-altitude cold low-pressure system that predominantly influences the northeastern region of China and its adjacent areas. This persistent weather system typically maintains its activity for periods ranging from 3 to 4 days or longer, exhibiting substantial meteorological impacts. Current methodologies for determining the spatial extent of the NECV primarily rely on extensive data analysis, which involves substantial computational resources and prolonged data processing time. Based on the above reasons, this paper proposes a method to detect the northeast cold vortex by forecasting and reanalyzing data and combining it with satellite cloud images, which solves the problem of poor timeliness of detecting the northeast cold vortex by using ERA5, and improves the detection capability of the northeast cold vortex. Compared with the single use of satellite cloud image to detect the northeast cold vortex, its effect is significantly improved, and it has guiding significance for the detection methods of the northeast cold vortex.

articleTitle: DenseTransformer: A generalizable and robust deep learning method for atrial fibrillation prediction from short electrocardiogram signals
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common kind of arrhythmia and its incidence and prevalence are increasing worldwide, with significant public health implications. As a result, increasing attention has been paid to predicting AF in order to prevent further progression of the disease. In this paper, we introduce a novel deep learning classification method that combines DenseNet and Transformer, namely DenseTransformer, to implement classification for AF prediction using short electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. DenseNet architecture is employed to extract local features and encourage feature reuse. Our model incorporates a novel bidirectional transformation mechanism, capturing global features and temporal dependency from both preceding and following context. We develop and evaluate the proposed method based on LTAFDB and NSRDB, which are available from the PhysioNet. The proposed method achieved $97.2 \%$ accuracy in predicting AF. The results indicate that the proposed method can accurately predict AF from short ECG signals. It can be foreseen that the proposed model shows great potential for use in clinical auxiliary diagnosis based on short ECG signals.
