articleTitle: Research on Reinforcement Measures For Voice Services in 5G Core Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: VoNR service of telecom operators involves 5G core network and IMS network, and there are many network elements involved in the realization of the service. IMS network, as the main provider of mobile voice service, has been deployed in scale as early as in the 4G era, and its development is relatively mature. In contrast, the 5G core network has been deployed for a short period of time, and the existing network application needs to be improved in many areas. This paper mainly focuses on voice services and discusses the measures needed to strengthen the $\mathbf{5 G}$ core network.

articleTitle: Transformer-based Multi-Touch Attribution Model for Large-Scale Digital Advertising Paths
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As digital advertising becomes more complex and widespread, traditional multi-touch attribution models and statistical methods often struggle to achieve high accuracy. While time-series deep learning models offer improvements, they face challenges such as long training times, slow parameter updates, and limited parallel processing. In response, this paper introduces the Transformer-based Multi-Touch Attribution model (TRMTA), which uses the Transformer’s global attention mechanism to enhance attribution accuracy in large-scale digital advertising campaigns. We validate the TRMTA model using nearly 260 million touchpoint data points from splash ads across 10 platforms. The results show that TRMTA outperforms traditional models like LSTM and Logistic Regression (LR). In real-world applications, the TRMTA model has helped advertisers optimize their strategies for the Double Eleven (11.11) shopping festival, resulting in a revenue increase of over $10 \%$.

articleTitle: Motion-Adaptive Deblurring of Fast Moving Objects
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Fast Moving objects (FMOs) captured by cameras often exhibit significant blur and artifacts. General deblurring algorithms face challenges in accurately restoring the appearance and intricate details of severely blurry regions within an image. To address these limitations and facilitate single image deblurring of FMOs, we propose a novel Motion-Adaptive FMOs image deblurring Network named MANet. Specifically, to effectively leverage the motion information of FMOs and guide the network to pay attention to blurry regions, we introduce three key modules including a motion-adaptive spatial channel attention module, a blur region identification module, and an adaptive dual branch module. The motion-adaptive spatial channel attention module incorporates motion cues and propagates them to subsequent restoration modules at each scale. Meanwhile, the blur region identification module precisely locates blurry regions for targeted processing. Furthermore, considering that blurry regions and clear regions exhibit distinct feature representations, the adaptive dual branch module is introduced to independently extract features from these two types of regions and subsequently fuse them rationally. Extensive evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate the proposed MANet performs favorably against general deblurring methods and existing FMO-specific deblurring approaches.

articleTitle: Lightweight Multi-Modal Few-Shot RF Fingerprint Recognition for Drones
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the increasing applications of drones in public safety, military reconnaissance, and commercial logistics, efficient and reliable identification of their identities has become a pressing issue. Addressing the challenges of sparse samples and diverse interference in complex electromagnetic environments, this paper proposes a drone RF fingerprint recognition method based on dual-modal few-shot learning. Researchers extract both timedomain and frequency-domain features by performing timefrequency transformation and statistical analysis on the original I/Q signals,. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms baseline approaches in accuracy and maintains a high recognition rate even in mixed interference scenarios and low signal-to-noise ratios. This provides an effective and feasible technical solution for drone identity authentication in complex electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: External parameter calibration method of outdoor pole camera based on drone assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of insufficient accuracy and poor applicability of traditional calibration methods in complex scenes, this paper proposes an extrinsic calibration method based on drone assistance. The target pixel coordinates in the images taken by the camera and the drone camera are extracted through target detection. The drone image and the map image are aligned using spatial alignment technology, and the target pixel coordinates in the drone image are converted into geographic coordinates. Finally, by matching the pixel coordinates and geographic coordinates of the same target, the camera extrinsics are calculated and optimized to achieve high-precision calibration. Experimental results show that the calibration accuracy of this method is better than that of traditional methods in a large field of view, the reprojection error is less than 3 pixels, and the geographic error is controlled within 0.5 meters. This study provides a calibration method that is easy to operate and reproduce, overcomes the limitations of traditional calibration technology in large-scale scenes, and provides a feasible solution for high-precision target positioning in complex scenes.

articleTitle: Bayesian Hierarchical Regression for Robust Multi-Site Neuroimaging Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Multi-site neuroimaging studies offer increased statistical power and generalizability but are often plagued by sitespecific variations that can confound analyses and lead to biased conclusions. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Bayesian hierarchical regression model that explicitly accounts for site-specific effects and heteroscedastic variance. Our approach incorporates site as a factor in the model, allowing for the estimation of site-specific effects while simultaneously modeling heteroscedasticity to capture varying levels of variability across sites. This not only improves the accuracy of the analysis but also provides a more nuanced understanding of the data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on a large multisite neuroimaging dataset, showing improved performance in regression and anomaly detection tasks compared to conventional methods. Our findings highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for site-specific effects and heteroscedasticity in multisite neuroimaging studies. The proposed Bayesian hierarchical regression model offers a robust and flexible framework for analyzing multi-site neuroimaging data, leading to more reliable and generalizable conclusions.

articleTitle: EEG emotion recognition based on 2DSinc convolution and attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In addressing the issues of low accuracy, Feature extraction capabilities are limited, and insufficient interpretability associated with conventional convolutional neural networks (CNN) in EEG emotion recognition tasks, this study introduces a novel EEG emotion recognition method inspired by the SincNet network architecture. This method also considers the limitation of SincNet, which is primarily applicable to single-channel audio signals. After preprocessing and segmenting the EEG signals, a parametric 2D Sinc layer is utilized to capture the essential features of the input signal. Local features are then further extracted using depthwise convolution. To improve the model’s ability to emphasize crucial information, an attention mechanism is incorporated to extract global features along the temporal dimension. Lastly, a fully connected layer is employed to complete the four-class classification task. Experimental results reveal that the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of $95.05 \%$ in subjectdependent experiments on the DEAP dataset, and $86.72 \%$ in crosssubject experiments. These results significantly outperform conventional CNN methods, The effectiveness of the proposed method for EEG emotion recognition tasks is confirmed.

articleTitle: Inverse Analysis of Dam Seepage Field and Seepage Safety Assessment Based on Monitoring Data of Osmometer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the seepage problem of earth-rock dam, this paper uses the real in-situ monitoring data collected by the osmometer buried in the earth-rock dam, and uses the method of combining numerical simulation with on-site monitoring to inverse the seepage parameters of materials in each partition of the dam. According to the calculated distribution of dam seepage field under different reservoir water level operation conditions, the dam seepage safety status is evaluated based on the conventional dam seepage failure type discrimination criteria. The research results of this paper can provide reference for the design and safe operation of earth-rock dams.

articleTitle: Research on detection of Pavement Surface Cracks Based on Improved YOLO v11
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Pavement surface crack detection is crucial for road safety. To improve the accuracy and robustness of current crack detection methods, this paper proposes a YOLO v11-based model that incorporates dynamic snake module, CAFM attention mechanism, and SIoU loss function. Experimental results demonstrate improvements of $2.71 \%, 4.66 \%$, and $7.65 \%$ in mAP@0.5, accuracy, and recall, respectively, compared to the original model. The proposed method ensures both real-time performance and accuracy, meeting the requirements for pavement crack detection.

articleTitle: Communication-Computation Overlap Strategy for Vector DSP Based on Phase Feature Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As the scale of computation continues to expand, it is necessary to focus not only on the improvement of computing performance but also on the impact of communication overhead, which cannot be ignored. The communication-computation overlap (CC overlap) strategy, as a technology that effectively reduces the impact of transmission on performance, is becoming increasingly important. However, traditional CC overlap strategies lack a clear data volume threshold to guide their application and fail to hide the prefetching overhead. We propose a phase feature optimized CC overlap strategy in vector DSPs. It divides the process into three phases and introduces three optimizations, building an efficient coding framework. This boosts overlap efficiency and adaptability to different data scales. Experiments on the FT-M7004 platform show the scheme speeds up two DSPLIB algorithms by over $10 \%$ on average in small and large data volume scenarios compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Path Planning and Obstacle Avoidance Algorithms for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of autonomous driving technology, path planning and obstacle avoidance strategies based on machine learning are of great significance for the efficient and safe operation of autonomous vehicles. In order to achieve automatic driving path planning and obstacle avoidance, this paper combines deep reinforcement learning and probability graph model to propose a complex method. First, Deep Q Network (DQN) perceives and decides the surrounding environment to obtain real-time information about road conditions, obstacle locations and other traffic participants. Markov Decision Process (MDP) etc are introduced to further perform path planning and dynamic obstacle prediction, optimize the trajectory selection and obstacle avoidance strategy of vehicles. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a much superior performance in the complex urban road environment, which can significantly enhance the operating precision and traffic safety of an autonomous vehicle. The suggested approach has validated terrestrial experiments in root tests, providing tremendous enhancements in navigation accuracy and measures of traffic safety for autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Intracranial Aneurysm Rupture Risk Assessment Based on Multi-scale Deep Transfer Learning and Clinical Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Background: Rupture of intracranial aneurysms significantly increases the risk of non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a condition often associated with high fatality. Accurately assessing the rupture risk of intracranial aneurysms is crucial for effective clinical interventions. Objective: This study presents an innovative, semi-automated framework that combines multi-scale deep transfer learning features (MDTLFs), enhanced by super-resolution reconstruction, along with clinical data, to improve the accuracy of aneurysm rupture risk assessment. By applying super-resolution to CTA images, we enhance feature extraction, thereby increasing the model’s sensitivity to anatomical structures that are prone to rupture. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 366 cases (226 unruptured, 140 ruptured), collecting clinical data alongside CTA images. For the first time, we applied super-resolution techniques with the Med3D model, extracting deep features from both original and super-resolved images and fusing them to form high-detail, multi-scale deep transfer learning features (MDTLFs). This approach captures structural details that are otherwise difficult to detect. The MDTLFs, along with clinical features, were optimized using LASSO regression to identify rupture-critical patterns, and the final feature set was evaluated across five machine learning classifiers (LR, RF, SVM, XGBoost, and AdaBoost) for predictive accuracy. Results: The multi-modal feature fusion framework achieved an accuracy of $89.5 \%$ and an AUC of 0.904, significantly outperforming singlefeature models (clinical AUC: 0.774, MDTLFs AUC: 0.855). Notably, super-resolution reconstruction proved essential in enhancing MDTLFs, leading to increased model accuracy by highlighting subtle image details that correlate with rupture risk. Conclusion: This study is a novel framework that combines MDTLFs, radiomics, and clinical data to enhance aneurysm rupture risk prediction. The innovative use of super-resolution reconstruction with multi-scale deep transfer learning marks a significant step forward, enabling more accurate and clinically relevant assessments.

articleTitle: Refining Graph OOD Detection in Heterophilous Contexts through Neural Collapse
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in graph neural networks plays a crucial role in relevant security deployments. Recent research on graph OOD detection focuses on the score of individual instances, utilizing aggregation operations to update scores. These approaches generally assume that neighboring instances are of the same distribution, an assumption known as homophily. However, in heteroophilic scenarios, these methods have a flaw in that the aggregation operation reduces the difference between the In-distribution (ID) data and the OOD data. To address this issue, we propose a novel inference-based approach, Graph Neural Collapse OOD (GNCO), which leverages the geometric properties of Neural Collapse and optimizes the aggregation operation, achieving generalization in heterophilous settings. In GNCO, we consider a unique geometric property of neural collapse, i.e., ID and OOD features tend to become orthogonal during the terminal phase of training. Based on this insight, the norm of the test instance feature within the ID subspace can be devised to derive the OOD score. We conducted comprehensive experiments to validate the efficacy of GNCO. Our results confirm that this method outperforms all benchmarks across a variety of real-world datasets.

articleTitle: A Data Balancing and Ensemble Learning Approach for Credit Card Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative method for identifying credit card fraud by combining the SMOTE-KMEANS technique with an ensemble machine learning model. The proposed model was benchmarked against traditional models such as logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines. Performance was evaluated using metrics, including accuracy, recall, and area under the curve (AUC). The results demonstrated that the proposed model achieved superior performance, with an AUC of 0.96 when combined with the SMOTE-KMEANS algorithm. This indicates a significant improvement in detecting fraudulent transactions while maintaining high precision and recall. The study also explores the application of different oversampling techniques to enhance the performance of various classifiers. The findings suggest that the proposed method is robust and effective for classification tasks on balanced datasets. Future research directions include further optimization of the SMOTE-KMEANS approach and its integration into existing fraud detection systems to enhance financial security and consumer protection.

articleTitle: Research on dpo handwritten text generation algorithm based on fine-grained improvement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Sign language text generation is an important research direction within sign language generation systems. The Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithm is a reinforcement learning model based on human feedback. It offers advantages such as controllable outputs, better alignment with human preferences, and independence from reward systems for evaluation. However, DPO-based sign language text generation faces three key challenges: (1) The scarcity of high-quality negative sample datasets in the field of sign language poses significant challenges to model training; therefore, this paper proposes a method leveraging word vector similarity to construct human preference datasets that make full use of negative samples. (2) The global optimization approach of traditional DPO algorithms, which struggles to handle local errors; therefore, a token-level dynamic weighting mechanism is introduced for finer-grained optimization. (3) The lack of systematic evaluation methods for assessing the accuracy and applicability of generated text; therefore, a multi-dimensional evaluation method based on a large model for handwritten text is proposed. Experimental results demonstrate that these fine-grained improvements lead to significant enhancements in the model performance for handwritten text generation tasks, with notable improvements in accuracy, fluency, and contextual understanding. This research provides new directions for advancing sign language text generation technologies.

articleTitle: Cross-Racial Face Detection Performance Analysis: A Comparative Study of YCrCb and YCrCb Color Spaces under Varied Environmental Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a robust comparative framework for face detection under varying environmental conditions through chromatic analysis in $Y C_{r} C_{b}$ and $Y C_{r}^{\prime} C_{b}^{\prime}$ color spaces, demonstrating geometric invariance to translation, rotation, and scale transformations. The methodology initiates with color space conversion of input facial images, followed by adaptive thresholding techniques for skin segmentation—employing optimized $C_{b} C_{r}$ and enhanced $C_{b}^{\prime} C_{r}^{\prime}$ channel boundaries derived from empirical skin distribution analysis. Subsequent refinement stages incorporate: (i) Morphological filtering using elliptical structuring elements for noise suppression, (ii) Geometric feature selection based on aspect ratio and compactness criteria, (iii) Multi-scale validation through pyramid decomposition Experimental results quantify detection accuracy improvements when employing the enhanced $Y C_{r}^{\prime} C_{b}^{\prime}$ model compared to conventional $Y C_{r} C_{b}$ approaches. The proposed dual-space analysis establishes a theoretical foundation for adaptive color space selection in cross-demographic face detection systems.

articleTitle: Centrality Analysis in the Multi-layer Temporal Trade Network of the Belt and Road Initiative Based on Motif
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the Belt and Road trade network, a country’s centrality is reflected not only in first-order trade interactions but also in higher-order trade interactions. Higher-order trade interactions refer to trade exchanges involving three or more countries. This study uses motifs to characterize higher-order interactions. Firstly, based on the trade volume data of countries along the Belt and Road from 2005 to 2022, this study applies information entropy to simplify the network and constructs multilayer temporal import and export trade networks. Then, using the eigenvector centrality method in complex networks combined with motifs, the study theoretically derives supercentrality matrices and marginal centrality expressions. Finally, experiments using these centrality expressions reveal that motif types significantly influence the centrality scores and rankings of certain countries, highlighting the necessity of considering higherorder interactions in centrality studies. Moreover, motif weights, inter-layer coupling strength, and hidden transition probability have limited impact on centrality rankings, demonstrating the robustness and stability of the proposed motif-based marginal centrality measurement method.

articleTitle: Research on the Parameters of Bistable Stochastic Resonance System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Stochastic resonance system provides an important means for low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) signal detection. Based on SNRstudy of the bistable stochastic resonance system, the relationship between the extreme value of output SNR of the system and input noise intensity are analyzed. The results show that when the noise intensity is high level, the system parameter corresponding to the maximum value of the SNR is larger and divergent. At the same time, the time-domain characteristics of the output signal corresponding to the optimal system parameters after multiple optimizations are closer to the actual signal.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Cluster Analysis System under Big Data Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Based on the distributed computing architecture, this research combines Apache Spark and Flink to optimise batch processing and streaming computation, and adopts algorithms such as K-Means, DBSCAN, and hierarchical clustering to perform efficient clustering analysis for different data characteristics. GPU acceleration, cache optimisation and indexing techniques are introduced to improve the computation performance, and a visual analysis interface is provided to enhance the user interaction experience. In this paper, we will elaborate the system architecture design, key technology implementation, experimental evaluation and optimisation strategy to explore the feasibility and superiority of the cluster analysis system in the big data environment.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Assisted Retinex Approach for Low-Light Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The method based on deep learning has made significant progress in low-light image restoration and enhancement. Especially in improving image quality under lowlight conditions. Traditional image enhancement techniques, such as RetinexNet. Have improved low-light image quality by decomposing reflectance and illumination. However, existing methods still face limitations in extreme low-light and complex environmental backgrounds. To address these issues. This paper proposes an improved method based on the RetinexNet framework. Integrating the Cross-Shaped Window Transformer (CSWin Transformer) Block into the RelightNet part of RetinexNet and introducing the Cross-Shaped Window SelfAttention mechanism. This method significantly enhances lowlight image details and contextual information by optimizing image relighting and detail restoration. Thus improving image recovery performance. Experimental results show that the method achieves significant improvements on low-light image datasets, with PSNR and SSIM reaching 38.0278 and 0.9462 Respectively, outperforming existing enhancement methods. Experiments demonstrate that this method has obvious advantages in detail recovery and handling complex backgrounds. Verifying the effectiveness and superiority of CSWin in enhancing complex low-light image tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Flight Control-Based Tunnel Drone Inspection System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Urban underground pipelines are the “lifeline” of the city. There are many problems of underground pipelines in our country. Although underground comprehensive pipe gallery is a solution, it also faces challenges. Aiming at the shortcomings of traditional manual and existing robots in pipe gallery inspection, this paper proposes a pipe gallery UAV inspection system based on intelligent flight control. The system integrates multiple algorithms to solve the problems of positioning, obstacle avoidance and defect detection in the complex environment of pipe gallery. Experiments show that the system has small lateral positioning error, good stability, high defect detection accuracy, greatly improved inspection efficiency, and reduced annual operation and maintenance costs. Its hardware design ensures the stable operation of extreme environments, and provides a technical solution with high reliability for the intelligent operation and maintenance of urban underground pipe gallery.

articleTitle: The Behavior Detection Method for Live Working Personnel Based on an Improved YOLOv4 Lightweight Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To meet the dual requirements of real-time performance and high accuracy in live-line workers’ behavior detection tasks, a detection method based on an improved YOLOv4 lightweight network is proposed. Firstly, the method replaces the CSPDarknet53 backbone of YOLOv4 with the GhostNet residual structure and optimizes the convolutional neural network using the Ghost module, significantly reducing computation and parameter overhead. Secondly, the introduction of the Global Attention Module (GAM) enhances the extraction of key features, improving detection accuracy. Finally, the Focal Loss is employed to optimize the loss function of the YOLOv4 network model, further enhancing detection performance and reducing computational resource consumption. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional YOLOv4, the proposed model reduces the parameter count by 10.3 M, improves mAP by $3.55 \%$, and increases detection speed by 1.12 times. The model demonstrates significant advantages in comprehensive detection performance, efficiently achieving real-time detection of live-line workers’ behavior, and provides strong technical support for the safe operation and maintenance of transmission line tasks.

articleTitle: BF-YOLOv8 Based Pavement Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Pavement defect detection refers to the various technical means to inspect, identify and evaluate road surfaces to ensure safety. Traditional target detection methods are inefficient although they are still effective in many occasions. Modern pavement defect detection is moving towards automation and intelligence, such as inspection by drones or automated vehicles, to improve the efficiency and accuracy of detection. In this paper, an improved yolov8 pavement defect detection algorithm BFyolov8 is proposed. In this method, the SAM- DETR++ fusion module is designed to enhance the model’s ability to detect small targets. The improved BAM module is added to the backbone to make the detection more efficient in paying attention to the main features of the input image. Moreover, to reduce AMP mixed-precision training, the 16-bit floating-point number (FP16) and the 32-bit floating-point number (FP32)is used to maintain accuracy as much as possible. This proposal effectively improves the accuracy and real-time performance of yolov8 in pavement defect detection applications.

articleTitle: Research on Safety Management and Control of Oil Depots Based on Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In view of the limitations of traditional safety management and control modes in oil depots, such as manual inspections, video surveillance, and automatic alarms, this paper, based on computer vision technology, focuses on designing the framework of an intelligent video analysis platform for oil depot safety management and control. It analyzes the impacts of factors like light changes and small targets in the complex environment of oil depots on target detection, along with corresponding solutions. Additionally, it conducts a comparative analysis of the advantages and disadvantages of three methods for identifying static protective clothing in oil depots. Moreover, a safety helmet detection model for oil depots based on YOLO8 has been constructed. The research findings are bound to support the construction of smart oil depots, promote the actual implementation of the three - tier intelligent safety management and control platform consisting of the general oil company, provincial oil companies, and oil depots, and ensure the intrinsic safety of oil depots.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Natural Language Processing Technology in Combating Cyber Violence
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study addresses the contemporary issue of cyber violence by developing a malicious content filtering algorithm to enhance online environmental health and safety. Leveraging comprehensive natural language processing (NLP) techniques, the research focuses on capturing implicit meanings and contextual associations in harmful speech through a cross-platform, multilingual algorithm design. The proposed system aims to achieve precise identification and effective blocking of toxic content across social media platforms, news comment sections, and forum discussions. By accommodating diverse linguistic and cultural contexts, the solution seeks to significantly reduce the dissemination and societal impact of malicious discourse, ultimately contributing to a more harmonious and equitable digital ecosystem.

articleTitle: Scam Detection for Ethereum Smart Contracts: Leveraging Graph Representation Learning for Secure Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As more and more attacks have been detected on Ethereum smart contracts, it has seriously affected finance and credibility. Current anti-fraud detection techniques, including code parsing or manual feature extraction, still have some shortcomings, although some generalization or adaptability can be obtained. In the face of this situation, this paper proposes to use graphical representation learning technology to find transaction patterns and distinguish malicious transaction contracts, that is, to represent Ethereum transaction data as graphs, and then use advanced ML technology to obtain reliable and accurate results. Taking into account the sample imbalance, we treated with SMOTE-ENN and tested several models, in which MLP performed better than GCN, but the exact effect depends on its field trials. Our research opens up more possibilities for trust and security in the Ethereum ecosystem.

articleTitle: Ecological Effects of Sex Ratio Regulation under Lotka-Volterra and Logestic Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the effects of sex ratio regulation on ecosystems based on Lotka-Volterra and Logestic modeling. First, the Logistic equation is used to describe the population growth under limited resources, and its growth rate decreases as the population approaches the maximum carrying capacity of the environment; the Lotka-Volterra equation is used to characterize the interactions among populations, and the differential equations are used to reflect the dynamics of the number of predators and the number of preys. Secondly, based on the Lotka-Volterra model, the Lotka-Volterra model was further extended to establish a competitive relationship equation to study the effects of competitive factors among species on population size; introduce an additional mortality term to correct the differential equation for species growth; and construct equations for the relationship between sex ratio and population growth rate, external resources, etc., to explore the mechanism of the change of sex ratio. Finally, by integrating these models, we simulated the changes of biomass of each species in ecosystems with different sex ratios, and quantitatively analyzed the stability of ecosystems by using Simpson’s Diversity Index and Alatalo’s Index, so as to reveal the relationship between the regulation of sex ratios and the stability of ecosystems.

articleTitle: An Ontology Based Method for Data Validation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has highlighted a critical imbalance in the acquisition of high-quality training data, which remains a significant bottleneck. Despite breakthroughs in model architectures and algorithms, outdated data engineering practices and the monopolization of premium datasets by major tech companies hinder progress. To address the urgent need for automated, demand-driven data assessment systems that facilitate customizable labeling and semantic-aware filtering of data, we propose an end-to-end data processing method that combines model recognition and knowledge inference, enabling adaptive rules for filtering irrelevant data based on varying requirements. By leveraging techniques such as Faster R-CNN for object detection and integrating ontology reasoning through OWL and SWRL, our method aims to maximize data utility while ensuring accuracy in recognition tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in enhancing data curation processes, ultimately contributing to more reliable AI systems capable of navigating complex real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Two Mapping Strategies for Autonomous Driving Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Many-core architectures hold tremendous potential in autonomous driving accelerators due to their significant energy efficiency advantages. However, effectively utilizing the vast computational resources of such architectures remains a major challenge and an open problem. To address this challenge, we propose two optimization strategies: Gluing Parallel Layers Dataflow (GPLD) and the Ouroboros-like resource allocation strategy. GPLD focuses on optimizing parallel layers, a dimension that has not yet been explored. We design a simple and elegant dataflow to directly glue parallel layers, allowing them to compute as a single layer. This approach reduces energy costs and improves the allocation of chiplet resources. The Ouroboros-like resource allocation strategy is employed to utilize idle resources during segment switching, thereby increasing overall throughput. Overall, these mapping optimizations improve 2.67× performance on average and reduce energy consumption by 50.68% compared to the state-of-the-art Tangram mapping strategy, optimized by us, across a wide range of DNNs.

articleTitle: A research on achieving the RFID anti-collision algorithm using Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper studies the anti-collision algorithm in chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) technology, aiming to improve the accuracy and robustness of multi-tag identification. The chipless RFID tag encodes information through a resonator with a specific geometric structure, and its reading methods are divided into two types: time domain and frequency domain. The frequency domain read uses the resonant peak to distinguish the coded information, but when multiple tags are read at the same time, the signals will collide, causing recognition errors. To solve this problem, a collision-proof algorithm based on compressed sensing (CS) and Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) is proposed.

articleTitle: A System for the Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Hydroacoustic Detection in Complex Ocean Physical Fields
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The present paper sets out a methodology for the scientific evaluation of the systematic utilisation effectiveness of hydroacoustic detection. This methodology is designed to enhance the detection and discovery capability of underwater noncooperative targets. The approach employed is to construct a set of hydroacoustic detection deduction effectiveness evaluation systems based on complex ocean physical fields. The construction of a time-ordered hydroacoustic detection projection system is based on a high-precision and high-reliability ocean acoustic computational model, combined with a sonar detection and discovery model. The effectiveness of hydroacoustic detection is evaluated based on the spatio-temporal cumulative effect of detection effectiveness. The system is capable of accurately deducing and predicting a variety of physical characteristics of hydroacoustic detection, and consequently guiding the joint and efficient deployment of multi-platform equipment for hydroacoustic detection missions in conjunction with the performance evaluation system.

articleTitle: Experimental and Numerical Simulation Study on Fire Detection System for Ship Cable Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The response time of various fire detectors in the ship cable tunnel were studied by the open fire and smoldering experiments. The results show that the alarm sequence of fire detectors was linear temperature sensitive cable, aspirating smoke detector and spot type smoke detector. The FDS numerical simulation software was used to verify the experimental results under the same working conditions. The parameters of each fire detector sensor were set. This study can further improve the selection of fire detectors for ship cable tunnels.

articleTitle: Optimal Cluster Head Selection Algorithm Based on LEACH in WSN
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks, to ensure efficient data collection and transmission, cluster head nodes must adequately cover all sensor nodes. However, the uneven distribution of cluster head nodes will significantly increase the energy consumption of network transmission, thus shortening the overall lifetime of the network. To address this problem, this paper proposes an optimal cluster head selection algorithm based on LEACH cluster routing protocol, OCHSA (Optimal Cluster Head Selection Algorithm based on LEACH in WSN), which aims to optimize the cluster head selection strategy to improve the energy efficiency of the network. selection strategy to improve the energy efficiency of the network and extend the lifetime of the system. In this paper, three key factors, namely coverage, distribution uniformity and residual energy of cluster head nodes, are comprehensively considered in the cluster head selection process to construct a cluster head performance evaluation function, which is used to measure the adaptability of each node as a cluster head. Then, the optimal cluster head set is solved by combining convex optimization to achieve the optimal allocation of cluster heads, reduce the energy consumption of data transmission, and prolong the life cycle of wireless sensor networks. Simulation experimental results show that compared with the traditional methods, this algorithm can effectively improve the network energy efficiency, optimize the rationality of cluster head selection, and has better stability and adaptability.

articleTitle: Multimodal Feature Fusion-Based Airborne-to-Ground Small Target Detection Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the difficulties of small target detection caused by differences in imaging principles between heterogeneous remote sensing images from different sensors, and the discrepancies in air-to-ground scenes, this paper proposes a small target detection method based on multimodal feature fusion for air-to-ground scenarios. The method extracts features from visible light and infrared images, uses a balanced multimodal matrix for feature fusion, and performs target detection using the fused feature map. A detection head specifically designed for small target detection is added to the YOLOv8s target detection network, enhancing the robustness of the detection network. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves the classification accuracy by 4.71% compared to the original YOLOv8s, effectively validating that the fusion of deep and shallow features can enhance the network’s perception ability for small air-to-ground targets.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithms-Based Sustainable Intelligent Transportation System Design
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Blockchain technology is being widely applied in fields such as smart cities, smart transportation, and smart grids. Therefore, this study mainly designs an intelligent transportation system based on blockchain, aiming to reduce the carbon emissions of urban transportation systems and improve the freight efficiency of transportation systems. Specifically, this study designs the urban logistics network based on decentralized architecture and metaheuristic algorithms, aiming to generate a distribution path with the least carbon emissions and shortest time for freight vehicles. Among them, the blockchain layer adopts a consortium chain design, with multi module smart contracts and privacy protection mechanisms to ensure data credibility and network security of intelligent transportation systems. Meta heuristic algorithms are used to dynamically solve multi-objective path planning problems. In addition, we validated the designed system based on several delivery examples and solved the problem using an improved Moss Growth Optimization (MGO) algorithm. The results indicate that blockchain-based intelligent transportation systems can effectively reduce the delivery costs and carbon emissions of transportation networks.

articleTitle: Efficient Resource Utilization through GPU Resource Pooling Management and Control Engine
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low efficiency of GPU resource scheduling in cloud computing, this paper proposes a GPU Resource Pooling Management and Control Engine based on Kubernetes. The traditional GPU scheduling method of subsystem is difficult to coordinate resources, and faces the problem of inefficient utilization of GPU resources caused by the difference of task priorities. In business scenarios such as remote sensing image processing and AI model training, flexible dynamic allocation and release mechanisms of GPU resources are required to improve resource utilization. On the basis of resource virtualization based on MIG technology of Kubernetes and NVIDIA A100 GPU, the engine realizes unified scheduling and efficient utilization of GPU resources through key technologies such as pooling management, resource release strategy and task execution strategy. Compared with the cloud platform without any scheduling platform, the throughput of the cluster is doubled, and the utilization of GPU resources is increased by $\mathbf{2 0 \% \sim 2 8 \%}$. The GPU Resource Pooling Management and Control Engine provides a new idea and method for the efficient management and utilization of GPU resources in cloud environment.

Author Keywords: GPU Resource Pooling Management and Control Engine

articleTitle: Oil well reconstruction from monocular RGB videos
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Reconstructing the oil well from pure images holds significant importance for improving and repairing oil wells. This process can offer valuable insights into the structural integrity of the well, allowing for better assessment and maintenance. The complexity arises from the need to accurately interpret visual data, such as identifying hidden or non-visible structural features and dealing with issues such as noise, low resolution, and distortions in the images. Therefore, we are devoted to offering fresh methods and creating high-quality 3D oil well geometric models from monocular RGB videos. To generate seamless reconstruction, we represent the oil well as the signed distance function field and conduct volume rendering on the signed distance function field to render the image. By minimizing the distance between rendered images and real images, we train the signed distance function field for acquiring the oil well geometric model. However, performing reconstruction purely from images is extremely challenging, and with only image supervision, the reconstructed geometric model is over smooth. To generate the detailed 3D geometry model, we propose to introduce dense point clouds created by multi-view stereo methods to supervise the training of the neural implicit signed distance function field. Our framework’s effectiveness and strength are clearly shown in the experimental results.

articleTitle: Leveraging Attention Mechanisms and Dual-Dimensional Convolution for Enhanced Remote Sensing Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Remote sensing change detection plays a vital role in various applications, including environmental monitoring, urban development, disaster management, and resource optimization. Traditional change detection methods, based on statistical and conventional approaches, face significant challenges in high-resolution remote sensing images. However, deep learning techniques have demonstrated remarkable success in improving the accuracy and efficiency of change detection by capturing complex patterns and subtle changes. Existing deep learning methods, while successful, often lack effective global-local feature understanding and bi-temporal interaction. This paper proposes a novel change detection method that leverages attention mechanisms and dual-dimensional cross convolution for bitemporal feature interactions. Specifically, two ResNet networks are employed: one with edge attention to enhance detailed local features and another with global attention to emphasize abstract, contextual features. This combination strengthens feature representation at different levels, enabling the model to focus on both precise localization and global relationships. Additionally, bitemporal interactions are achieved through dual-dimensional convolution, which improves the understanding of temporal changes across images. The method performance is validated on the real-world CLCD dataset, outperforming existing state-of-theart methods in change detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Risk Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and its morbidity and mortality are at a high level. Accurately predicting the morbidity risk of cardiovascular disease is of great significance for early intervention and prevention. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as angiography, have high diagnostic accuracy, but they are costly and traumatic. The methods based on electrocardiogram or scoring index depend on the experience of professionals and are difficult to be widely promoted. Over the past few years, the extensive use of electronic health record (EHR) data combined with advancements in machine learning has enabled the prediction of cardiovascular disease risk through deep learning algorithms. In this research, we developed a cardiovascular disease risk prediction model utilizing Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and evaluated their comparative performance. Our analysis of EHR data from a major tertiary hospital revealed that the LSTM model achieved the highest precision, recall, and F1 score, with precision at $87.3 \%$, recall at $84.7 \%$, and F1 score at $89.2 \%$. This study offers an effective and accurate machine learning approach for predicting cardiovascular disease risk and provides a theoretical foundation for the development of clinical decision support systems.

articleTitle: Weak target detection algorithm for passive radar based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of the degradation of the detection performance of weak targets in the case of low signal-to-noise ratio, a weak target detection network model is proposed. This model converts one-dimensional radar data into two-dimensional image data and processes the images. A weak target detection network model for passive bistatic radar is put forward. The dataset is made by using the PPI (Plan Position Indicator) diagram. Based on the YOLOv8 basic framework, first of all, an attention mechanism module, namely the EffectiveSEModule, is added, which reduces the computational complexity and information loss while maintaining the performance of the model. Secondly, the neck network is replaced with the HSPAN-DySample network. With the help of a series of mechanisms such as its dynamic sampling, feature fusion, and detail enhancement, it can improve the detection ability for small targets. Then, the WIoU dynamic non-monotonic focusing mechanism is used to focus on anchor boxes of ordinary quality, thus improving the overall performance of the detector. Finally, an auxiliary detection head is added, which can better propagate the gradient, accelerate the training process, and prevent the problem of gradient vanishing. In order to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm, ablation experiments and comparative experiments are carried out. The experimental results show that the improved algorithm significantly reduces the situations of false detections and missed detections. The precision is increased to $90.5 \%$, an increase of $4.7 \%$, and the detection ability for weak targets is enhanced.

articleTitle: Super-ADF: An enhanced algorithm for metal surface defect detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Due to the aging of industrial equipment, safety accidents have become increasingly frequent. The prolonged use of mechanical equipment often leads to corrosion and rust on metal surfaces, resulting in defects and cracks. Therefore, metal surface defect detection plays a crucial role in quality control within the industrial and manufacturing sectors. To address this issue, this paper proposes a metal surface defect detection method based on an improved YOLOv9 model, named Super-ADF. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Super-ADF achieves an mAP of $84.0 \%$ on the NEU-DET dataset, representing an $8.5 \%$ improvement over the baseline YOLOv9 model. The results highlight that the proposed Super-ADF significantly outperforms traditional YOLOv9 in defect detection tasks, particularly in boundary detection and complex background scenarios. This represents a critical breakthrough for addressing metal surface defect detection challenges in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Railway Foreign Object Intrusion Detection Inspired by Star-operation and Coordinate Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Railway construction has advanced, reducing casualties from accidents. However, the number remains high. Identifying and avoiding foreign objects that invade railway safety boundaries is an urgent issue. Omissions and misdetections are common problems. Deep learning-based railway foreign object intrusion detection algorithms can replace manual inspections and traditional methods. These algorithms enable accurate division of intrusion limits and precise detection of foreign objects. However, existing methods face challenges. These include insufficient railway datasets, inaccurate safety limit demarcation, excessive model parameters, long detection times, and issues with missing and false detections. To address these problems, this paper proposes an adaptive improvement to YOLOv8n. The goal is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of railway foreign object detection. Experimental results show the improved model achieves $55.1 \%$ mAP50 on the OSDaR23 dataset. The inference speed reaches 46.2 FPS. The recall rate increases by $3.1 \%$.

articleTitle: PCB Defect Inspection based on YOLOv5-GCBNet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Addressing the issues of missed detections, challenges in feature extraction, and low detection accuracy associated with the traditional YOLOv5 model for Printed Circuit Boards (PCB) defect inspection, this study proposes the YOLOv5-GCBNet model algorithm. Firstly, the C3 module in the backbone network of the YOLOv5s model is replaced with the Global Context Network (GCNet) to more effectively capture the spatial and feature information of defect targets. Secondly, to enhance the detection accuracy for small targets, a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) is integrated into the Neck structure to fully exploit multi-scale feature information and mitigate the issue of feature information loss. Lastly, the use of Distance Intersection over Union (DIoU) Loss as the model’s loss function significantly improves regression accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the traditional YOLOv5 model, the proposed method achieves increases in precision, recall, and mean average precision (mAP) by 2.9%, 1.4%, and 2.6%, respectively.

articleTitle: Automated UI Interface Generation via Diffusion Models: Enhancing Personalization and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study proposes a UI interface generation method based on a diffusion model, aiming to achieve high-quality, diversified, and personalized interface design through generative artificial intelligence technology. The diffusion model is based on its step-by-step denoising generation process. By combining the conditional generation mechanism, design optimization module, and user feedback mechanism, the model can generate a UI interface that meets the requirements based on multimodal inputs such as text descriptions and sketches provided by users. In the study, a complete experimental evaluation framework was designed, and mainstream generation models (such as GAN, VAE, DALL·E, etc.) were selected for comparative experiments. The generation results were quantitatively analyzed from indicators such as PSNR, SSIM, and FID. The results show that the model proposed in this study is superior to other models in terms of generation quality and user satisfaction, especially in terms of logical clarity of information transmission and visual aesthetics. The ablation experiment further verifies the key role of conditional generation and design optimization modules in improving interface quality. This study provides a new technical path for UI design automation and lays the foundation for the intelligent and personalized development of human-computer interaction interfaces. In the future, the application potential of the model in virtual reality, game design, and other fields will be further explored.

articleTitle: Shanghai Port Container Throughput Prediction Based on EEMD-WOA-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Given the important role of container throughput prediction in port management and development, this paper proposes a combined prediction model based on EEMD-WOA-LSTM. The model first uses the Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) technique to decompose monthly container throughput data into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMF) and trend residuals with different characteristics. Then, it utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network optimized by Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) to predict each component. Finally, the predictions of all components are integrated to obtain the final forecast value. Empirical results show that the proposed combined prediction model significantly outperforms traditional models in terms of prediction accuracy and stability, demonstrating good application prospects. This model can provide scientific evidence and decision support for relevant port authorities and shipping enterprises.

articleTitle: LKD-YOLO: Improved YOLOv8 for Rice panicle detection in drone images
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Rice is one of the major staple crops in the world, and accurately and quickly identifying rice panicles is a key step in implementing precision agriculture in the rice sector. The rise of computer vision technology and drone technology has provided effective means for rice panicle detection. However, in drone images, rice panicles occupy a small portion of the image pixels and are densely distributed, often overlapping with each other, and the features differ depending on the height of the capture. These challenges make it difficult for existing object detection models to detect rice panicles effectively. This paper primarily uses YOLOv8 as the baseline model and proposes the LKD-YOLO detection method. LKD-YOLO introduces an additional small target detection layer, which enhances the model's ability to detect small targets. To address issues in the dataset such as multi-height distribution, occlusion, and density, we proposed the LKM module, a feature extraction module that primarily uses multi-scale large kernel convolutions. This module effectively extracts key features of rice panicles. Additionally, we improved the detection head by incorporating an attention mechanism-based target detection head, known as Dyhead. As a result, the final model's detection accuracy, measured by mAP50, improved by $3.6 \%$ compared to the baseline model (YOLOv8s).

Author Keywords: YOLOv8, rice panicle detection, large kernel, small object

articleTitle: Design Method of Timer Based on FreeRTOS Real-Time Embedded Operating System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Given the current situation that various kinds of real-time communication protocols and real-time control systems running on modern industrial control equipment need many types of high-precision timing services, a design method of timer based on FreeRTOS real-time embedded operating system is proposed. Using the deterministic real-time task management mechanism of FreeRTOS real-time embedded operating system, the timing service addition, timer counting, and timing service function operation are managed by special thread tasks, which solves the problem of large cumulative error caused by the deep coupling of the above operations. Based on stm32f407, a test platform is built to test the timer’s timing error and timing delay duration. The experimental results show that the timing error is within 5us, and the timing delay duration is within 30us, which meets the requirements of timing service accuracy in most cases.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Detection of Fraudulent Transactions in E-commerce Using Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, ecommerce platforms are facing an increasing number of fraud threats. Effectively identifying and preventing these fraudulent activities has become a critical research problem. Traditional fraud detection methods typically rely on supervised learning, which requires large amounts of labeled data. However, such data is often difficult to obtain, and the continuous evolution of fraudulent activities further reduces the adaptability and effectiveness of traditional methods. To address this issue, this study proposes an unsupervised e-commerce fraud detection algorithm based on SimCLR. The algorithm leverages the contrastive learning framework to effectively detect fraud by learning the underlying representations of transaction data in an unlabeled setting. Experimental results on the eBay platform dataset show that the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional unsupervised methods such as K-means, Isolation Forest, and Autoencoders in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, demonstrating strong fraud detection capabilities. The results confirm that the SimCLR-based unsupervised fraud detection method has broad application prospects in e-commerce platform security, improving both detection accuracy and robustness. In the future, with the increasing scale and diversity of datasets, the model’s performance will continue to improve, and it could be integrated with real-time monitoring systems to provide more efficient security for e-commerce platforms.

articleTitle: AttYOLO: A model for object detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a fundamental task in computer vision, object detection serves as critical infrastructure for advanced image understanding by providing structured localization and classification data. Addressing the limitation of existing lightweight models in feature representation within complex scenarios, this study proposes an enhanced architecture based on YOLOv7-tiny. The integration of Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) modules establishes cross-channel interaction mechanisms, which significantly improves discriminative feature capture while preserving real-time inference capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate a $1.1 \%$ absolute improvement in mAP metrics on coco dataset, offering a novel technical solution for high-precision real-time detection on embedded systems.

articleTitle: Research on Emergency Communication Network Link Planning Based on Knowledge Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of emergency communication network link planning, and proposes a knowledgebased emergency communication network link planning strategy to address the shortcomings of traditional planning methods that rely on manual experience, cannot fully explore data information, and are difficult to achieve global optimality. Our strategy introduces the knowledge graph completion method, which transforms the network link planning problem into a knowledge graph completion task. Taking emergency communication support requirements as the logical starting point, it uses vertical domain knowledge graphs for knowledge reasoning and then plans communication network links. Performance analysis shows that our strategy achieves a human-machine collaborative planning mode, reduces the cognitive burden of network planners, and provides new ideas and methods for emergency communication network link planning.

articleTitle: A Data Augmentation Method for Financial Datasets Using Diffusion Models with Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, financial institutions have faced challenges in risk assessment and intelligent decision-making due to data scarcity and privacy concerns. To address this issue, we propose a novel data augmentation method based on Diffusion Models enhanced with a self-attention mechanism for financial datasets. Our approach introduces self-attention into the reverse denoising process of diffusion models to effectively capture the global dependencies among financial variables, thereby significantly improving the quality of synthesized financial data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed diffusion model outperforms traditional generative adversarial networks (GANs) in terms of fidelity and distribution alignment, achieving higher data quality and consistency. Additionally, comprehensive ablation studies validate the effectiveness of integrating selfattention mechanisms into diffusion models. This research highlights the potential of diffusion-based data augmentation in addressing data scarcity and privacy issues in the financial domain.

articleTitle: Optimal Ratio Mask-Driven Time-Frequency Neural Architecture for Acoustic Echo Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Acoustic echo cancellation is a crucial technology for enhancing speech clarity and user experience. This paper proposes a bidirectional long short-term memory (BLSTM)-based neural architecture that combines time-domain convolutional feature extraction with frequency-domain long-term dependency modeling. It also proposes an optimal ratio masking method specifically designed for acoustic echo cancellation, overcoming the signal assumption constraints of existing masking approaches to precisely define near-end estimated speech output. Furthermore, the proposed framework integrates the feature learning capabilities of deep neural networks with the adaptive filtering characteristics of a frequency-domain state-block partitioned linear algorithm, establishing a collaborative cancellation mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enhances both echo cancellation performance and near-end speech quality, exhibiting superior effectiveness in acoustic echo cancellation.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of acoustic imaging fusion localization algorithm based on microphone array
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Fault location in power cables has always been a difficult problem in power system operation. Therefore, the acoustic imaging fusion location system based on microphone array can be designed to locate power cable faults. The microphone array is used to collect the sound data of the inspected power cable. Then the algorithm is used to process the collected data to obtain information such as the azimuth and pitch angle of the sound source point relative to the reference point. Finally the sound field cloud map is generated based on the localization position and the amplitude information of the sound. The structure and algorithm of microphone array are the key of the system. This paper intends to complete the design and implementation of the microphone array-based acoustic imaging fusion localization algorithm through theoretical research and simulation.

articleTitle: Collision Avoidance for Radio Frequency Identification Tags: Simulation and Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Tag collisions are a common and significant obstacle in radio frequency identification (RFID) systems, directly affecting the identification efficiency and system throughput. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dynamic frame slotted RFID collision avoidance algorithm based on multiple frequencies. The proposed algorithm organizes tags into groups, limits the number of tags responding within each group, and dynamically adjusts the frame length to optimize management within the group. By efficiently allocating tags with different frequencies within the group, the proposed algorithm effectively reduces collision slots and increases system throughput per unit of time. Simulation and practical test results demonstrate that, compared to traditional RFID collision avoidance algorithms, the proposed algorithm shows significant advantages in improving throughput and reducing the number of collisions. It can be applied to practical RFID systems in high-density tag scenarios.

articleTitle: Residual Attention-Enhanced Bitemporal Change Detection with Pseudo-Change Suppression
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the increasing resolution of remote sensing images, surface change detection has become more detailed yet more challenging due to pseudo-changes caused by seasonal variations and imaging conditions. Traditional change detection methods, including pixel-level and object-level approaches, often assume highly similar image data, limiting their effectiveness in complex environments. While deep learning techniques have enhanced detection accuracy, convolutional neural network (CNN)-based models still suffer from vanishing gradients and high computational costs, hindering large-scale applicability. To address these issues, we propose a bitemporal change detection method that integrates residual attention mechanisms with differential operations to suppress pseudo-changes and enhance feature extraction. The model employs channel attention to assign adaptive weights to spectral features and utilizes residual connections to strengthen temporal feature representation. Furthermore, differential operations generate fine-grained difference maps, effectively distinguishing real changes from pseudo-changes. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves detection robustness and precision, offering a more reliable solution for high-resolution remote sensing change detection.

articleTitle: A high-order compensated bandgap reference design with a buffer circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issue of low power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) in traditional bandgap reference circuits, a novel bandgap reference scheme is proposed. This scheme employs a five-transistor unit and an emitter follower to form a two-stage operational amplifier, isolating the reference voltage from other modules and thereby ensuring the gain of the reference generation circuit. Additionally, a high-order compensation circuit is introduced to reduce temperature drift and enhance precision. Based on a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ BCD process and validated through Cadence simulations, the results demonstrate a temperature drift of $\mathbf{T}_{\text {dit, REF1 }}$ $=20 \mathrm{ppm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and a power supply rejection ratio of -113 dB over a temperature range of $-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. This circuit is capable of generating high-precision reference voltages and bias currents.

articleTitle: CHP-YOLO: An Optimized Deep Learning Methods for Safety Protection Equipment Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the working environment of grain depots, ensuring that personnel safety protection equipment wearing correctly is crucial for safe production. Aiming at the problem of granary personnel wearing detection, this paper uses web crawlers and autonomous photography to construct a SPE (Safety Protection Equipment Detection) dataset. By replacing the YOLOv8 backbone C2f with the C2f_CCNeck module based on CondConv(Conditional Parameterized Convolution), the new YOLO network is lightweight. Then, the improved H-CBAM attention mechanism, and the pruning technology of BatchNormal are integrated. The improved lightweight YOLO detection method CHP-YOLO is proposed. Through ablation experiments, the improved CHP-YOLO shows relatively excellent detection performance. This method effectively improves the accuracy and robustness of Safety Protection Equipment Detection.

articleTitle: Textual Knowledge Fusion Reasoning Detector for Remote Sensing Few-Shot Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Due to the difficulty and time consumption of object-level annotations, remote sensing few-shot object detection has recently become a popular research topic. However, remote sensing objects exhibit significant variations in orientation and size, resulting in the misclassification of novel classes. Except for annotation samples, the text information between novel and base classes remains constant. Thus, in this paper, we explore how to leverage text information to resolve class confusion. Specifically, we propose a textual knowledge extractor and a cross-modal attention fusion module. The former is designed to extract textual knowledge for each class, while the latter aims to fuse it with visual knowledge. Experiments on the DIOR dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A Fast Algorithm for Foil Recognition and Positioning Based on Monocular Stereo Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Foil is a passive jamming device composed of metal foil, metal wire or metal-coated medium. Due to its low cost, convenient use and wide frequency band, it has been widely applied in modern military fields such as radar jamming, missile penetration and electronic warfare. However, as the foil is thin and overlaps with each other during the transmission on the conveyor belt, some edges are occluded, thereby interfering with the recognition effect. Therefore, the recognition and positioning of foil in a dynamic environment by machine vision confronts significant challenges. The rapid and accurate recognition and positioning of foil is a key technology to ensure the precise grasping of the robotic manipulator. Although traditional methods such as manual, mechanical and sensor positioning have their respective advantages, they have limitations in aspects such as recognition accuracy, reliability and environmental adaptability. To address the issue of the robotic manipulator’s rapid and accurate grasping of foil during its transmission on the conveyor belt, this paper compares three object detection algorithms: Faster R-CNN, SSD and YOLOv8s.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Jamming Suppression Using Regularized Eigenvalue Oblique Projection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of radar system application scenarios and the increasing complexity of the electromagnetic environment, traditional spatial anti-jamming methods often struggle to counter mainlobe interference effectively. Classical approaches such as Minimum Variance Distortionless Response, power inversion, and subspace projection demonstrate good performance in suppressing sidelobe and even backlobe interference. However, when interference and target signals are highly overlapped or closely spaced in angle, these algorithms typically exhibit significant gain attenuation near the target direction due to the formation of nulls, making it difficult to detect the target signal effectively. To address these issues, this chapter introduces a mainlobe interference suppression algorithm based on Regularized Eigenvalue Oblique Projection. By incorporating sidelobe constraint conditions, this algorithm can effectively suppress mainlobe interference while better preserving the desired signal and minimizing the impact on sidelobe interference suppression performance.

articleTitle: Smart Contract Reentry Vulnerability Detection Based on Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: A federated learning based smart contract reentry vulnerability detection method is proposed to address the issues of multiple data sources and data privacy in existing smart contract reentry vulnerability detection methods, in order to address the privacy and distributed storage issues of smart contract code data.
