By integrating horizontal federated learning and deep learning methods, model parameters are shared among various participants without sharing raw data, achieving protection of data privacy and security. At the same time, model training is allowed on different datasets, thereby more comprehensively discovering smart contract re-entry vulnerabilities. In the detection of re-entry vulnerabilities in smart contracts, by updating model parameters locally and aggregating parameters on a central server, it is possible to effectively detect re-entry vulnerabilities in smart contracts while protecting the privacy and security of contract data. The final experiment shows that the proposed method can protect privacy while still ensuring high model accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Semantic Segmentation for Autonomous Driving with Model Stacking and Patch-Based Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is crucial for autonomous driving because it enables vehicles to accurately understand and interpret their surroundings, which is essential for making safe and informed driving decisions. In this paper, we propose two effective strategies to improve the performance of semantic segmentation: model stacking and patch-based data augmentation. Specifically, we stack the predictions of U-Net, U-Net++, and DeepLabV3 and use them as inputs to meta models, aiming to utilize the complementary strengths of these individual models for better prediction. In addition, to address the challenge of detecting small objects, we slice the dataset into smaller segments and apply randomized data augmentation techniques to each segment independently. This approach not only increases the diversity of the training data, but also helps the model to better recognize and predict small objects. We conducted comprehensive experiments on the CamVid dataset and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model stacking and patch-based data augmentation methods.

articleTitle: Indoor Positioning Algorithm Based on Bluetooth and Pedometer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to achieve the function of personnel position supervision and recording in large indoor spaces through sensor signals, this paper proposed a fusion indoor localization method based on Bluetooth and pedometer. The current fingerprint data and pedometer data were got and the algorithm parameters were initialized. Initial prediction of positioning coordinate was finished by estimation of the pedometer scale and direction for the calculation of the variance value of the fingerprint positioning. The Kalman gain was calculated with the Kalman filter to correct the $d_{x}$ and $d_{y}$ directions. According to $d_{x}$ and $d_{y}$, the prediction data of the positioning coordinate was adjusted as the final positioning coordinate data to complete the indoor positioning. This algorithm integrates Bluetooth’s fingerprint data with pedometer’s inertial navigation data. Testing has shown that the positioning trajectory is smooth, with no jumping or deviation, achieving precise positioning effectively.

articleTitle: Differentiable Neural Architecture Search Based on Hybrid Attention for Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of deep learning has highlighted the growing challenge of high computational costs in traditional neural architecture design. This has spurred significant research interest in efficient automated neural architecture search methods, particularly the gradientbased Differentiable Architecture Search (DARTS) known for its computational efficiency. This paper presents a novel hybrid attention-enhanced differentiable neural architecture search method by integrating channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms. The proposed approach not only improves classification accuracy but also significantly reduces computational resource requirements. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves architecture search within 0.28 GPU-days while attaining error rates of $\mathbf{2. 5 0 \%}$ and $\mathbf{1 7. 4 1 \%}$ on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets respectively, outperforming both traditional neural architecture search methods and the baseline DARTS model.

articleTitle: Monitoring and evaluation of air quality in Jinan based on machine learning random forest model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The present study focuses on the monitoring and evaluation of air quality in Jinan, and utilises the random forest algorithm to construct a prediction model. Employing data from the China Air Quality Online monitoring and analysis platform from 1 January 2021 to 11 January 2025, the performance of the model was evaluated through data pre-processing, model construction and parameter optimisation. The findings demonstrate that the random forest model effectively captures the evolving trend of the air quality index in Jinan, thereby providing a scientific foundation for urban air quality monitoring and management.

articleTitle: A Broadband Sleeve Dynamic Seawater Monopole Antenna for Marine Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to enhance the bandwidth of dynamic seawater monopole antennas by incorporating a metal sleeve. Based on the theory of sleeve antennas, this study analyzes the operational principles of dynamic sleeve seawater monopole antennas. Electromagnetic simulations conducted using FEKO software demonstrate that the addition of a sleeve can increase the antenna’s impedance bandwidth from $75 \%$ to $93 \%$. Experimental validation was performed in a saltwater pool setup, where network analyzer measurements confirmed the improvement in bandwidth due to the sleeve. The wideband sleeve dynamic seawater monopole antenna holds potential for future marine wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Similarity-guided Model-selection of Adversarial attack Methods Based on Transferability
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Black-box attacks based on adversarial instance transferability have become a research hotspot. This method uses known white box models (alternative models) to create adversarial examples that pose a threat to other unknown black box models. However, current black box attack methods based on transferability face many challenges, such as high query counts and difficulty balancing transferability and attack success rates. To address these challenges, this article introduces a similarity guided model selection adversarial attack method (SMAT) based on transferability. It combines transfer-based techniques with score-based attacks to analyze the similarity between the target model and candidate alternative models, and selects the model that is closer to the target model on the decision boundary from the candidate alternative model set as the alternative model.. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet have shown that LBAT reduces queries while maintaining transferability and success. This study enhances the theoretical framework of black box attacks, which contributes to the robustness evaluation of DNNs and advances adversarial machine learning.

articleTitle: Research on Mixed-Precision Quantization Optimization Method for Neural Networks Based on Quantization Sensitivity and Hardware Constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In mixed-precision quantization of neural network models, determining the quantization bit-width for each layer is a critical challenge. This paper proposes an optimization method that comprehensively considers quantization sensitivity and hardware constraints. By establishing quantitative relationships between quantization bit-width and hardware resources (computational overhead and bandwidth requirements), the problem is transformed into an optimization problem and solved using a hierarchical greedy algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces quantization-induced accuracy loss while satisfying hardware resource constraints.

articleTitle: Approaches to Address Occlusion and Small Target Challenges in Restaurant Rat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In this study, an improved target detection algorithm is proposed for the problem of rat detection in restaurant environments. The restaurant environment is characterized by obvious light changes, complex occlusion, and ground reflections, which bring more challenges to the accurate detection of rats. For this reason, we make the following improvements to the YOLOv5 algorithm. First, we introduce the Glare Suppression Module, which utilizes an adaptive feature correction method to reduce the interference of highly reflective areas such as oil and water stains on the ground on the detection model, and to improve the recognition ability of the rat target in low-contrast scenes. Secondly, combined with the Background Adaptive Modeling (BAM) technology, the stability and generalization ability of the model is improved by dynamically learning the background features of the restaurant environment to reduce the false detections caused by the activities of the restaurant personnel, changes in the tables and chairs, and other factors. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5 algorithm can effectively improve the precision and recall rate of rat detection, reduce the false detection rate, and ensure the real-time performance in the restaurant environment, which provides efficient and reliable technical support for restaurant hygiene monitoring and pest rat prevention and control.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Malware Family Labeling: A Multi-Engine-Tag Discrepancy-Aware Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Malware detection and classification predominantly rely on machine learning models, which necessitate the provision of authoritative family labels in the annotated data used for model training. Within the scope of extant research methodologies, the formulation of such authoritative family labels is customarily derived from virus labels furnished by a plurality of antivirus engines, procured through a crowdsourcing methodology. A pivotal challenge that necessitates resolution in this context pertains to the incongruity in virus nomenclature across diverse engines. Prevailing strategies frequently resort to a majority voting mechanism to mitigate this discrepancy, yet they fail to account for the interdependencies and reference relationships that exist among the engines. This manuscript introduces a Multi-Engine-Tag Discrepancy-Aware Framework (MET-DAF), designed to facilitate the construction of malware family labels while addressing the inherent biases present in multi-engine labeling systems. The framework initially delineates the reference relationships between antivirus engines by analyzing label co-occurrence patterns. Following this, engines implicated in reference relationships are systematically excluded, and a crowdsourcing strategy is employed to establish authoritative family labels. The robustness and efficacy of our proposed framework have been rigorously assessed and corroborated across a triad of datasets: the publicly accessible Malheur and MalGenome datasets, as well as a proprietary dataset, CollectData, comprising authentic network traffic data amassed by our research collective.

articleTitle: LSTM-based Price Prediction and Dynamic Risk Management in Decentralized Blockchain Protocol
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study investigates Bitcoin price prediction and dynamic risk management strategies within decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network models. The research demonstrates that the LSTM model effectively captures Bitcoin’s general price trends and short-term fluctuations under typical market conditions. However, during periods of extreme volatility, the prediction model exhibits notable lag and reduced amplitude in capturing abrupt price changes, highlighting its limitations when relying solely on historical price data. Furthermore, this paper proposes a dynamic collateral ratio adjustment mechanism based on predicted price deviations, aimed at mitigating liquidation risks in DeFi lending protocols. Dynamically adjusting collateral ratios has the potential to substantially improve protocol stability compared to traditional static collateral frameworks.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Text Summarization Using Transformer and Pointer-Generator Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Due to the explosive growth of digital content, automated text summary generation has become a critical task for digesting large amounts of information efficiently. In this work, we propose a new method of automatic text summarization based on the combination of Transformer and Pointer-Generator network. The model learns with the existing architecture, leverages the strong context modeling ability of Transformer to capture long-distance dependency, and brings in pointer mechanism in Pointer-Generator network to deal with non-lexical words effectively and enhance the abstraction of summary generation. Firstly, we come up with a multi-layer hybrid framework which integrates the attention mechanism of Transformer with the overlay mechanism of Pointer-Generator to produce a more precise and fluent summaries. This weighted combination can then be refined by implementing a fine-tuning stage that updates the weights of the two networks conditional to the attributes of the input data. Experimental results demonstrate that on the standard dataset, our model outperforms the current best summary generation models with respect to ROUGE score.

articleTitle: Smart City Logistics: Leveraging AI for Last-Mile Delivery Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Urban environments face significant challenges in last-mile delivery, which is a crucial component of logistics. To address these challenges, we introduce a framework called Smart City Logistics, utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance delivery efficiency. The framework optimizes routing and improves resource allocation by analyzing real-time data from multiple sources, including traffic patterns and user preferences. The system employs machine learning algorithms for predictive analytics, enabling it to adjust in response to evolving demand. Furthermore, we investigate the integration of AI with advanced infrastructure, such as smart traffic signals and autonomous delivery drones, fostering a more agile delivery network. Case studies across various cities reveal substantial improvements in both delivery speed and operational costs, showcasing AI’s transformative impact on logistics and its potential for sustainable urban delivery solutions.

articleTitle: Design of a Single-Shot Signal Amplifier based on Prefetching Instruction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Microarchitectural attacks increasingly exploit performance-enhancing components such as branch predictors, caches, and hardware prefetchers. This paper introduces a single-shot signal amplification method based on PRFM prefetch instructions, enabling active cache state manipulation to enhance side-channel attacks. Our method significantly improves signal-to-noise ratio, reduces reliance on high-precision timers, and effectively amplifies microarchitectural leakage in constrained environments. Experimental results on Raspberry Pi 4B demonstrate a $6.1 \times$ amplification factor and 95% cache state detection accuracy, even under low-precision timer conditions. Compared to conventional methods, our approach reduces the number of required attack samples while maintaining high reliability. This research provides new insights into efficient cache-side channel exploitation and defense strategies.

articleTitle: Research and Practice of Dam Safety Management Platform Based on Internet of Things and Twin Simulation Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of information silos and insufficient dynamic simulation capabilities in traditional dam safety monitoring, a dam safety monitoring and management method based on the Internet of Things and twin simulation technology is proposed. By constructing an “air - space - ground hydraulic - engineering” integrated IoT information perception system, real - time collection of all - element data of the dam is achieved. Based on the digital twin technology, a dam twin model is constructed, and technical difficulties such as massive terrain scheduling, dam - terrain mosaic, and the expression of safety information in 3D space are studied. A dam safety management platform is designed. Using the digital twin framework of geographic information to construct a real - coordinate space reference, combined with multi - source data fusion and real - time simulation, rapid, efficient, and intuitive twin simulation of dam safety information is realized. This provides managers with a means to quickly obtain the safety status of the dam, improves the level of dam safety management, and provides support for the intelligent management of river basins.

articleTitle: From Text to Impact: A Deep Multimodal Approach for Predicting and Explaining Scholarly Influence Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The dynamics of scholarly influence are shaped by both semantic innovations in text content and structural patterns in citation networks. However, existing literature metrology methods often analyze these modalities in isolation, neglecting their temporal interplay and failing to explain prediction rationales. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a deep multimodal framework for predicting and explaining scholarly influence dynamics through joint modeling of text semantics and citation networks. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) a Temporal Graph Attention Network (TGAT) that captures evolving citation relationships and knowledge diffusion paths, (2) a BERT-Heterogeneous Graph Transformer (HGT) hybrid architecture that aligns semantic embeddings with topological node representations via cross-modal attention, and (3) a SHAP-based attribution mechanism that quantifies the marginal contribution of textual claims, citation contexts, and structural positions to influence propagation. Evaluated on a large-scale academic graph dataset spanning 500,000 computer science papers (2010–2023), the model achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting future high-impact works (F1-score: 0.79) while revealing actionable insights: temporal citation bursts are found to amplify semantic novelty by 37%, and cross-disciplinary references contribute $2.4 \times$ higher influence than intra-disciplinary ones.

articleTitle: A novel adaptive beamforming method based on the adjacent point difference matching
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The performance of adaptive beamforming method is influenced by the low signal-to-noise ratio and short sampling points condition. In this paper, a robust adaptive beamforming method based on the adjacent point difference matching is proposed. Using the desired signal characteristics is not a mutation at the adjacent point, as well the correlation between the signals of the adjacent sampling points should be the biggest feature. The adjacent point difference signal matching power is obtained to find the diagonal loading factor corresponding to the maximum power, and determine the weight vector of the beam, which is the purpose of extracting the desired target signal, inhibiting the interference and noise. This method requires no user parameters, it owns strong robustness and high estimation accuracy. Finally, the simulation results which are based on the uniform linear array show that the method is able to effectively obtain the desired target signal and restrain the interference signal, and still have wonderful beamformation performance.

articleTitle: Decentralized Dynamic Task Allocation Algorithm Based on a Bidding Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the multi-UAV cooperative task planning problem, this paper proposes a decentralized dynamic task allocation method based on a bidding mechanism. In this method, each UAV autonomously decides task selection through a bidding strategy and dynamically adjusts its allocation plan during execution to adapt to complex and dynamic task environments. A mathematical model for UAV task allocation is established, considering UAV states, task rewards, and execution costs. A bidding-based task allocation algorithm is designed to maximize overall utility. This approach introduces a task reward-cost tradeoff mechanism to enhance task completion rates while reducing unnecessary resource consumption. Additionally, a task-locking strategy is proposed to ensure allocation stability and minimize efficiency losses caused by frequent task switching. Simulation experiments validate that the proposed method outperforms traditional task allocation algorithms in terms of task completion rate, computational overhead, and global utility, effectively improving the task coordination capability of multi-UAV systems in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Trends and Developments in Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis: A Bibliometric Study Using CiteSpace and the Web of Science Database (2010-2025)
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and natural language processing (NLP), aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) has emerged as a crucial subfield of fine-grained sentiment analysis, widely applied in e-commerce, public opinion monitoring, and intelligent customer service. This study employs bibliometric analysis to systematically examine research trends in ABSA from 2010 to 2025, utilizing data retrieved from the Web of Science core collection and analyzed through CiteSpace. The findings reveal a significant increase in ABSA research since 2019, with deep learning models such as BiLSTM, CRF, and attention mechanisms driving major breakthroughs. Additionally, the study identifies leading countries, institutions, and influential authors in this field, highlighting the shift from traditional sentiment lexicons and machine learning approaches to deep learning-based methodologies. The insights presented in this paper contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the ABSA research landscape, offering valuable references for future academic and industrial applications.

articleTitle: A Method for Shape Correction of Towed Array Based on Attitude Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the field of underwater acoustic detection, tow line array is widely used, but its formation is easily distorted by water flow, vehicle movement and other factors, which seriously affects the detection performance. In this paper, an attitude sensor based flare-up correction method is proposed. The attitude sensor can obtain the characteristics of heading Angle and pitch Angle in real time. The parabola model in three-dimensional space is established. According to the actual attitude data of each element in the towed line array, the corresponding formation model is established to optimize and solve, so as to realize the accurate correction of the towed line burst. The experimental results show that this method can effectively improve the accuracy of the flareup of the towed line, significantly enhance the detection performance of the towed line array, and provide a new effective way for the correction of the flare-up of the towed line, and has broad application prospects in the fields of underwater acoustic detection and Marine safety monitoring.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Secure Communication in Coupled Phase-Shift STAR-RIS Aided MU-MISO Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper explores the energy-efficient secure communication design enabled by simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS). In particular, we consider a coupled phase-shift STAR-RIS aided downlink network within a multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system, where eavesdroppers are present. To optimize the system’s secrecy energy efficiency (SEE), we jointly design the secure beamforming and STAR-RIS coefficients. An alternating optimization (AO) framework is proposed to tackle the non-convexity of the problem. Specifically, the beamforming is configured via the successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm, while closed-form solutions for the coupled STAR-RIS coefficients are derived using the penalty dual decomposition (PDD) framework. Numerical results validate the algorithm’s effectiveness in enhancing both energy efficiency and security, and reveal the trade-off between hardware feasibility and performance.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Particle Filter Technique for Nonlinear System State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive particle filter (APF) method to enhance the accuracy of indoor positioning and state estimation in nonlinear systems. Traditional particle filter methods are often hindered by issues such as particle degradation and impoverishment, which compromise the accuracy of state estimation, particularly in complex and nonlinear environments. To address these challenges, the proposed method dynamically adjusts the particle weights based on their distribution, ensuring a more balanced representation of the system’s state distribution and preventing the collapse of particle diversity. Experimental results validate the robustness and enhanced accuracy of the adaptive approach, with the mean absolute error (MAE) reduced to approximately $7-8 \mathrm{~cm}$, demonstrating the method’s effectiveness in achieving high-precision indoor positioning. This research provides a promising solution for accurate state estimation in nonlinear systems and contributes to the advancement of particle filtering techniques for complex practical applications.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Modeling Algorithm for Endangered Species Population Dynamics based on Dynamic Parameter Optimization and Bayesian Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the fixed parameter assumption of the classical logistic model is difficult to portray the superlinear death effect and Allee effect, this paper proposes a population modeling algorithm that integrates dynamic parameter optimization and Bayesian learning. By constructing a time-varying parameter space, we establish the dual feedback correction equations of environmental capacity and growth rate, and design an adaptive sliding window mechanism to dynamically optimize the parameter sensitivity. The algorithm combines the improved Bayesian optimization module and introduces dynamic exploration factors to balance the global search and local convergence efficiency. Experiments using the Danding Crane population as an example show that the dynamic model shortens the response time lag by 53%, improves the recovery efficiency of manual intervention by 40%, and reduces the prediction error by 42% compared with the traditional method under sudden environmental changes. The framework provides a highly adaptive modeling tool for endangered species conservation, which can be extended to the dynamic management of complex ecosystems.

articleTitle: Autoregressive Model-Based Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Main Lobe Jamming Suppression in Phased Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel blind extraction method based on autoregressive (AR) model and particle swarm optimization (PSO). By constructing an AR model of the transmitted signal and optimizing the extraction vector via PSO, the algorithm achieves effective suppression of main lobe jamming without prior knowledge of jamming characteristics. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms classical blind separation techniques (e.g., JADE and FastICA) in terms of signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) improvement and computational efficiency, particularly in low-SNR scenarios.

articleTitle: An Efficient UAV-Based Data Collection Scheme for Energy-Harvesting Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Addressing the data collection challenges in energy-harvesting Internet of Things (IoT), this paper proposes an efficient data collection scheme utilizing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). In this scheme, the UAV serves as a mobile data fusion center, where sensors transmit their observations through coherent multiple access channels. Considering the energy status of each sensor, the problem is formulated as a convex optimization model. A neural network is introduced to predict the number of time slots required for collecting data from varying numbers of sensors. Additionally, a grouping strategy is employed, utilizing the mutual coherence value in the measurement matrix to determine whether grouped data collection is necessary, thereby reducing the scale of the convex problem in large-scale sensor networks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively alleviates the difficulties in solving convex optimization problems, significantly improving reconstruction accuracy and reducing algorithmic time complexity under the same number of time slots.

articleTitle: Evaluation Model Construction of Intercultural Adaptability of Chinese-Foreign Joint Education Students Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid expansion of the scale of Sino-foreign cooperation in running schools, the assessment of students' cross-cultural adaptability has become an important link to ensure the quality of education. Traditional evaluation methods rely on fixed weight system and cross-sectional data analysis, which are difficult to capture the dynamic and nonlinear characteristics of acculturation process, resulting in delayed interventions and inaccurate policy implementation. In this study, we propose a dynamic evaluation model based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. By constructing a four-dimensional index system covering psychological adaptation, social adaptation, academic adaptation, and environmental adaptation, and combining with grade perception embedding and temporal attention mechanism, the model can realize the adaptive evolution of index weights. The experimental results show that the model achieves a weighted accuracy of $87.3 \%$ in the data of 1,042 students in four school years, which is $9.6 \%$ higher than static model. Its early warning mechanism can identify academic crisis 2.3 semesters in advance, which provides strong support for the quality assurance of education.

articleTitle: Signal Enhancement Method of Adaptive Filtering Algorithm in Microelectronic Sensor Array
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study optimizes signal processing in microelectronic sensor arrays through adaptive filtering algorithm, improves signal quality and signal-to-noise ratio, and suppresses noise interference. The study aims to solve the problem of effective enhancement of multi-channel sensor signals and provide technical support for high-precision data acquisition and analysis. This paper introduces a sub-band-based DFRCT (Discrete Fractional Cosine Transform)-LMS (Least Mean Squares) algorithm, which uses DFRCT to decompose the collected multi-channel signal in the frequency domain, divides the signal into multiple sub-bands, and performs independent noise suppression and enhancement processing on each sub-band signal. Then, the filter coefficients are dynamically adjusted through the LMS algorithm to minimize the error between the output signal and the expected signal, thereby improving the signal quality. Experimental results show that the signal processed by the proposed algorithm has significant improvements in SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) and MSE (Mean Squared Error) compared with traditional Kalman filtering and Wiener filtering algorithms. When the signal sequence length is 10s, the SNR of the DFRCT-LMS algorithm is 30.5 dB and the MSE is 0.08, which is significantly better than Kalman filtering (SNR is 24.8 dB, MSE is 0.23) and Wiener filtering (SNR is 27.1 dB, MSE is 0.15).

articleTitle: Vision-Based Robotic Grasping Method for Nest Frame Based on Gen6D and AnyGrasp
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Beekeeping plays a significant role in agricultural production, while the traditional farming method makes beekeepers not only have heavy physical labor, but also easy to be attacked by bees. Nest frame grasping is the core task of honey harvesting robots, for which a vision-based robotic grasping method combining Gen6D with AnyGrasp is proposed. After that, an evaluation and decision system based on the nest frame mechanics model is added to select the most suitable grasping pose. Finally, vision program tests and grasping experimental based on a mobile base 6-DOF manipulator are carried out. The method succeeds in 35 gripping experiments under 4 different working conditions, with acceptable response time, specifically, 10.632 s on average. The study contributes to the application of honey harvesting robots, saving response time and improving grasping accuracy significantly.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Multimodal Learning for Tumor Classification in Chest Radiography
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Chest radiography plays a crucial role in the early detection and classification of tumors, yet the reliance on labeled data poses significant challenges in medical imaging. To address this, we introduce a Self-Supervised Multimodal Learning for Tumor Classification(SML-TC) framework that effectively combines visual and textual modalities. This approach harnesses both radiographic images and their corresponding reports, allowing the model to develop rich feature representations w/o extensive labeled datasets. By employing self-supervised learning, our method enhances diagnostic performance while overcoming the limitations posed by sparse annotations. Specifically, our framework learns meaningful representations and incorporates data augmentation, even with a limited amount of annotated data, allowing the model to better capture distinctive identifying features for tumor classification. Comprehensive experiments conducted on various chest radiographs reveal that our approach substantially exceeds the performance of conventional supervised learning methods. Additionally, the results demonstrate heightened accuracy in tumor detection and classification, emphasizing the potential impact of our model in clinical practice and its capability to assist radiologists with informed, data-driven interpretations.

articleTitle: AI Agent Implementation in Hall for Workshop of Metasynthetic Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Based on the hall for workshop of metasynthetic engineering theory as proposed by Qian Xuesen and AI agent technological approaches, we proposed an AI agent-driven collaborative system design, with a focus on the design of modules such as knowledge base, task decomposition, and tool integration. To address the deficiency of dynamic adjustment capabilities in existing systems, this paper proposes to integrate chain of thought and critical path algorithms to decompose research tasks, and solve problems caused by long execution chains. The system design incorporates essential characteristics of metasynthetic engineering, demonstrating strong domain adaptability in complex decisionmaking scenarios while establishing an extensible technical paradigm for intelligent research enhancement.

articleTitle: Speech Feature-Based Depression Detection and Interpretability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Depression is a common mental disorder whose clinical diagnosis currently relies primarily on subjective scales and physician assessments, lacking objective and rapid detection methods. This paper proposes a depression detection method based on speech signal analysis. First, speech data from participants are collected, from which multiple acoustic featuressuch as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), fundamental frequency, energy, and formants-are extracted. Next, the XGBoost algorithm is employed to construct a depression classification model, and the model’s performance is evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is utilized to interpret the model’s predictions, revealing the importance of individual acoustic features in the decision-making process. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves strong performance across various metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and Area Under the Curve (AUC). Furthermore, the SHAP analysis highlights that certain speech features significantly contribute to distinguishing depression. This study offers a novel approach and provides insights for early screening and intelligent diagnosis of depression using speech signals.

articleTitle: A lightweight small-object detection algorithm for remote sensing images based on 4SDC-YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the field of object detection, remote sensing image detection has become a critical research focus. However, existing small-object detection algorithms for remote sensing images often fail to strike an effective balance between detection accuracy and computational complexity, thereby limiting their application on mobile devices. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight small-object detection algorithm for remote sensing images, named 4SDC-YOLOv8, built upon YOLOv8. Firstly, we incorporate the SimSPPF spatial pyramid pooling structure, using pooling kernels of different sizes across multiple scales to improve the detector’s performance. Secondly, we design a lightweight neck network that leverages the dynamic upsampling operator DySample and the partial convolution Partial Conv to introduce the new CSPPC architecture, reducing redundant computations and enhancing both real-time performance and model compactness. Finally, we add a dedicated small-object detection layer, enabling the feature map to capture rich semantic and spatial information, with four detection heads supporting multi-scale small-object detection and improving detection capability for small targets. Experimental results on the DIOR dataset show that, compared with YOLOv8, 4SDC-YOLOv8 significantly reduces model size and computational load by 24.6% and 24%, respectively, achieves an accuracy of up to 90%, and maintains a respectable real-time performance at 145 FPS. Confirm that 4SDC-YOLOv8 effectively balances detection accuracy and computational complexity, thereby offering a promising reference for implementing small-object remote sensing detection on mobile devices.

articleTitle: Vision-Driven 3D Two-Hand Reconstruction for Mixed Reality-based remote cooperation system
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the increasing demand for high-precision operations, effective operational guidance has become increasingly critical in complex tasks. Traditionally, operators typically rely on reading text manuals or verbal communication with remote experts, but these approaches are inefficient for tasks requiring high precision and fail to provide the intuitive guidance needed for delicate operations. To address these limitations, we propose an integrated framework, MRAHandNet (Mixed Reality Assisted Hand Network), which combines vision-driven 3D two-hand reconstruction with mixed reality (MR) technology. The framework aims to transmit the shape and pose parameters of hand models to drive 3D virtual hand models in MR headsets, generating natural and precise interactive hand poses and shapes. This provides intuitive and high-precision operation guidance to operators during complex tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. This research not only lays a robust foundation for future high-precision operational tasks but also contributes to advancing remote cooperation and human-computer interaction technologies.

articleTitle: An Approach Based on BiLSTM-Transformer for Marine Inertial Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) denial environment, for the problem of fast dispersion of the positioning error of pure inertial navigation system (INS), this paper proposes a hybrid deep learning model based on bidirectional long and short term memory network (BiLSTM) and Transformer. The model establishes the mapping relationship between IMU timing data and location information through a multi-level feature fusion architecture.First, a causal convolutional layer is used to extract local dynamics features. Second, BiLSTM is utilized to capture the bidirectional long-term dependency of sensor data. Finally, the cross-channel feature interaction and dynamic weight allocation are realized by the multi-head self-attention mechanism, which improves the accuracy of the model.In order to verify the effectiveness of this method, this study conducted sea trials and collected data under different navigation conditions. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme effectively reduces the error accumulation of the inertial navigation system compared with the traditional method in pure inertial autonomous positioning, which proves the reliability and universality of the method, and has the value of popularization and engineering application.

articleTitle: Algorithm of Intelligent Speed Regulation of Fan Based on PID Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The traditional PID control has difficulties in parameter tuning, especially in complex working conditions to achieve optimal control effect. Therefore, BP neural network technology is introduced in this paper, and PID parameters are dynamically adjusted by back propagation algorithm to adapt to the changes of environmental temperature, humidity, and human activities. The experimental results show that the algorithm can quickly respond to environmental changes, achieve accurate speed control, and has good adaptability and anti-interference ability. Compared with the traditional PID control, the algorithm shows significant improvement in dynamic response speed, steady-state accuracy and energy saving effect, which provides a new technical idea for the development of intelligent fan speed control system.

articleTitle: CPO-CLSA: A Hybrid Emotion Classification and Detection Method Using Enhanced Feature Extraction from Wearable Physiological Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To overcome limitations in feature extraction and improve classification accuracy in emotion models, a novel CPOCLSA model using wearable physiological signals is proposed. The CLSA (CNN-LSTM Spatial Attention) architecture features a dual-branch design, combining CNN for spatial feature extraction, LSTM for temporal dependencies in emotional transitions, and a spatial attention mechanism for efficient feature selection. The Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) algorithm is used for automatic hyperparameter tuning, enhancing training efficiency and generalization. Experiments on Non-EEG, WESAD, and NEEG-Sub datasets show the CPO-CLSA model achieves 99.8% accuracy on Non-EEG and 99% on WESAD, demonstrating its effectiveness in dynamic adaptability and precise emotion classification. This model offers a robust solution for real-time emotion recognition in wearable devices, with significant potential for mental health monitoring and adaptive human-computer interaction systems.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Anomaly Detection in High-Frequency Trading Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm based on a staged sliding window Transformer architecture to detect abnormal behaviors in the microstructure of the foreign exchange market, focusing on high-frequency EUR/USD trading data. The method captures multi-scale temporal features through a staged sliding window, extracts global and local dependencies by combining the self-attention mechanism and weighted attention mechanism of the Transformer, and uses a classifier to identify abnormal events. Experimental results on a real high-frequency dataset containing order book depth, spread, and trading volume show that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional machine learning (such as decision trees and random forests) and deep learning methods (such as MLP, CNN, RNN, LSTM) in terms of accuracy (0.93), F1-Score (0.91), and AUC-ROC (0.95). Ablation experiments verify the contribution of each component, and the visualization of order book depth and anomaly detection further reveals the effectiveness of the model under complex market dynamics. Despite the false positive problem, the model still provides important support for market supervision. In the future, noise processing can be optimized and extended to other markets to improve generalization and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Distributed Archives Management System Based on Microservice Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the deepening of social informatization, archive management system, as an important tool of information management, can simplify the process of archive collection, sorting, storage and retrieval through digital means, and improve the efficiency of archive management. However, in the face of increasingly diverse service demands and the increasing volume of archive data, the traditional centralized architecture system has obvious shortcomings in business expansion, functional flexibility and operation convenience, which can no longer meet the current project application. In view of this situation, this paper will study the system construction and user experience respectively, and put forward a set of design and implementation scheme of distributed archive management system based on microservice architecture to promote the digital and intelligent transformation of archive management mode. Practice has proved that the overall scheme decouples all functional modules of archive management through microservice architecture, and realizes efficient storage and rapid retrieval of data by combining distributed storage technology, so as to meet the storage, retrieval and utilization requirements of massive archive data, and provide new ideas and practical reference for the optimization and upgrading of archive management system.

articleTitle: Ef-OFDP: An Efficient OpenFlow-based Topology Discovery Protocol for SDN
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issues of high control plane load, excessive redundant traffic, and topology update delays in traditional topology discovery protocols in SDN, this paper proposes an optimized mechanism, Ef-OFDP. By integrating the Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC) algorithm and Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) technology, Ef-OFDP constructs a dual-layer probing architecture comprising covering switches and ordinary switches, and integrates BFD to enable dynamic awareness of link states and trigger events, thereby reducing the overhead of periodic LLDP packets. Simulation experiments validate Ef-OFDP’s performance in heterogeneous topologies (tree, linear, Fat-Tree). Results demonstrate that compared to OFDP and OFDPv2, Ef-OFDP achieves over 50% efficiency gain in total volumes of Packet-Out and Packet-In messages, with even more pronounced benefits in large-scale networks. The solution in this paper provides a low-overhead and highly responsive topology discovery method for SDN scalability bottlenecks, suitable for dynamic scenarios such as data centers and distributed edge networks.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 for Panoramic Classroom Behavior Recognition: PMS-YOLO
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent education, real-time monitoring of student classroom behavior to optimize teaching strategies has become an important requirement in intelligent education systems. However, existing object detection algorithms face challenges such as significant scale variations among targets, severe occlusion, and limited computational resources when dealing with student classroom behavior recognition tasks. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved lightweight multi-scale detection model-PMSYOLO(Pyramid Multi-Scale YOLO). The model significantly improves the detection accuracy of small targets and the robustness in complex occlusion scenarios by constructing a multiscale pyramid network (P2-P5) and combining the SEAM occlusion-aware attention mechanism. Through lightweight design, PMS-YOLO maintains high detection accuracy while significantly reducing computational complexity. Experimental results show that on the custom dataset (SCB-Dataset), the mAP50 of PMS-YOLO reached $91.6 \%$, an increase of 5.5 percentage points compared to YOLOv8n, with a model parameter size of only 3.4M and a computational volume of 9.2 GFLOPs. This study provides new ideas for target detection in complex scenarios and offers technical support for the development of intelligent education.

articleTitle: The joint optimization of truck-drone routes for last-mile delivery
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This article proposes a joint allocation problem between truck and drone. On the basis of considering the constraints of drone battery capacity and load capacity, a mixed integer programming model for collaborative delivery between drones and vehicles was constructed to minimize the total delivery cost. In order to effectively solve the coordinated distribution path planning problem of a single drone and a single aircraft, chaotic mapping is applied to the initial population, adaptive population ratios are used, and a spiral search strategy is adopted to improve the sparrow search algorithm. Several local search strategies have been proposed. Finally, numerical experiments verified its effectiveness and compared the proposed model with traditional travel salesman problem models, highlighting its advantages.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection With OCF- And Otsu-Based Isolation Forest
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to identify anomalous pixels that differ significantly from their surrounding environment by analyzing the spectral characteristics of each pixel in a hyperspectral image (HSI). This technique is widely used in remote sensing, environmental monitoring, military reconnaissance, and other fields. Existing HAD methods face high computational costs, feature redundancy, and poor segmentation, which results in high-dimensional data processing and detection efficiency. To address these issues, this article proposes an isolation forest (iForest) method based on OCF and Otsu (OOIF), which is based on the assumption that anomalous pixels are more easily isolated than normal pixels. Specifically, when constructing the isolation tree (iTree) structure, OOIF first uses the optimal clustering framework (OCF) to select band combinations that are information-rich and low-correlated. Secondly, this method introduces Otsu’s method to optimize the selection of hyperplane intercepts for iTree partitioning. By calculating the slope that maximizes data separation, the accuracy of each split is further enhanced. Experimental results show that the algorithm performs better than the comparative algorithms on multiple datasets.

articleTitle: Research on reliability modeling of CNC equipment subsystem
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to reduce the reliability modeling error of CNC equipment, It is proposed in the paper that when a fault occurs in one subsystem, the fault data of other subsystems can be processed as truncated data. The fault sequence can be corrected by means of the average rank method, then the parameters of the model can be estimated and the fitting test can be performed. Finally,taking a series of machining center as an example, the validity of this method is verified by modeling the subsystem.

articleTitle: Decomposition-guided local-global fusion neural network for residential carbon emission prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Residential carbon emissions refer to the release of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases from residential buildings and related activities. With rapid urbanization and rising residential energy demand, these emissions have become a significant part of global greenhouse gas emissions. This paper proposes a data-driven deep learning model to predict carbon emission trends in China’s residential sector. Using carbon data from January 1, 2022, to August 31, 2024, experiments validate the model’s superior performance in forecasting across various intervals compared to other competitive models. The results indicate excellence in all evaluation metrics. Additionally, policy recommendations are provided based on predictions, offering both scientific and technical support for carbon neutrality goals in the context of global climate change.

articleTitle: Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network for Multiscale Temporal Modeling in Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) plays a crucial role as one of the key components of 5 G communication services. Predictive tasks tailored for URLLC scenarios can provide support for latency stability. However, current time-series models fail to consider the correlation between different scales of periods in latency, making it difficult to effectively capture the statistical characteristics of real data cycles. Moreover, existing computer vision models and natural language processing lack adaptation to the physical meaning of 5G Channel State Information (CSI), resulting in poor performance. In this paper, we propose a lightweight convolutional neural network based on depthwise separable modules for multiscale temporal modeling. Specifically, we employ channels with independently learnable weights of different sizes to separately capture cycles, trends, and short-term fluctuations, thus breaking the patterns of inherent cycles captured by traditional methods. Validation in real-world URLLC scenarios demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cloud Computing Energy Consumption Prediction Using Convolutional Neural Networks with Bidirectional Gated Cycle Unit
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a model that combines a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) optimization for predicting cloud computing power consumption. Experimental results show that the model significantly improves prediction accuracy, with the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the training set decreasing from 0.6 to below 0.2, and the loss value dropping from 0.08 to 0.02, eventually stabilizing. These results indicate a notable enhancement in the model’s prediction performance for cloud computing power consumption. The model achieves an $\mathrm{R}^{2}$ of 0.59 on the training set and 0.54 on the test set, demonstrating reasonable predictive capability, though the slightly lower performance on the test set suggests some overfitting. Despite this, the model presents a viable approach for cloud power consumption prediction. Future research will focus on further optimizing the algorithm and improving the model’s generalization ability to enhance its accuracy and stability in real-world applications. This study offers valuable theoretical insights and technical guidance for optimizing cloud computing resource management and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Hydraulic concrete defect detection based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The timely identification of defects is critical to ensuring operational safety in hydraulic concrete structures. To address limitations of traditional manual inspection methods—which are labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to human error—we propose a deep learning-based computer vision framework for automated defect detection. This approach eliminates the need for complex handcrafted feature engineering by leveraging convolutional neural networks to autonomously learn discriminative features from remote imagery. Specifically, we enhance the ResNeXt50 architecture through the integration of a channel attention mechanism, enabling adaptive recalibration of feature responses to emphasize defect-relevant information and improve feature representation capabilities. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves an F1 score of 88.0%, demonstrating effective classification performance across common concrete defect categories.

articleTitle: A FISCO BCOS-Based Secure Transmission System Design and Implementation for UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address data security challenges in dynamic UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) networking environments, this paper proposes a lightweight transmission architecture based on the FISCO BCOS consortium blockchain. The architecture integrates device fingerprint binding and SM3 hash aggregation mechanisms, achieving high tamper detection rates and low authentication latency in a 10-node laboratory environment. Experimental results demonstrate that the system effectively defends against man-in-the-middle and replay attacks in 5 G networks, while reducing blockchain storage overhead by $68 \%$ compared to traditional solutions. This study provides a verifiable security solution for resource-constrained UAV networks.

articleTitle: MVC: Multi-stage video caption generation model based on multi-modality
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In image caption generation, embedding image captions as a feature into the model input has been proven to be an effective method. However, in the field of video captioning, the input features of most models are still single-modal videos without text features; in addition, the captions generated by current video captioning models are relatively simple and not specific and detailed enough.To solve these problems, this paper proposes a new MultiModal Coarse-to-Fine caption generation framework, which consists of three parts: a retrieval module, a coarse-grained caption generation module and a caption polishing module. We conducted extensive experiments on the MSR-VTT and MSVD datasets, and the experimental results showed that MVC performs comparable to or even better than the state-of-the-art methods in terms of CIDEr and METEOR metrics.

articleTitle: Action Intention Recognition and Robotic Arm Actuation Based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory and Brain-Computer Interface
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To recognize action intention of the people with physical disabilities or paralysis, the combination of braincomputer interface (BCI) technology and robotic arms is a solution with great potential. As one of the most common BCI paradigms, Electroencephalogram (EEG) motor imagery (MI) can capture the electrical signals in the human brain. It can classify the people’s intention hidden in the EEG signal and drive the robotic arm to realize the action intention. Deep learning (DL) methods are used to accomplish this classification task. In this paper, a BiLSTMbased approach is proposed to classify EEG signal, and then the classification result is imported into a robotic arm to catch or release an object.

articleTitle: Research on refresh technology of electronic ink screen based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low refresh rate and high-power consumption of electronic ink screen, this paper studies a refresh optimization technology based on FPGA and proposes a dynamic waveform optimization algorithm (DWOA). The algorithm analyzes the dynamic and static areas of the image content, dynamically adjusts the driving waveform, selects high-frequency refresh waveform for the dynamic area, and selects low-frequency refresh waveform for the static area, thereby reducing unnecessary refresh operations and improving display efficiency. The system architecture is based on Xilinx ZYNQ7010/7017 chip, combined with dual-core ARM Cortex-A9 (PS side) and FPGA (PL side), realizing software and hardware collaborative optimization. The experiment was carried out in the Vivado 18.2 development environment, and the image sequence containing static and dynamic content was used for testing. The results show that the DWOA algorithm increases the refresh rate from 0.5 Hz of the traditional algorithm to 1.2 Hz, and reduces the power consumption from 2.5 W to 1.8 W. The algorithm not only significantly improves the display performance of the electronic ink screen, but also reduces energy consumption, providing a new technical path for the application of electronic ink screen in the field of dynamic display, which has important theoretical and practical significance.

articleTitle: A Diffusion-Based Approach for Mogu Painting Style Transfer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning have propelled style transfer as a critical technique in computer vision, enabling the transformation of artistic styles across diverse images. While considerable progress has been made in areas such as anime, impressionism, and modern art, the domain of traditional Chinese painting remains relatively underexplored. Among its unique styles, the Mogu (Boneless) technique, pioneered by artists like Yun Shouping, is characterized by fluid brushstrokes and subtle gradient blending, resulting in ethereal and dynamic depictions. Motivated by this distinctive artistic process, we introduce a novel neural network framework for Mogu-style transfer. Our approach begins with the extraction and optimization of edge features, followed by the fusion of content and edge features to enhance the representation of floral subjects. We then incorporate Yun Shouping’s signature color techniques and blend style and content through a U-Net-based diffusion model. Finally, global optimization is applied to refine the entire image, ensuring the generated output closely adheres to the stylistic principles of Mogu painting. To validate the effectiveness of our framework, we construct a dataset of Mogu paintings by Yun Shouping and conduct comprehensive experiments. The results highlight the framework’s ability to produce visually compelling and stylistically faithful outputs.

articleTitle: Adversarial Prompt Optimization in LLMs: HijackNet’s Approach to Robustness and Defense Evasion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper introduces HijackNet, an adversarial prompt hijacking framework designed to improve hijacking success rates and generalization in multi-lingual tasks. Combining Neural Architecture Search (NAS), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO), HijackNet generates adversarial prompts that adapt to target tasks while bypassing model defense mechanisms. This framework optimizes hijacking success, defense evasion, and task completion through a combination of a prompt generator and adversarial optimizer. We introduce a Defense Robustness Score (DRS) to evaluate the stability of prompts in adversarial settings. HijackNet improves adversarial prompt generation, advancing the security and robustness of large language models in adversarial environments.

articleTitle: Synergistic application of deep generative models and reinforcement learning in automated decision-making
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Automated decision-making has become a critical field in artificial intelligence, addressing complex challenges in autonomous driving, finance, healthcare, and industrial applications. Traditional decision-making systems often struggle with issues such as data scarcity, environmental unpredictability, and the high costs of real-world testing. These limitations hinder the development of robust and adaptive decision-making frameworks, particularly in dynamic and high-stakes scenarios.To address these challenges, this study integrates deep generative models with reinforcement learning (RL) to enhance automated decision-making. Generative models, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), create realistic synthetic data and simulate diverse scenarios, providing RL agents with enriched training environments. Meanwhile, RL enables adaptive decision strategies through continuous interaction with these simulated environments. This synergy overcomes traditional bottlenecks by improving data availability, training efficiency, and adaptability to real-world complexities. The innovation of this research lies in its hybrid framework, which combines the strengths of generative models and RL to address challenges in data-scarce, high-uncertainty environments. The proposed approach not only accelerates learning and enhances robustness but also paves the way for applications requiring ethical, safe, and transparent decisionmaking.

articleTitle: Research on Fast Startup Method of VxWorks Operating System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Compared with many embedded operating system, the VxWorks operating system has a faster startup speed. But it still needs to be improved for many time sensitive systems. This paper analyzes the startup process of VxWorks to identify the factors which affect the startup speed, and proposes a fast startup method based on boot mode, flash and memory improvement. To verify the effectiveness of the fast startup method, a hardware environment based on PowerPC was set up. The experimental results show that it only takes 0.80 s to boot up a 1580 K -sized VxWorks image. Compared with the normal booting time-10 seconds, the fast startup method reduces the total booting time by 91%.

articleTitle: Evidence-guided Feature Learning for Text-to-Image Person Re-identification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Text-to-Image Person Re-identification aims to retrieve person images based on natural language descriptions. Existing methods primarily rely on deep feature mapping to learn cross-modal consistency but often overlook the crucial visual-semantic evidence associations between text and images, leading to less interpretable matching processes. To address this issue, we propose an Evidence-guided Feature Learning framework to enhance the accuracy and robustness of cross-modal alignment. Specifically, Furthermore, we introduce an Evidence-guided Feature Aggregation strategy to enhance representation capability by fusing salient local features. Additionally, we propose an Evidence Consistency Loss to constrain the stability and generalization ability of text-to-image matching. Experimental results on CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in retrieval accuracy.

articleTitle: Intelligent Tourism System Based on a BERT Model for the Cultural Relics Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional BERT models and fine-tuned general-domain BERT models in semantic understanding within the cultural relics domain, this paper proposes an adapted BERT model specifically designed for this field. The study utilizes the fine-tuned WENWU-BERT semantic understanding model, integrates the Chroma vector database for knowledge retrieval, and employs the API interface of the DeepSeek intelligent Q&A system to infer and generate final answers. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed WENWU-BERT model outperforms traditional BERT models in both semantic understanding accuracy and Q&A quality.

articleTitle: Autonomous positioning and navigation of a quadruped robot for power transmission inspection integrating IMU and visual SLAM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the difficulty of accurately identifying and recognizing complex scenes in power transmission inspection sites for quadruped robots, which leads to poor autonomous positioning and navigation accuracy of robots, a power transmission inspection quadruped robot autonomous positioning and navigation method that integrates IMU and visual SLAM is proposed. Firstly, the original point cloud is segmented, and IMU pre integrated pose is used to remove the nonlinear motion distortion of the original point cloud. The obtained point cloud is then subjected to line and surface feature extraction. Then match the line and surface features of adjacent frames, and fuse the initial pose obtained by IMU pre integration in the hierarchical pose estimation process. Finally, based on visual SLAM optimization constraints on the pose, keyframes are matched with local maps, and factor graph optimization is used to achieve accurate SLAM for power transmission inspection, realizing autonomous positioning and navigation of the quadruped robot for power transmission inspection. The experimental results show that the proposed method has high autonomous positioning and navigation accuracy, high attitude control accuracy, and short time consumption for the quadruped transmission inspection robot. It provides technical reference for intelligent perception and safety inspection of the quadruped transmission inspection robot.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous visual localization and map construction

articleTitle: Model Analysis of Communication Entropy of Intangible Cultural Heritage within a Smart Ecosystem Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Based on the Intelligent Ecology Theory and Digital Humanities Technology, this study proposes Cultural Communication Entropy (CCE), a quantitative model for evaluating intangible cultural heritage (ICH) dissemination. The framework integrates spatiotemporal dimensions-open systems, nonlinear interactions, and dynamic entropy-through three core indicators: Communication Efficiency Entropy ($\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{e}}$), Information Fidelity Entropy ($\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}$), and Interaction Quality Entropy ($\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}$). Empirical analysis of 5,000 official and 1,000 control videos from Douyin revealed critical patterns: (1) Exponential decay of $E_{e}$ with a $32 \%$ acceleration post- 72 hours (attributed to platform algorithms); (2) Official content exhibited higher entropy stability (Median $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}=1.45$ vs. 1.12, Cohen’s $\mathrm{d}=1.05$); (3) High-entropy videos outperformed low-entropy counterparts in cross-platform sharing ($23 \%$ vs. $12 \%$) and cultural depth ($\mathrm{E}_{\text {culture }}=0.736$ vs. 0.412). The model integrates LSTM path prediction and blockchain-enhanced fidelity optimization, validated via cross-platform API synchronization (Bilibili, $\mathbf{r = 0. 7 9}$) and blockchain-encrypted data verification.

articleTitle: Record-driven Simulated Flight Training Mission Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In consumer-grade flight simulation, there is no convenient personalized solution for users' flight training that can reasonably generate new mission scenes based on their training performance. This paper introduces a novel task focused on generating flight mission scenes for users guided by their training records. We present a comprehensive framework capable of autonomously producing mission scenes. Integrating a Mission Type Recommendation and a Scene Planning module allows for the analysis of users’ proficiency and the output of scene parameters tailored to different flight simulation platforms using large language models (LLMs). Our user study to validate the effectiveness of the method on difficulty rationality, scene authenticity and parameter effectiveness.

articleTitle: A DLL-TDC Circuit with Calibration Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a DLL-TDC circuit with a calibration neural network to address the issue of uneven delay time distribution across each delay unit of the TDC. Following the integration of the DLL circuit into the TDC for the purpose of average calibration, this paper also proposes the construction of a neural network model which purpose of this is to calculate the accurate delay time of each delay unit. Furthermore, the neural network model can also replace the repetitive code density measurement work in order to complete bin-by-bin calibration. The neural network model has an accuracy rate of over $91 \%$.

articleTitle: DLNet: A Lightweight Drivable Area Segmentation Method Based on DeepLabV3+
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Drivable area segmentation is an important part of ensuring safe travel with intelligent driving. In real traffic scenarios, the drivable region presents different sizes due to obstacle occlusion. In order to take into account the characteristics of multi-scale feature extraction and reduce the computational cost of the model, this paper introduces DLNet, an improved model based on DeepLabV3+, which is good at striking a balance between efficiency and cost.The three improved modules of DLNet, the Network Pruning and Optimization Module of MobileNetV2, the MPAM(Multi-scale pooling of attention module) Module, and the Stacked Upsampling Module, can reduce the number of model parameters and the computational effort of the model, while maintaining a high degree of accuracy. Experimental results on the Cityscapes dataset show that the mean pixel accuracy (MPA) is improved by about 0.6% and the mean intersection over union ratio (MIOU) is improved by 0.4% compared to the original model DeepLabV3+ model. The number of parameters is reduced to only 39.2% of the original model and the computational load is reduced to 12.3%. There is also a large improvement compared to other models.

articleTitle: Application of an Improved Genetic Algorithm in Reactive Power Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The genetic algorithm serves as an efficient global optimization search method for the reactive power management within power systems. To minimize active power losses and ensure that reactive power remains within designated limits, chaotic search techniques have been integrated with the traditional genetic algorithm, resulting in the development of an enhanced genetic algorithm that incorporates chaos search. This method initiates the population generation through chaotic sequence exploration and refines the crossover, mutation, and selection operators.
