These enhancements significantly bolster the global optimization capabilities of the genetic algorithm, effectively reduce the likelihood of local convergence, and improve both convergence speed and computational accuracy. A simulation study was conducted to optimize the system’s reactive power. The simulation results indicate that the improved genetic algorithm can more accurately identify the global optimum, significantly accelerates the convergence process, and outperforms the standard genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Cooperative Optimization Strategies for Data Collection and Machine Learning in Large-Scale Distributed Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the development of large-scale distributed systems, how to efficiently collect and process data to support machine learning will become an increasingly important problem. However, traditional techniques often treat data acquisition and machine-learning tasks as disjoint processes, resulting in sloppy, less performant solutions. In this paper, we propose a new collaborative optimization framework which simultaneously considers the data acquisition and machine learning tasks. The method has innovatively introduced the feedback mechanism between the data acquisition module and machine learning module based on the current distributed learning model, and has achieved adaptive flexible data selection, intelligent resource allocation and dynamic optimization. Through state-of-the-art approaches like distributed reinforcement learning and data-driven scheduling protocols combined with decentralized gradient descent, the model has demonstrated superior scalability, low latency and precision compared to conventional solutions. It has been illustrated by experimental results that the accuracy of the proposed model is $15 \%$ higher than the benchmark method.

articleTitle: Network traffic anomaly detection method based on asymmetric convolutional residual memory network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Traffic anomaly detection has become a critical issue in the field of network security due to the ongoing evolution of network assaults. Deep learning-based techniques for detecting network traffic anomalies usually have poor generalization, restricted representation capabilities, and high computational cost. This research suggests an Asymmetric Convolutional Residual Memory Network (ACRMNet) to overcome these issues. The model improves the precision and robustness of anomaly detection by effectively extracting spatial and temporal information from network traffic data by using asymmetric convolution, residual networks, and LSTM modules. Experimental results show that by lowering computing complexity and increasing detection accuracy, ACRMNet performs better than other models, especially when processing complicated traffic data.

articleTitle: Software Modularity Measurement Method Based on Weighted Software Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the complexity of software function and structure, the difficulty of software development becomes more and more, the guarantee of software quality becomes more and more challenging, and the cost of maintenance and management also rises. Software measurement serves a significant function in software engineering as a quantitative method for data definition, collection and analysis of software development projects, processes and products. Among them, software modularity is the key factor in software structure measurement. In order to solve this problem, a new modularity metric Q is proposed to evaluate the modularity of software from the point of view of complex network. First, the structure of the software is represented using a characteristic coupling network (FCN). Then, the original class structure of software is regarded as the characteristic community, and the modularity index used to evaluate the community structure in the complex network field is introduced to measure the modularity of the class, so as to provide a more scientific and comprehensive measurement method.

articleTitle: Multi-Regularized Nonnegative Tensor Factorization for Context-Aware Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a powerful high-dimensional data analysis tool, tensor factorization has important applications in context-aware recommendation systems. However, traditional tensor factorization methods often face problems of model overfitting and low recommended accuracy when dealing with high-dimensional sparse data. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a Multi-regularized Nonnegative Tensor Factorization (MNTF) model that combines $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ regularization. By introducing $L_{1}$ regularization, the model can achieve sparsity, thereby effectively selecting important features and reducing complexity. At the same time, $L_{2}$ regularization further improves the generalization ability of the model by smoothing parameter values. In addition, the nonnegative constraint ensures that the decomposition results have better interpretability, making them more consistent with the data characteristics in actual application scenarios. Experimental results show that compared with other current methods, this method significantly improves the recommendation performance on multiple real datasets.

articleTitle: PolSAR Image Classification by Multi-objective optimization-based High-Order Discriminative Random Fields
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To effectively improve PolSAR image classification accuracy, which is adversely affected by feature redundancy and the curse of dimensionality, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimization-based high-order discriminative random fields (MoODRF) model. The model integrates NSGA-II and ReliefF to achieve optimal feature selection for high-dimensional data,the optimal feature set is then input into using Support Vector Machines (SVMs) to construct the unary potential, while a binary potential is modeled using a generalized Ising model with an additional edge penalty function. The high-order potential energy is captured using high-order cliques generated by superpixels,enabling the model to simultaneously incorporate texture and polarimetric features, as well as spatial neighborhood information, and higher-order structural information.Finally, the classification result of the PolSAR image is obtained using the Iterated Conditional Modes(ICM) method.The efficacy of the suggested strategy is demonstrated by experiments using actual PolSAR images.

articleTitle: RGB-D-Based 3D Scale Recovery for Residential interior Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) visual generation technologies, represented by Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), have been widely applied in various fields in recent years. Prior to NeRF reconstruction based on deep learning, traditional algorithms are typically used to estimate camera poses. However, Multi-View Stereo (MVS) algorithms solely relying on RGB photographs can only determine the relative 3D structure of targets and cannot accurately estimate their actual 3D scale. Depth cameras, as imaging devices capable of capturing both target pixel information (RGB) and depth information (D), have become popular in civilian applications. MVS technology based on RGB-D images can provide camera poses with real-scale information. However, due to practical factors such as lighting and surface reflection of materials, depth values measured by civilian depth cameras often contain certain errors. Therefore, how to effectively eliminate depth errors in RGB-D images to accurately recover the actual 3D scale of targets is an urgent issue to be addressed in practical applications. To address this issue, this study proposes two improved algorithms for RGB-D multi-view scale recovery based on previous work: The first improved algorithm (Adaptive-3D-BA) directly obtains camera pose estimates with real-scale information by adaptively adjusting depth values and incorporating them into the traditional Bundle Adjustment (BA) algorithm. The second improved algorithm (BA-SE) adds a Scale Estimation (SE) postprocessing module to the traditional BA based on RGB images, utilizing the least squares method to recover the actual scale information of the camera. Comparative analysis on the TUM dataset verifies the effectiveness of the above methods in improving measurement accuracy. The results indicate that the proposed algorithms can provide accurate scale information for indoor 3D reconstruction of old residential buildings, holding broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Research on IPv6 Address Security Application based on DUID and SNMP
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the wide application of IPv6, the problem of IPv4 address resource exhaustion has been solved, but it also brings new challenges. Aiming at the address security management problem in IPv6 network, this paper proposes an IPv6 address management and alarm method based on DUID (DHCPv6 Unique Identifier), DHCPv6 and SNMP. In view of the difficulties in IPv6 address management and operation, and the inability to effectively read terminal equipment information in the application scenario of gas mine office network, a management system based on C/S mode was designed. The client collected local equipment network configuration information through the network card, and uploaded it to the server for centralized management. After the server checks the validity, once the illegal access is detected, the system will automatically trigger an alarm and notify the administrator. At the same time, by using SNMP protocol in the server to collect network equipment information, to ensure the effective management of network equipment. The actual deployment and application results show that this method improves the management efficiency in Ipv6 environment, and ensures the convenience and efficiency of IPv6 address management and application security.

articleTitle: GCL: An Optimization Strategy for Eliminating I/O and Garbage Collection Conflicts in SSD RAID
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Faced with large-capacity storage requirements, the SSD RAID-5 system offers fast I/O performance and fault tolerance. However, as the space management module of SSDs, the complexity of the garbage collection (GC) operating mechanism is the primary cause of the decline in read and write performance. Furthermore, this situation will only become more severe in SSD RAID systems. This article proposes a garbage collection lock strategy based on SSD RAID - 5, named GCL (Garbage Collection Lock). This strategy restricts the number of SSDs that need garbage collection to one each time and utilizes the fault-tolerance mechanism of RAID-5 to reconstruct read operations that need to be carried out on the locked device. Additionally, for write operations, we prioritize caching the locked device write requests during garbage collection. Through a series of simulation tests on several real disk workloads, we have shown that GCL can effectively improve system performance. Compared with RR, GCL increased the reconstruction operation rate by an average of 23% and reduced the overall response time by an average of 5.6%.

articleTitle: Multi-Carrier Filtering Method for Satellite Mobile Communication System Based on CNN+LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issues of adjacent channel interference, nonlinearTo address the issues of adjacent channel interference, nonlinear hardware resource limitations faced by multi and hardware resource limitations faced by multi-carrier signal demodulation in satellite mobile communication systems, this paper proposes a joint filtering method based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM). By designing multi-scale convolutional kernels to hierarchically extract time-frequency features, combined with bidirectional LSTM to model temporal correlations, and introducing an attention mechanism to dynamically focus on key frequency bands, it replaces the explicit extraction and downconversion process of traditional Kaiser window half-band filters. Experiments show that under the condition of 15dB Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), this scheme reduces the Symbol Error Rate (SER) by $40 \%$ compared to traditional methods ($0.7 \%$ vs $1.8 \%$), improves the Adjacent Channel Rejection Ratio by 4 dB, and reduces hardware resource usage by $50 \%$.

articleTitle: A Lightweight AES Algorithm Optimization for NoC Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In response to the contradiction between high throughput and low hardware overhead faced by data encryption in Network on Chip (NoC) communication, this paper proposes a lightweight AES implementation method based on chaos initial permutation (IP) matrix and look up table optimization based on composite field $\mathrm{GF}\left(2^{4}\right)^{2}$. By introducing the Logistic-Tent composite chaotic system to generate a nonlinear initial permutation matrix, replacing the SubBytes operation, randomness of the diffusion layer is effectively improved; Composite filed $\mathrm{GF}\left(2^{4}\right)^{2}$ compress the storage size of the look up table to 12.5% of the original structure (from 4KB to 0.25KB). The average encryption time is optimized by 26.6% compared with SIMON, and only increase 4.5% average execution time of base NoC in Gem5 simulator. NIST tests are also used to evaluate the effectiveness of proposed algorithm. All results have shown that this method significantly improves the adaptability of AES in NoC.

articleTitle: Multi AGV Task Allocation Considering Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Multi robot task allocation problem (MRTP) has important application value in the fields of intelligent manufacturing, warehousing logistics and unmanned distribution. The traditional genetic algorithm (GA) has the problems of unbalanced load and easy to fall into local optimization in task allocation. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved genetic algorithm to improve the load balance and overall performance of multi robot task allocation based on automated guided vehicle (AGV) by optimizing the fitness function and introducing adaptive crossover mutation strategy. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional GA, the improved genetic algorithm can better balance the load, reduce the task completion time, and improve the convergence speed of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-population Co-evolutionary Multi-objective Optimization Algorithm Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Evolutionary computation is widely applied in multi-objective optimization due to its excellent global search capability and the characteristic of having multiple solutions. Among them, the Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm has received extensive attention from researchers because of its good development ability and fast convergence speed. However, a single population tends to fall into local optima when dealing with complex optimization problems. The algorithm still has issues such as low development precision and poor diversity of solutions. To address this, this paper proposes a Multi-Objective Optimization algorithm based on Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimization (MOGWO) and Improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Co-evolution (MCMOIPG). In each iteration, the population is randomly divided into MOPSO and MOGWO parts. In MOPSO, to balance the influence of solution precision and diversity, a learning factor combining non-dominated sorting and crowding distance is proposed. The position change of particles is influenced by the learning factor. The algorithm is compared with four other algorithms on the CEC2009 standard multi-objective test functions. Experimental results show that MCMO-IPG has superior performance in terms of solution precision, diversity, and algorithm stability.

articleTitle: Research on decoding technology of visual brain-computer interface based on convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Brain-computer interface is to establish a direct communication channel between human brain and computer by reading the electrical signal of human brain activity, so as to realize the direct communication between human and computer and machine. At present, certain progress has been made in the application of brain-computer interface technology in the treatment and rehabilitation training of diseases related to movement disorders. The new machine learning technology represented by deep learning has received more and more attention in the field of brain-computer interface, especially the brain-computer interface system based on convolutional neural network can effectively solve the problem of low recognition accuracy of traditional brain-computer interface system. In this paper, the decoding technology of visual brain-computer interface based on CNN is studied.

articleTitle: Research on estimation method for OFDM channel of power line carrier based on LR-LMMSE algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Channel estimation methods for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems are key technologies for performance optimization in communication systems, particularly in power line communication (PLC) environments where the channel has significant frequency selectivity and noise. This paper investigates a Low-Rank Linear Minimum Mean Square Error (LR-LMMSE) channel estimation algorithm aimed at reducing the computational complexity of traditional minimum mean square error (MMSE) and Linear Minimum Mean Square Error (LMMSE) algorithms, which are critical for efficient signal recovery in PLC systems. The proposed algorithm simplifies high-dimensional matrix operations into low-dimensional computations by performing low-rank decomposition on the channel correlation matrix, thereby significantly reducing computational complexity while maintaining robust estimation accuracy. Theoretical analyses and simulation outcomes indicate that the LR-LMMSE algorithm effectively balances computational complexity with estimation performance, making it a suitable solution for channel estimation in large-scale MIMO and high-dimensional OFDM systems, particularly in the context of PLC with high computational efficiency and reliability requirements.

Author Keywords: Low-Rank Linear Minimum Mean Square Error

articleTitle: A hybrid network combining convolutional neural networks and transformers for skin disease segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a new hybrid network combining convolutional neural networks and transformers for skin disease segmentation, named TBMAU-Net, specifically designed for high-precision segmentation of skin lesion areas. The model leverages Transformers to capture long-range dependencies and employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract detailed local information. A novel hybrid module that integrates CNNs with Transformers is introduced to effectively capture both global and local feature information. To enhance the extracted features, we utilize a depthwise separable convolution attention module, which dynamically assigns attention weights during the encoding phase, thereby enriching the channel and spatial information. We also introduce a multi-scale aggregation module that fuses features from multiple scales, promoting robust feature interactions and compensating for variations in image resolutions. Extensive experiments conducted on the publicly available ISIC 2016 and PH2 datasets demonstrate that TBMAU-Net achieves an optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency. It outperforms many state-of-the-art methods in segmentation performance, showing remarkable capability in handling irregular shapes, significant color variations, ambiguous boundaries, and complex interference-prone lesion areas. These advanced functionalities significantly ease the challenge for medical professionals in accurately assessing complex skin lesions. By integrating the strengths of both Transformers and CNNs, TBMAU-Net represents a significant step forward in medical image segmentation, offering improved precision and reliability in diagnosing skin conditions.

articleTitle: Reward Defining in Multi-armed Bandit SAT Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: SAT solvers are widely used in various fields, and significant efforts have been made to improve the efficiency of Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL) solvers by integrating the Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) algorithm. A notable example is the Kissat_MAB solver. However, existing MAB-based solvers face limitations due to their reward functions, which are not wellaligned with the complexities of CDCL SAT solving, leading to biased heuristic selection, especially in challenging instances. To address this, we propose a novel MAB framework, MAB-DC, featuring a new reward function designed to better adapt to SAT solving. This framework is generalizable and can be applied to all MAB-based solvers. Building on the advanced Kissat_MAB solver, we develop Kissat_MAB-DC. Experimental evaluations on 800 instances from SAT 2022 and SAT 2023 demonstrate that Kissat_MAB-DC outperforms Kissat_MAB, Kissat_MABHyWalk, and Kissat_MAB_Conflict+ in terms of both the number of solved instances and average runtime, particularly for satisfiable instances. Additionally, Kissat_MAB-DC achieved second place in the 2024 SAT Competition.

articleTitle: Communication Signal Recognition Based on Time-Frequency and Bispectral Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the complex electromagnetic environment, the existing single-feature-domain methods for non-cooperative communication signal recognition have limited representation ability in diverse signal scenarios, leading to insufficient recognition accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a deep learning method based on time-frequency bispectrum multifeature fusion. The proposed method innovatively constructs a joint feature extraction framework that combines time-frequency analysis and bispectrum analysis. Time-frequency analysis is employed to capture the dynamic characteristics of signals, while bispectrum analysis is used to extract higher-order statistical information. This combination enables complementary feature representation. Furthermore, a deep model integrating the ResNet18 network and SE attention mechanism is designed. The residual structure in ResNet18 is utilized to mine spatial deep features, and the channel attention mechanism adaptively optimizes the weights of key features. This enhances the robustness of the model under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better recognition accuracy than traditional single-feature-domain methods in low SNR scenarios.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal Analysis of Fishing Vessel Operational Behavior and Merchant Vessel Trajectory in the Yellow Sea Based on AIS Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to further ensure the safety of shipping in China’s neighbouring waters, this study investigates crawling, preprocessing and behavioural analysis of fishing vessel trajectory data based on AIS vessel data in the Yellow Sea area. The aim is to identify fishing vessel operation patterns and merchant vessel route distribution patterns. Through speed screening, thermal distribution map construction and trajectory clustering analysis, the behavioural patterns of fishing vessels were identified, and the clustering characteristics of merchant vessels’ transoceanic voyage trajectories were analysed. The results of the study demonstrate that fishing behaviour can be screened by means of sailing speed screening of fishing vessel trajectories, and the clustering of merchant vessel trajectories reveals the spatial distribution pattern of major routes. This study provides data-driven technical support for the regulation of fisheries and the safety of shipping in the sea area.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Combinatorial Visual Feedback for Virtual Grasping with Bare Hands
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Due to the lack of haptic feedback and depth cues in virtual environments, visual feedback is usually used as a substitute to guide users during virtual grasping with bare hands. Prior studies have designed and evaluated visual cues for a portion of the interaction process of virtual grasping, such as the object proximity phase, the object contact phase, and the object grasping phase. However, a visual feedback strategy for the entire process of virtual grasping has not been proposed. In this paper, we proposed four combinations of visual feedback from three types of single visual feedback including proximity feedback, contact feedback, and grasp confirmation feedback. We presented a controlled usability evaluation of combinatorial visual feedback and single visual feedback in virtual object-grasping tasks using bare hands. The results show that proximity + grasp confirmation feedback and proximity + contact + grasp confirmation feedback are superior in task performance and user satisfaction. To rationalize the trade-off between cost-effectiveness and high performance, we further recommend proximity + grasp confirmation feedback as the visual feedback strategy for virtual grasping.

articleTitle: Port Wind Speed Prediction Model Based on VMD and GRU-MLP
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study proposes a combined prediction model integrating variational mode decomposition (VMD), gated recurrent unit (GRU), and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to address the low accuracy and poor fitting performance of existing short-term port wind speed prediction models. The model’s performance is evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Experiments were conducted with real-time wind speed data collected from wind speed sensors on large cranes to predict wind speed for the next 10 minutes. Comparative analysis results demonstrate that the VMD-GRU-MLP model achieves higher predictive accuracy for short-term forecasts.

articleTitle: A U-Net–Based Automated Fluorescence and Morphological Analysis of CH25H Knockdown and Overexpressing Cell Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Elucidating the influence of $\mathbf{C H 2 5 H}$ on cellular metabolism, immune regulation, and viral infection at the molecular level holds significant promise for understanding the pathogenesis of related diseases. Conventional fluorescence microscopy-based quantitative methods are time-consuming and prone to subjective bias in large-scale experiments. To address these limitations, this study established stable cell lines with CH25H knockdown and overexpression, employing a U-Net model for automated segmentation and quantitative analysis of fluorescence images. This approach encompasses cell-line construction, microscopic imaging, high-throughput image segmentation, and statistical evaluation. The results demonstrate that U-Net achieves high accuracy in delineating cellular contours and quantifying fluorescence signals, effectively identifying morphological and expression-level variations across different clones. By reducing experimental duration and operator-induced bias, this automated analysis method proves valuable for subsequent $\mathbf{C H 2 5 H}$ function investigations and the design of largescale cellular assays.

articleTitle: Enhanced UAV Detection in Foggy Environments: Integrating Receptive Field Attention and Global Context in YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Detecting unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in foggy conditions poses significant challenges due to poor visibility and image degradation. To address this, we propose Defog-YOLO, a neural network that integrates receptive field spatial attention convolution (RFAConv) and the global context attention mechanism (GCNet) into YOLOv8 for enhanced UAV detection. The RFAConv, incorporated into the defogging module of the All-in-One dehazing network (AOD-Net), effectively extracts UAV features from foggy images. Meanwhile, the GCNet, integrated into YOLOv8, leverages long-range dependencies to boost the detection of small objects. An end-to-end joint inference framework optimizes the performance of both defogging and detection. We introduce a new dataset, GUET-UAV-FOG, comprising both real and synthesized foggy UAV images to evaluate our approach. Experimental results demonstrate that Defog-YOLO significantly improves mean average precision (mAP) up to $80.2 \%$, outperforming baseline methods, thus showcasing its effectiveness in UAV detection even under adverse foggy conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Online Bookstore Based on ASP
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: E-commerce technology is booming, and online bookstores are springing up and developing rapidly. This paper focuses on the online bookstore system with ASP.NET technology framework as the core, and discusses the whole process of its design and realization. The system adopts B/S architecture, with Visual Studio as the integrated development environment, and at the same time, with the help of SQL Server database to store data information, and through ADO.NET to realize the database connection and access. The system is mainly divided into two parts: frontend and backend. The frontend covers user registration, login, shopping cart management and other functional modules, so that users can conveniently browse books, add to the shopping cart and settlement and other operations. The backend is mainly responsible for order processing, user information management and other functional modules to help administrators efficiently manage the daily operation of the bookstore. The development of the system provides users with convenient and rich book purchase channels, helps merchants to reduce costs and expand the market, and has a certain application value.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Embedded Virtualization Technology Based on i.MX 8MP
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper transplants the hypervisor middleware based on the embedded virtualization technology of the NXP I.MX8MP hardware platform. By modifying the underlying device tree and partition configuration files, four Linux partitions are able to run independently on the same platform. On this basis, an efficient data exchange scheme between partitions is designed and implemented based on the shared memory communication mechanism. Direct access to the shared memory data buffer by the application layer avoids multiple copies of data in the kernel space and user space, reducing communication overhead. Test results show that when transmitting 10 KB of data, the transmission delay is mainly concentrated around $50 \mu \mathrm{~s}$, which effectively improves communication efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of an Adaptive English Education Management Information System Based on Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The rapid development of deep learning models has driven the development of teaching management systems in higher education institutions. Therefore, education management information systems based on artificial intelligence (AI) technology have attracted the attention of a large number of researchers. In this study, an adaptive English education management information system based on deep learning was designed to evaluate the performance of teachers in higher education institutions. The system consists of three levels: data layer, deep learning model layer, and application layer. The deep learning model layer can call on multimodal data from the data layer, scientifically evaluate the performance of teachers based on deep neural network algorithms, and finally display it in the visualization module of the application layer. On this basis, in order to improve the prediction accuracy of deep learning models, an improved Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) is proposed to optimize the hyperparameters of deep learning. Finally, case studies were conducted using data from three different higher education institutions, and the analysis results showed that the predictive framework used in this study had high accuracy.

articleTitle: Small target detection based on multimodal data fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Object detection is a fundamental task in remote sensing with wide applications in autonomous vehicle navigation, surveillance, and search-and-rescue operations. Remote sensing images, typically captured by satellites, aircraft, and UAV sensors, are of great significance in both military and civilian domains due to their extensive coverage and ease of collection. However, several challenges arise in the capture of remote sensing images: first, objects are often very small relative to the size of the image, leading to limited feature information; second, objects can be oriented arbitrarily, requiring detection algorithms to learn rotation-invariant features for better performance; and third, noise and occlusions need to be handled by detection algorithms. In this paper, we propose MR-YOLOV5, a convolutional network specifically designed for real-time object detection in remote sensing images. MR-YOLOV5 is capable of detecting small objects with arbitrary orientations and tight spacing, as well as performing large-scale object detection. Additionally, by integrating multi-modal remote sensing data, the network’s performance in detecting challenging objects is enhanced. Experimental results on the publicly available VEDAI dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Chinese Named Entity Recognition Based on Multi-feature fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Chinese Named Entity Recognition(NER) is a critical technology for processing Chinese text information, its core goal is to identify and extract named entities with specific semantic meaning from unstructured text. Although the technology of Chinese named entity recognition is constantly developing, there is still a problem that it is not possible to make full use of the unique information of Chinese characters such as glyphes and ‘pinyin’ to deeply mine the rich semantics contained in Chinese. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a Chinese named entity recognition mode, MFF-NER, based on multi-feature fusion. The model uses convolutional neural network and multi-head self-attention mechanism to capture the grapheme features and ‘pinyin’ features hidden in Chinese characters, integrates multi-dimensional information, and then uses bidirectional long short-term memory neural network to learn long-distance context representation. Finally, conditional random fields are integrated to model constraints in sentence sequence labels, thereby enhancing the model’s deep semantic mining capabilities and improving overall performance. Experimental results prove that the proposed model can effectively improve the performance of Chinese named entity recognition task.

articleTitle: Comparison and Optimization of Amdo Tibetan Speech Recognition Based on Transducer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Amdo Tibetan, as a low-resource language with a complex phonological system, faces dual challenges in speech recognition: data scarcity and insufficient model generalization. Under the condition of limited Tibetan corpus resources, this study constructs a Transducer model based on the Kaldi-2 framework. To address the complex syllable structures (e.g., consonant clusters) and tonal variations in Tibetan, we introduce noise injection during data processing, integrate Tibetan n-gram language models, and employ BPE subword tokenization to optimize training data. We compare the performance of two encoders, Conformer<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> and Zipformer<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup>, under seven decoding strategies in low-data scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate Zipformer’s superiority in multi-scale temporal modeling. The optimized Zipformer outperforms Conformer across multiple dimensions: under the Fast Beam Search N-Best Language Model Enhanced decoding rule, Zipformer reduces the word error rate (WER) from $11.72 \%$ to $6.44 \%$, achieves a $22.6 \%$ improvement in inference speed, and reduces memory consumption to 0.9 GB. These results highlight Zipformer’s efficiency and accuracy in handling complex speech recognition tasks, attributed to its multi-scale modeling capability and adaptability to long-term dependencies in Tibetan. This research provides practical guidelines for model selection and optimization in low-resource, phonologically complex languages, offering a feasible technical solution for digitizing minority languages.

articleTitle: Qwen-VL2 Model with NEFTune technique For Medical Report Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study highlights the growing integration of AI into the biomedical domain, focusing on developing a medical report generation model by leveraging Alibaba’s open-source vision-language model, Qwen2-VL, for supervised learning. Qwen2-VL supports multilingual interactions, covering English, Chinese, and several other languages, and is capable of real-time image and video content analysis, showcasing advanced visual understanding and generation capabilities. Despite its versatility, Qwen2-VL’s generated results lack the professionalism and reliability necessary for specialized medical reports without proper fine-tuning. To address this, a dedicated instruction fine-tuning dataset was constructed for the model, accompanied by performance evaluation using relevant metrics. Additionally, NEFTune, a method designed to enhance noise resistance, was utilized to improve the model’s performance. Experimental comparisons with other models, such as Llava, CogVLM, and Qwen-VL, demonstrated that the enhanced Qwen2-VL model achieved superior performance on the Rouge metric, highlighting its effectiveness for medical report generation.

articleTitle: Enhanced Knowledge Graph Recommendation Algorithm Integrating Graph Attention and Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that current knowledge graph based recommendation systems cannot capture complex high-order entity relationship information, an enhanced knowledge graph recommendation algorithm model (GAKR-GCL) that integrates graph attention and contrastive learning is proposed. GAKR-GCL improves the effectiveness of knowledge graph embedding modules by comparing learning and graph attention networks, while utilizing adaptive gating mechanisms combined with graph attention networks to generate more accurate item feature vectors. Specifically, firstly, the model utilizes a multi-layer perceptron to extract high-order latent features of users. Then, the model dynamically adjusts the weights of collaborative filtering vectors and knowledge graph entity vectors through an adaptive gating mechanism, generating more accurate item representations. Next, the knowledge graph embedding module is combined with graph attention network to aggregate multi hop neighborhood information, generate enhanced entity representations, and introduce multi view contrastive learning to improve the model’s generalization ability. In addition, L2 regularization is used to prevent over-fitting of the model. Finally, the normalized inner product operation is used as the evaluation function to predict the user’s preferences for the item. In three publicly available datasets, MovieLens-1M, Book Crossing, and Last.FM show that the GAKR-GCL model can effectively improve recommendation performance compared to other benchmark models.

articleTitle: Conical Window-Attentive Point Cloud Segmentation Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The sparse and uneven nature of point cloud data leads to suboptimal performance of traditional segmentation approaches at greater distances, resulting in a degradation of overall accuracy. To tackle this challenge, this study employs a cone window technique to effectively segment point clouds, thereby aggregating long-range information. Additionally, exponential positional encoding is introduced to enhance the capability of positional encoding. Ultimately, an adaptive feature selection module is utilized to yield more effective features. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm in this paper effectively improves the model’s segmentation accuracy and outperforms other solutions proposed in the field.

articleTitle: Dynamic Attention-Guided Video Generation from Text with Multi-Scale Synthesis and LoRA Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper introduces DAG-VSNet, a new architecture for high-quality text-to-video generation. The model uses a Dynamic Text Encoder (DTE), Multi-Scale Video Generator (MS-VG), Dynamic Attention Map (DAM), and LoRA-Enhanced Video Generator (LVG). The DTE captures temporal patterns, and the DAM helps focus on important text features. The MS-VG improves video details at different scales, and the LVG fine-tunes pre-trained weights with less computation. Experiments show DAG-VSNet works better than baseline models in metrics like Inception Score (IS), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Temporal Consistency Score (TCS), and Text-Video Alignment Score (TVAS). Ablation studies show that LoRA, dynamic attention, and multi-scale methods improve performance. This work provides a useful framework for future research in text-driven video generation.

articleTitle: Coaxially Fed Circular Waveguide Antenna and Performance Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Electronic devices such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth often experience signal attenuation due to obstacles like walls and metal objects. This issue can be mitigated by designing a waveguide antenna to enhance signal directionality, improving performance in environments with obstructions. In this study, a circular waveguide antenna was designed with a coaxial feed, optimized for an operating frequency of 2.45 GHz. The antenna design focused on controlling internal radiation and assessing the effects of various parameters on performance. To further improve directionality, a conical horn structure was added at the open end of the waveguide, transforming it into a horn antenna. The conical horn increased the antenna’s gain and directivity, making it more suitable for applications requiring focused radiation, though it came at the cost of increased return loss. Simulations were performed to determine the optimal antenna parameters, including waveguide length, coaxial insertion depth, and horn dimensions. The final design achieved excellent return loss performance, with -53 dB at 2.45 GHz for the basic circular waveguide antenna. After the conical horn addition, the return loss was reduced to -25 dB, but the directionality significantly improved, enhancing signal strength in the desired direction. Overall, the design trade-off between return loss and directivity makes this antenna practical for environments that prioritize focused signal radiation over minimal signal loss.

articleTitle: An Improved VFNet Network for Ship Detection in SAR Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate detection of ships in high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery plays an important role in effective maritime search and rescue, as well as maritime surveillance and monitoring. Recently, many deep learning-based detection networks have been proposed for SAR ship detection. However, there are still some detection challenges, particularly in inshore regions where the complex background interference from man-made structures frequently lead to a high false alarm rate. In addition, small ships with limited pixels are easily to be missed detection, especially in inshore regions. To solve the aforementioned problems, we develop an anchor-free SAR ship detection method based on improved VarifocalNet (VFNet). Specifically, a refined channel attention and fusion module (RCAFM) is designed to improve the detection performance. Within this module, the refined channel attention module is utilized to suppress the interference of irrelevant background information and enhance the detection network attention on the areas related to ship detection. Furthermore, the refined feature map is integrated with semantically richer feature map to improve the detection performance of ship in SAR imagery. The experiments conducted on the HRSID dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average precision of $92.3 \%$ at an IoU threshold of 0.5 and $80.0 \%$ at an IoU threshold of 0.75, which outperforms the baseline by $0.9 \%$ and $1.2 \%$, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Real-Time Collaborative Multi-End Interaction Platform Based on WebSocket and WebRTC
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Based on Node.js service,this study combines WebSocket and WebRTC technologies to build an online collaboration platform that supports real-time collaboration and multi-terminal interaction:WebSocket implements full-duplex communication to ensure real-time data transmission and synchronized rendering of webpages, and WebRTC supports real-time audio/video communication and data transmission in the browser:WebSocket implements full-duplex communication to ensure real-time data transmission and synchronized rendering of web pages. At the same time, WebRTC supports real-time audio and video communication and data transmission in browsers. The platform provides an effective solution for cross-platform online collaboration with excellent performance in user operation synchronization,audio and video communication and data storage.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Completion Based on Entity Description Information and Graph Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Knowledge graphs, as a structured knowledge representation, are widely used in fields such as recommender systems and intelligent Q&A. However, existing knowledge graphs usually suffer from the problem of incomplete information, especially in large-scale entity and relationship scenarios, and lack efficient complementation methods. To this end, this paper proposes TNGAT, a knowledge graph complementation model based on entity descriptions and neighborhood information, which improves the complementation performance by combining BERT to generate semantic representations of entities with Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to weightedly aggregate neighbor information. In addition, TNGAT employs ConvR decoder to optimize relational inference. Experimental results show that TNGAT significantly outperforms existing methods on the FB15K237 and WN18RR datasets, validating its superiority.

articleTitle: DiffSegLoc: Privacy Preserving Visual Localization with Diffusion Models and Segmentation Consistency
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Visual localization is fundamental in computer vision and is widely integrated in autonomous driving, virtual reality and industrial manufacturing. Robust and accurate visual localization has attracted intense attention. In practice, query images often contain privacy information, including human faces, vehicles and road signs. Existing visual localization methods exploit direct visual information from these images, which may cause privacy disclosure. In this paper, a novel privacy preserving framework has been proposed to perform style-transfer on images using diffusion models and maintain semantic consistency for accurate and robust visual localization. First, it transfer the style of images using large vision models(LVMs) constrained by text prompts and semantic segmentation. Then, it estimates the camera pose by employing a feature matching algorithm for style transferred images. Experimental results on public visual localization datasets show that, in comparison with state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method can achieve comparable performance in terms of visual localization accuracy, meanwhile ensuring privacy preserving.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Application of an Intelligent Work Order Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, intelligent work order management systems offer significant advantages in improving work efficiency and service quality. This paper designs and implements an intelligent work order management system based on big data analysis and machine learning techniques, aiming to optimize the work order processing workflow, enhance processing efficiency, and improve customer satisfaction. The system introduces technologies such as early warning models, real-time reminder mechanisms, and automated outbound calling systems, significantly reducing work order timeout rates, improving work order acceptance rates, and optimizing the response time for sensitive requests. After implementing the early warning mechanism, the timeout rate of work orders decreased from 11.67% to 4.00%, and the acceptance rate increased from 83.33% to 95%. Additionally, the system’s stability and scalability were effectively validated, ensuring efficient operation in future high-concurrency environments. Experimental results show that after the intelligent transformation, the system performs excellently on several key metrics, with work order processing time reduced from 12 hours to 8 hours, response time for sensitive requests shortened from 20 minutes to 5 minutes, and customer satisfaction increased from 70% to 90%. These improvements effectively reduced labor costs and significantly enhanced customer satisfaction, demonstrating strong practical application value.

articleTitle: Lightweight metal parts detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv11n
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The progress of science and technology and the development of management concept promote the change of warehouse management to improve efficiency, reduce costs and improve service quality. As a key process, the warehouse picking mode has evolved from manual to mechanization to automation and intelligence. Although automation and intelligence improve the efficiency and accuracy of picking, many medium, small and micro enterprises are still in the stage of mechanization or manual picking. For precision parts manufacturers that cannot use automated equipment, people are optimizing picking paths and using voice technology and augmented reality (AR) technologies to improve efficiency. Augmented reality increases worker wellbeing by increasing speed and reducing error rates, but target recognition is still limited by network latency. In order to reduce the number of model parameters, narrow the model size, and ensure that the model can be successfully deployed on mobile devices with limited computing resources. This paper presents a lightweight metal parts detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv11 to improve the warehouse picking efficiency of small and medium enterprises. By constructing a metal parts data set containing real picking scenes, introducing the LSCD-Head detection head, LAMP pruning method and knowledge distillation, the model is lightweight and maintains high accuracy. The experimental results show that while maintaining the accuracy, the number of parameters and the calculation tation are significantly reduced and the speed is improved, which is better than the traditional YOLOv11n model.

articleTitle: Similarity Feature Fusion and Adversarial Shape Constraints for Precise Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate image segmentation can help doctors obtain important pathological information from complex medical images, and is of great significance in preoperative diagnosis, surgical planning, and postoperative evaluation of diseases. Due to the characteristics of physiological structure, the location and shape of lesions in medical image data are extremely irregular, the morphological volume in different individuals is highly variable, and the junction area of different tissues often has fuzzy boundaries. This paper proposes a segmentation method based on similarity feature fusion and adversarial shape constraint. The similarity feature fusion method designed in the feature fusion process filters out interference information and suppresses artifact activation by establishing a similarity matrix of the same spatial position in different feature maps. To address the problem of inaccurate segmentation of lesion edges, we proposed a selfsupervised shape-guided strategy based on a generative adversarial network. By training its encoder-decoder through reconstructing labels and prediction results, the prediction results of the supervised segmentation network are constantly approaching the true labels. We have achieved excellent results on both the polyp dataset and the skin lesion dataset, with mIoU values of $84.11 \%$ and $87.36 \%$, respectively.

articleTitle: Knowledge mapping of Belief Rule Based research : --A visual analysis using CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Belief Rule-Based(BRB) is an expert system that supports data-driven modeling and deals with uncertain information. Over the past decade, the literature on BRB has developed rapidly. However, almost no studies have utilized bibliometric visualization methods to present and analyze the research on BRB. To determine the evolution, current status, and trends in the BRB research, this study examines 249 BRB research articles published between 2006 and 2023 in the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace is used to construct and visualize the knowledge map. In this study, we identify the most influential publications in the field of BRB, recognized the main journals, key authors, institutions, and countries. Additionally, we analyze co-authorship and clustering relationships to identify research hotspots and trends. We present all research topics using bibliometric visualization to provide new insights and ideas for related research. Our findings are as follows: First, the most significant developments and advancements in BRB research have primarily occurred in China and the United Kingdom. Second, existing research in the BRB domain mainly focuses on decision-making, fault detection, and risk assessment. Third, BRB, as a new artificial intelligence method, has an obvious growth trend in artificial intelligence research and may become an emerging theme trend.

articleTitle: FA-CloudSeg:Feature-Aligned Architecture for Ground-Based Cloud Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a vital component of the Earth’s system, clouds play a crucial role in climate change research and meteorological forecasting. Due to the blurred edges and highly variable shapes of cloud layers, existing deep learning methods for cloud image segmentation often suffer from boundary misjudgments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) model named FA-CloudSeg, which effectively optimizes segmentation performance for complex cloud boundaries through the integration of an Image Embedding Layer, Self-Attention Module, and Feature-Aligned Module. The proposed network exhibits the following key characteristics: First, Image Embedding Layer: Extracts cloud-related features from images, enhancing the network’s ability to distinguish cloud regions. Second, Self-Attention Module: Captures global dependencies to improve feature representation under varying lighting and morphological conditions. Finally, Feature-Aligned Module: Integrates shallow and deep-level information while maintaining cross-scale consistency, refining segmentation accuracy for intricate cloud boundaries. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate that the model outperforms existing methods in core metrics such as recall rate, offering a novel solution for ground-based cloud image segmentation.

articleTitle: Critical design of a satellite GCS software architecture supporting multi-site collaboration and task automation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As satellites evolve towards large-scale low Earth orbit constellations and multifunctional geostationary satellites, satellite control technology and service systems are continuously updated, making traditional business management models inadequate to meet new demands. To meet the development goals of modern control systems, such as massive satellite tracking and automated management of routine operations, this paper proposes a ground control management system software architecture based on modularization, automation, and intelligent design, supporting flexible deployment across multiple sites, and designs key mechanisms for multi-site collaborative tracking, automated strategy calculation, and task execution. The article introduces the implementation methods of key business mechanisms based on a distributed framework and provides application cases for comprehensive demonstration. Based on this framework and key mechanisms, it can fully utilize the hardware resources of the control and measurement station network, improve the efficiency of control and measurement services, enhance the level of business automation, and simultaneously support various control and measurement management task requirements for large-scale constellations and multifunctional satellites.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Authentication Scheme Based on Improved SVM in Static Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This thesis proposes a physical layer authentication scheme based on multiple physical layer features and machine learning for static scenarios in Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET). The scheme first trains and constructs the authentication model using multiple physical layer channel feature data and introduces data augmentation methods to enhance data diversity. This data augmentation strategy, combined with the multi-feature approach, significantly improves the effectiveness and richness of the feature data, thereby enhancing the stability and accuracy of the authentication model. Moreover, the scheme employs One-Class Support Vector Machine (OC-SVM) for the construction of the authentication model, which is trained solely on data from legitimate vehicles. This not only effectively reduces the training overhead of the model but also aligns more closely with the needs of real-world application scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme performs excellently in terms of authentication effectiveness, stability, and robustness, while also having low overhead, thus verifying its feasibility and superiority in static VANETs scenarios.

articleTitle: A Visual SLAM System in Dynamic Environments Based on ORB-SLAM3
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Vision SLAM has remained a central problem in robotics in recent years. Traditional vision SLAM methods often assume a static environment, but dynamic environments are more common in real-world scenarios. In dynamic environments, static assumptions often pose many challenges, such as feature point tracking, map construction, and accuracy degradation in localization. This paper presents a visual SLAM system for dynamic environments, built on ORB-SLAM3. An additional target detection thread is introduced alongside the original three threads to identify dynamic objects, enhancing system accuracy. First, the improved YOLOv7 is used to detect and remove dynamic feature points in the scene in real time, and then integrates semantic information, depth data, and optical flow to detect dynamic regions and filter out dynamic feature points., which assists the system in localization and map building. We validate our algorithm on TUM dataset and Bonn dataset respectively, and the results demonstrate that our algorithm provides higher localization accuracy and greater robustness than the original ORB-SLAM3.

articleTitle: An anchor-free drogue tracking network based on Shufflenet V2
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To solve the issue of tracking the refueling drogue in aerial refueling, a lightweight anchor-free drogue tracking network is developed in this paper. It is based on Shufflenet V2 and belongs to the twin network framework. According to the translation invariance needs of the twin network in the feature extraction stage, along with the Shffulenet lightweight network, a feature extraction network for the refueling drogue is created. The overall step size of this feature extraction network is 8, and the receptive field of the output feature makes up $68.5 \%$ of the template image, which is in line with the design standard of the typical twin network. Following the idea of Ocean/Ocean++, an anchor-free architecture is adopted by the network. Dilated convolutions in different directions are employed to mimic the anchor frames with diverse aspect ratios preset in the anchor frame network, guaranteeing the network’s responsiveness to different scales. Tests reveal that the network strikes a good equilibrium between precision and real-time operation, fulfilling the design prerequisites of the drogue tracking network.

articleTitle: Research on Interactive Network Traffic Anomaly Detection Method with Advice Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In modern networks facing increasing cyberattacks, the design of accurate and efficient methods for identifying and classifying anomalous traffic is of significant research value and practical importance. However, data-driven detection models often struggle to adapt to complex and dynamic network environments. Interactive learning can effectively improve the learning speed and convergence of algorithms by incorporating human feedback or advice into the learning process. In this paper, we propose an interactive network traffic anomaly detection method with advice fusion. It formulates the network traffic anomaly detection task as a Markov Decision Process and uses the Double Deep Q-Network algorithm to train the agent, where appropriate human advice is introduced into the procedure to accelerate model learning and convergence. Experiments on the NSL-KDD and AWID datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other learning-based approaches, particularly in detecting rare and hard-to-identify anomaly traffic types. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different thresholds on human interventions and the model’s performance. The results show that as the threshold and the amount of human advice increase, the detection performance significantly improves.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification via Improved Convolutional Neural Network with Spectral-Spatial Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: paper proposes a hyperspectral image classification method based on an improved Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combined with an enhanced Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism. The method effectively extracts spectral-spatial features through deep convolutional layers, while the enhanced SE module integrates multi-scale pooling and spatial attention to dynamically adjust the weights of spectral and spatial features, enhancing the model’s focus on critical information. To address the class imbalance problem in hyperspectral datasets, Gaussian noise injection and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) are introduced, improving the model’s robustness and generalization capability. Extensive experiments conducted on the Indian Pines, Pavia University, and Salinas datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves classification accuracies of $95.75 \%, 98.88 \%$, and 97.84%, with mean average precision (mAP) values of $89.41 \%, 99.33 \%$, and 93.12%, respectively. Compared to traditional CNNs and other classic methods, the proposed method shows significant advantages in classifying complex and similar categories, validating the effectiveness of combining spectral-spatial features with attention mechanisms.The proposed approach provides a new technical direction for hyperspectral image classification, offering substantial potential for improving classification accuracy and addressing class imbalance issues in high-dimensional data.

articleTitle: Research on Real-time and Non-real-time Task Core Division and Collaborative Processing Technology for Distribution Network Monitoring and Control Chip
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of smart grids, the complexity of tasks in distribution network monitoring and control systems has been continuously increasing. Efficiently handling real-time and non-real-time tasks has become a key factor in improving system performance. This paper addresses the real-time and non-real-time task scheduling problem of distribution network monitoring and control chips in a multi-core architecture and proposes an optimized solution based on multi-core collaborative processing. By allocating tasks between real-time cores and non-real-time cores, and combining Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) with Linux operating system, task priority scheduling and resource allocation are achieved. Furthermore, the impact of inter-core collaboration mechanisms on system performance is explored, proposing optimization solutions for shared memory and message mailbox mechanisms. A comparative analysis of communication delay, bandwidth utilization, and data consistency under different mechanisms is conducted. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves system response time, task completion rate, and stability under high-load conditions, providing effective technical support for the efficient operation of distribution network monitoring systems.

Author Keywords: Distribution Network Monitoring and Control Chip

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain-Based Multispectral Pedestrian Detection Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In numerous all-weather applications, multi-modal pedestrian detection has been widely adopted, notably in autonomous driving and video surveillance. Exploiting the complementary strengths of different modalities is one of the most effective ways to enhance detection performance. However, misalignment in the spatial domain and variability in modality reliability can hinder robust cross-modal feature extraction, thereby limiting the potential of multi-modal pedestrian detection.To address these issues, this paper proposes a cross-modal object detection method based on unregistered optical and infrared images, termed the Frequency-Domain-Based Multispectral Pedestrian Detection Network (FD-MPedNet). Specifically, we design a Multi-Scale Channel-Spatial (MSCS) module that leverages deformable convolutions and multi-scale convolution operations to effectively capture edge information and extract features across different spatial scales, while preserving channel priors to avoid disregarding their inherent feature distributions. Additionally, we introduce an Adaptive Frequency Domain Feature Fusion (AFDFF) module, wherein the frequency bands of different modalities are decomposed to fuse low-frequency components for global information exchange, while retaining the original high-frequency features to enhance the model’ s sensitivity to object pixels. Experimental results on the challenging KAIST dataset demonstrate that the proposed FD-MPedNet achieves outstanding performance.

articleTitle: Utilizing Large Language Models for Quality Enhancement of Text Annotation Data: A Chain of Thought Reasoning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Large language models (LLMS) have shown great potential for automating and improving the quality of data annotation. This study proposes a quality improvement pipeline, which combines Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning with supervised fine-tuning (Effective fine-tuning by Parameters (PEFT) strategies) to address the common problem of inconsistencies and inaccuracies in the annotations generated by LLMS. The pipeline consists of task-specific tag acquisition, guided inference generation for tag proof, targeted fine-tuning, and sequential evaluation and filtering to guarantee the quality of multidimensional annotations. Using a distributed multi-GPU setup, inference accuracy is improved when the method is evaluated on a modified cmre2018 dataset, and the sucess rate goes from a benchmark of 55.1 percent to more than 80 percent. This shows the efficiency of the pipeline in enhancing the LLM-based annotation process, and it also highlights the potential of llm to simplify and improve annotation quality for complex dataintensive tasks.

articleTitle: Fusion of Masked Attention Mechanism and Multi-Granularity Labels for Thangka Image-Text Matching
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a unique painting art, Thangka has been included in the list of intangible cultural heritage. The digital protection and research of Thangka has important social and practical significance for the development, inheritance and innovative development of national culture. This paper combines attention mechanism and multi-granularity label, and studies the Thangka image-text matching method with 30 common Thangkas of different themes as the research object. This paper proposes a novel image-text matching structure that integrates mask attention mechanism and multi-granularity label. The structure has the following improvements: 1) A named entity recognition model for Thangka text is designed to more fully mine the structure and semantic information of the text; 2) The traditional attention mechanism is improved, a mask layer is added, and the multi-label matching process is completed for the processing of unrelated data; 3) A new way of mapping images and texts. Comparative experiments and ablation experiments were conducted on the proposed method. It was found that the recall rate of the proposed method in image matching text and text matching image was improved by $3.8 \%$ and $4.9 \%$ respectively on the Thangka dataset compared with other methods. The recall rate on the Flickr30k dataset was better than all traditional VSE models in two matching tasks. The performance is not inferior to the current pre-trained models that require large-scale data training, which shows that our model works well on different data sets.

articleTitle: Technical Practice of Integrating Real-Time Interactive Modules for Networked Co-Creation Communities—Example of YS’s Meta-Universe Platform Project
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to enhance the efficiency of user interaction in virtual social and creative space, the technical practice of the real-time interaction module of online co-creation community is analysed by taking the meta-universe platform of YS Company as an example. The study shows that the integration of the Unity engine, RVC audio-voice model and distributed system architecture successfully achieves low-latency and high-precision data synchronisation in a highly concurrent environment. Test results show that the platform maintains a frame rate of $\geq 60 \mathrm{fps}$ and a data synchronisation error of $\leq 5 \mathrm{~ms}$ under low-concurrency environments; under high concurrency, the frame rate is stable at more than 50 fps and the system load is moderate. The crossplatform adaptation test shows that the response time of a PC device is 95 ms, the rendering frame rate is 60 fps, and the compatibility score is 5 points; the response time of mobile device and VR device is 120 ms and 150 ms respectively, the rendering frame rate is 50 fps and 45 fps respectively, and the compatibility score is 4 points. The stability of the system is good on all platforms, meeting the demand for efficient interaction and real-time response.

articleTitle: Instruction and Demonstration-based service attribute Mining mechanism for textual data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Attribute-based access control is fundamentally dependent on the service attribute calibration of object sources. Traditionally, the calibration of service attribute for textual data has been primarily reliant on human experts and machine learning methods, yet the efficiency and few-shot ability are insufficient. Thus, a service attribute mining mechanism for textual data, termed IDM, has been introduced. This mechanism addresses the aforementioned challenges by transforming the extraction of service attribute, previously a sequence-calibrated problem, into a controllable-generation problem through instruction learning and in-context learning. The service attribute extraction component of the proposed mechanism achieved an optimal average F1 score in few-shot experiments on the CoNLL2003 dataset, surpassing the baseline model. This positions the mechanism as state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: A Java EE layered architecture for domain driven design
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of software business, the traditional layered architecture based on MVC mode gradually exposes the shortcomings of tight coupling of service layer logic, difficult maintenance and expansion. To solve the above problems, the paper proposes a 4-tier architecture model based on DDD+ESSSDJ framework. This architecture takes domain driven design as the methodology, and designs the domain model layer around the system business. The presentation layer is established with Element UI, and the controller is realized through Spring MVC. Spring Data JDBC+MinIOService+AuthService is used to interact with the infrastructure layer, and Spring is used to integrate the application layer, domain layer and infrastructure layer. Based on the application background of the target assessment system of colleges and universities, the strategic design part focuses on the division of fields and the establishment of a ubiquitous language. In the tactical design phase, the design and implementation process of the domain model is described in detail around the indicator domain. Finally, it shows the partial implementation effect of the target assessment system. The practice results show that the domain driven design method can reasonably guide the establishment of the business model, avoid the coupling state formed by the core logic scattered in the Service layer, and the application of related frameworks can improve the efficiency of system development.

articleTitle: Machine learning-based data-driven modeling of deep-sea mining vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study proposes a data-driven modeling method for mining vehicle motion that aims to address the limitations of traditional methods and the challenges of adaptability to real-world environments.
