The proposed approach utilizes the APSO-XGBoost enhanced fusion algorithm, training a data-driven model with experimental data from the RecurDyn simulation. The model is optimized using data enhancement techniques, highlighting the differential speed data features and integrating the APSO algorithm. A comparison of the proposed method with traditional approaches reveals its superiority in predicting the speed and angular velocity of the mining vehicle. This provides a novel foundation for the intelligent control of deep-sea mining vehicles.

articleTitle: Slibfs: Towards Small Write Optimization in Per-File Virtualization NVM-based Filesystems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Non-volatile memory (NVM) technologies can provide both data persistence and high performance at memory level. However, prevalent kernel-based and userspace filesystems alike fall short in adequately addressing the challenges posed by small writes, despite the dominance of small write operations as revealed by analyses of modern filesystem workloads. These previous filesystems either compromise on write consistency or resort to Copy-on-Write methodologies, which incur substantial write amplification. In this paper, we propose a small write optimization method for NVM and implemented a prototype Slibfs. Leveraging an evolved per-file virtualization design, Slibfs innovates with write transaction isolation strategies, separating transactions by type to handle varying write sizes optimally. It further incorporates a Journal-Log decoupling structure to segregate write payload from transaction metadata, and establishes a dedicated pipeline for small write transactions (S Write Tx), ensuring rapid and consistent write operations. Extensive evaluations confirm Slibfs’s effectiveness, exhibiting a 2.25x remarkable throughput improvement over MadFS, specifically for small write scenarios. Hence, Slibfs marks a pivotal step towards realizing high-performance, reliable NVM filesystems that adeptly cater to the unique challenges of small write workloads.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Optimization-Based Load Balancing Scheduling Algorithm for Flink Tasks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issues of resource usage imbalance and throughput bottlenecks caused by Flink’s default scheduling strategy, a balanced scheduling algorithm based on Simulated Annealing and Particle Swarm Optimization (SA-PSOBS) is proposed. First, by real-time collection of task monitoring and load metrics, the scheduling results are dynamically adjusted, resolving the weight deficiency problem of static scheduling strategies. Second, a two-stage optimization approach is adopted: in the Task-to-Slot allocation phase, the Simulated Annealing algorithm is used to optimize resource load balancing among Slots; in the Slot-to-TaskManager allocation phase, the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm is employed to balance resource differences among TaskManagers. Additionally, a Slots waiting mechanism is introduced, combined with weighted fitness calculations based on feature matrices of tasks, Slots, and TaskManagers, to further optimize global resource allocation. Experiments conducted on the NASA-HTTP-LOG dataset and WordCount job show that for a job with 100 tasks, throughput increases by $9.673 \%$ under globally consistent parallelism and by 41.929% under non-consistent parallelism; for a job with 500 tasks, throughput increases by $10.919 \%$ under globally consistent parallelism and by $16.631 \%$ under non-consistent parallelism. The proposed algorithm effectively resolves resource imbalance and throughput bottlenecks, outperforming both the default scheduling strategy and the Round-Robin static load balancing algorithm.

articleTitle: A Latent Diffusion Model for Heart Sound Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: There are already many analyses of heart sounds used to develop diagnostic systems for the heart condition. However, the existing heart sound database state is not sufficient to train a large number of deep learning models and is not balanced – the normal heart sounds are always more present than abnormal heart sounds. Hence, we are interested in algorithms that can generate heart sounds as they can enhance the current database state. We enter the field of large-scale modelling in medical synthesis by proposing a latent diffusion model for heart sound generation, which can generate highly realistic heart sounds. We further guide the synthesis process through text prompts and labels, revealing the research field of prompted heart sound synthesis. In terms of experimental results, our proposed method achieves good results compared to existing mathematical models. At the same time, when the generated audio is used as an unlabelled dataset in semi-supervised learning, it shows an improvement effect on the classification model. This indicates that the heart sounds generated by the diffusion model bear great value.

articleTitle: An Improved Study of Fine-Grained Text Sentiment Analysis Based on Semantic Map Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The challenge of semantic dynamics and feature coupling difficulties in fine-grained sentiment analysis tasks. Therefore, we innovatively propose an improved framework based on dynamic semantic selection and multi-scale feature enhancement, i.e., RDGCN+ATOSS+GAT, which overcomes the challenge of hierarchical semantic representation of complex sentences and effectively solves the dilemma of parsing multiobjective sentiment conflicts by constructing an adaptive task oriented semantic selection module, ATOSS, and an attentional enhancement architecture of graphs, GAT. The experimental results show that the improved model performs excellently on the fused dataset under the weighted evaluation system, with a weighted accuracy as high as 83.21% and a weighted F1 score of 78.65%. Compared with the baseline model RDGCN, the weighted accuracy is improved by 2.73% and the weighted F1 score by 4.73%, while the logarithmic loss is reduced by 10.94%. The advantages of ATOSS in handling long datasets are fully verified in the long-short dataset comparison experiments. The ablation experiments further confirm that the ATOSS module has a significant hierarchical semantic decoupling advantage in long text scenarios (3.82% reduction in weighted F1 scores), while the GAT module plays a central role in capturing fine-grained sentiment features by virtue of the multi-head attention mechanism (3.55% reduction in weighted F1 scores). With the help of a dynamic weight fusion strategy, the framework deftly balances the cross-domain generalisation capabilities and demonstrates excellent robustness in complex semantic scenarios such as contradictory modifier clauses. The method proposed in this study opens up a new technical paradigm in the field of opinion analysis, which is of great value in e-commerce review mining and opinion analysis applications.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Application of a Generative AI-Based Tilting Prediction Model for Ancient Buildings
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Ancient buildings, as an integral part of human cultural heritage, face tilting issues that not only affect their aesthetic appeal but may also lead to structural instability or even collapse, posing serious threats to building safety and human lives. Traditional monitoring methods rely on physical sensors and manual inspections, which suffer from limitations such as data scarcity, low prediction accuracy, and poor real-time performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes a generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based tilting prediction model for ancient buildings. By leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation, diverse combinations of tilting and contributing factor data are generated, effectively resolving the issue of data scarcity. The model adopts a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architecture, with inputs including contributing factors such as foundation settlement, vibration frequency, temperature, and humidity, and outputs including tilt angles and tilt rates, enabling accurate capture of complex nonlinear relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that the model significantly outperforms traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and generalization ability, and its effectiveness is validated through a real-world monitoring system. This study provides scientific and technical support for early warning and preventive conservation of ancient building tilting, offering significant theoretical value and practical application.

articleTitle: Meta-AGI: A Hierarchical Meta-Learning Framework for Generalizable Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Meta learning carries the hope of adaptation by Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents for novel tasks. However current meta-learning is not able to meet the need of generalising across diverse task distributions as well as the need for meeting sufficient learning dynamics. Here in this paper we propose Meta-Artificial General Intelligence (Meta-AGI). Meta-AGI is a hierarchical meta-learning framework developed to meet the requirements in generalization and efficiency which is achieved by the combination of three key components including Hierarchical Task Decomposition (HTD), Adaptive Meta-Optimization (AMO) and Structured Experience Replay (SER). In this paper we have provided theoretical analysis establishing generalization bounds and convergence rates as well as demonstrating superior performance across globally accepted multiple benchmarks consisting of Meta-World, Omniglot, Mini-ImageNet and MuJoCo. MetaAGI demonstrated a 15% improvement in few-shot accuracy on Meta-World by reducing the error rate from 31.8% to20.5% and a $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$ reduction in sample complexity which allowed faster learning with fewer data points and thus lowering computational overhead by approximately $10 \%$. These results established MetaAGI as the foundational framework for generalizable artificial intelligence. Meta-AGI demonstrated exceptional results in real-world applications showcasing its capacity beyond theoretical advances. In industrial robotics our Meta-AGI achieved a $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$ reduction in robot programming time and $65 \%$ improvement in task adaptation. In healthcare implementation our Meta-AGI showed92% diagnostic accuracy across diverse medical imaging tasks and in educational applications it demonstrated $\mathbf{4 5 \%}$ faster student learning rates. These results establish our Meta-AGI as the foundational framework for applied generalizable artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: FusionHLAII: A Hierarchical Model for Predicting HLA II–Peptide Interactions
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the field of immunotherapy for diseases, an accurate prediction of the binding of the HLA class II molecule to peptides is crucial for the development of effective vaccines and immunotherapies. We have developed a hierarchical deep learning model that innovatively combines amino acid physicochemical property encoding with advanced neural architectures, including the BiGRU and Transformer networks. The model captures temporal dependencies using BiGRU and leverages the multi-head self-attention mechanism in the Transformer to explore global interactions between HLA and peptides. Our model significantly improves the identification of key antigen-binding features, improving prediction accuracy and biological relevance. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to existing methods, our approach shows significant advantages in both prediction performance and mechanistic understanding, offering more precise immune-binding predictions and providing a powerful computational tool and new perspectives for immunological research. Codes are available at https://github. com/LinsLab/FusionHLAII.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Blockchain and Big Data Multimedia Visualization Technology in the Bidding Management of Scientific Research Projects
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of information technology and the advancement of globalization, the management model of scientific research projects has gradually transformed towards digitalization, informatization and visualization. Traditional scientific research project bidding management methods often rely on tools such as documents and static emails, which are difficult to meet the requirements of modern scientific research project management and bidding processes for efficiency, transparency, and real-time communication. Multimedia visualization technology, especially the application of technologies such as big data visualization, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR), provides innovative solutions for scientific research project management and bidding management. Starting from the basic process of scientific research project bidding management, this paper discusses in detail the application of multimedia visualization technology, including its role in project planning, schedule management, resource allocation, risk management, decision support and information transparency. By analyzing existing literature and actual application cases, this paper further explains how multimedia visualization technology can improve the efficiency of scientific research project management, enhance the transparency of the bidding process and optimize the decision-making process. Finally, the challenges and future development directions of the application of this technology are proposed.

articleTitle: Learning to Assemble Compositional Neural Modules for Visual Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Visual reasoning is one of the fundamental abilities of human intelligence. For multi-hop reasoning problems, Neural Module Network (NMN) explicitly incorporates the logical structure of the problems and reveals better flexibility and generalization ability compared with other monolithic models. However, applying each module to a routine limits the scalability of conventional NMNs when processing unseen question semantics. We notice that each routine has mostly three sub-routines: base routine, attribute, and module argument, and make each model concentrate on a sub-routine to make the execution of all routines in a disentangled way. Then, to better achieve the module functionality, we propose language feature filtering to extract the routine-specific features from the self-encoded language token features. The filtered language features are then fused with the hidden token features with cross-attention and MLP and the fused token features are the outputs of each module. Experimental results on CLOSURE and CLEVR-CoGenT reveal that the proposed Compositional NMN (CNMN) can achieve better performances compared with other NMNs with less number of modules, which further validates the effectiveness of learning compositional modules for multi-hop visual reasoning problems.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Traffic Flow Prediction with Dynamic FPGA Reconfiguration for Efficient Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Urban areas are in the face of persistent traffic congestion, which disrupts city running and hinders sustainability attempts. There is no doubt that accurate traffic paragon prediction is crucial for effective intelligent transportation systems to some extent. However, current methods are beset by two main challenges: inadequate modeling of intricate traffic dynamics and limited hardware capabilities at the edge.This study introduces MSTF-Net, a novel framework that integrates diverse neural network architectures using adaptive fusion techniques. We propose a two-layer filtering approach after thinking thoroughly: one layer leverages static geographic boundaries, while the other adapts to dynamic traffic conditions. In terms of the practical meaning, this method deeply enhances computational efficiency while preserving prediction accuracy. For the innovative part, we developed a variable-precision FPGA implementation for the BiLSTM component, expeditiously balancing computational accuracy and energy efficiency for real-world applications. Evaluations on the PEMSD4 dataset demonstrate that MSTF-Net outperforms existing approaches, achieving an RMSE of 28.2 for short-term predictions (15 minutes) and maintaining robust performance over longer times. Compared to traditional fixedprecision methods, the reconfiguration strategy for the BiLSTM module reduces energy consumption by 2.8 times. This optimized implementation achieves 5.6 times higher power efficiency, in contrast to equivalent GPU-based execution. This paper presents a comprehensive hardware-software co-design methodology, offering practical insights for developing efficient traffic systems, making it less affected by the constrained traffic resources.

articleTitle: A Discussion of The Generalization of The Central Projection Theorem in Fractional Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, electron microscope 3D reconstruction has gradually become the mainstream technology of structural biology. Fourier transform central projection theorem is an important tool in electron microscope 3D reconstruction. However, due to the mechanics of electron microscopy, it faces the challenge of what is known as a “missing wedge.” In this paper, we focus on discussing the “missing wedge” problem of 3D reconstruction from the field of image processing. A new mathematical tool, Fractional Fourier transform, is introduced into the 3D reconstruction technique of electron microscope. Combined with most existing methods, the difficulty of this idea is whether the central projection theorem can be generalized under fractional Fourier transform. The validity of the central projection theorem in Fractional Fourier transform is discussed in this paper. The process of discussion shows that the condition of this extension is strict, and attempts to analyze the reason why the theorem cannot be generalized from mathematical derivation. Combined with numerical results, the theoretical conclusions are further illustrated. It is worth noting that the strict generalization of the theorem does not mean that the fractional Fourier transform cannot be applied to three-dimensional reconstruction problems, only that some solutions are no longer used. To some extent, the new method based on fractional Fourier transform is proposed.

articleTitle: Acceleration of WRF Physical Parameterization Scheme YSU via OpenACC directives
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to improve the operational efficiency of the Weather Research and Forecast (WRF) model, the OpenACC instruction is used to accelerate the microphysics scheme embedded in the Weather Research and Forecast model. As one of the time-consuming physical parameterization schemes, the WRF Planetary Boundary Layer Microphysics Scheme (YSU) is parallelized to the graphics processing unit. Several methods were used to rewrite the original Fortran code to improve parallelism, including loop-in-shift, improved array dimensions, and so on. The transcoding tool GPUFORT is also applied to generate HIP C code for an explicit kernel that can be executed on a domestic accelerator. In addition, on this basis, the performance analysis is done and the merging kernel is optimized to reduce the time overhead of starting the kernel as much as possible. The project was tested by using multiple heterogeneous platforms including NVIDIA and domestic accelerators, as well as a variety of compilers, and the acceleration effects of different situations were compared. Experimental results show that under the premise of passing the correctness verification, the heterogeneous optimized version of YSU achieves a 19.90-fold acceleration on a single NVIDIA Tesla P100 accelerator card and a 17.33-fold acceleration on a single domestic accelerator. The acceleration effect of the domestic accelerator in the physical parameterization scheme reflects the successful application of the domestic accelerator in the WRF model.

articleTitle: Hybrid orbit endogenous secure satellite authentication technology
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Satellite Internet has the characteristics of wide-area coverage, flexible deployment, high bandwidth and low latency, which can cover remote areas that are hard to reach by terrestrial networks and provide Internet services. Aiming at the current problem that terminal access authentication is carried out locally at the gateway station, the service scope is limited and there is a single point of failure of the server, as well as the risk of centralised data leakage during the authentication process, this paper proposes a hybrid orbital endogenous security authentication technique combining GEO and LEO using the relative position invariance of GEO and the high efficiency of LEO data transmission to improve the robustness, scalability and security of the system. Simulation results show that the scheme has better delay and throughput performance while ensuring authentication security.

articleTitle: Grouped Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Consensus Mechanism Based on Node Behaviour Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the wide application of block-chain technology, Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) algorithm, as a classical consensus mechanism, has attracted attention due to its advantages in tolerating Byzantine faults. However, the PBFT algorithm faces challenges in practical applications such as Byzantine nodes may be selected as master nodes, high system communication overheads, and long consensus latency. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes a grouped Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus mechanism based on node behavioral analysis, named ABA-PBFT.Firstly, the mechanism constructs a node voting weight evaluation model by introducing a dynamic analysis of node behavior, and accumulating behavioral data based on node performances in the consensus process. Second, based on the performance values of the nodes, the nodes are divided into high-performance group (HPG), medium-performance group (MPG), and low-performance group (LPG), and the master node is randomly selected from the HPG group. Finally, according to the node grouping, the PBFT full consensus process is optimized in stages to reduce the communication overhead and consensus delay. Through simulation experiments, it is verified that ABA-PBFT significantly outperforms the traditional PBFT algorithm in key performance indicators such as consensus latency, throughput, communications overhead, which effectively reduces the risk of the system suffering from the Byzantine attack and enhances the security and stability of the block-chain system. The research in this paper provides a new idea and method for the optimization of block-chain consensus mechanism, which has a wide application prospect.

articleTitle: High Dynamic Range and High Precision Phase Resolution Algorithm Based on Dynamic Frequency Phase Locking
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As the core equipment for integrated circuit manufacturing, the multi-degree-of-freedom super-precision positioning technology of the photolithography machine's working table is the key to achieving nanometer-level pattern overlay accuracy. At the 14 -nanometer and below process nodes, the working table needs to maintain sub-nanometer-level positioning stability during high-speed scanning motion, which sets extremely high requirements for the dynamic accuracy and anti-interference ability of the displacement measurement system. Aiming at the phase-solving problem in heterodyne interferometric signal processing, this paper proposes a dynamic frequency-locked phase-locked algorithm. The innovation lies in the use of two groups of orthogonal and equally-spaced reference frequency signals ($3-37 \text{MHz}$, spaced 1 MHz) to mix with the input signal. The difference-frequency component is extracted by a low-pass filter (with a cutoff frequency of 500 kHz). Compared with traditional methods, the core innovation is the introduction of a dynamic frequency-switching mechanism. When the measurement signal frequency exceeds the ±500 kHz range of the current reference channel, it automatically switches to the adjacent reference frequency channel, achieving frequency tracking and maintaining phase continuity. To verify the algorithm's performance, an experimental platform based on a signal generator was built. The static test shows that the algorithm's phase fluctuation peak-to-peak is less than ±0.4 mrad, with a static standard deviation of 0.101 mrad (equivalent displacement of 8.04 pm), which is 4.9 times and 3.1 times better than that of the orthogonal phase-locked method (0.492 mrad) and the frequency-comb phase-locked method (0.318 mrad). In the 0.096 mrad step test, the system resolution reaches 7.63 pm. In the dynamic test, the dynamic standard deviation is below $0.75~\text{mrad} (59.7 \text{pm})$, verifying the algorithm’s robustness in high-speed and frequency-varying scenarios.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Auto-Vectorization via Relational Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the growing demand for energy efficiency in high-performance computing, traditional auto-vectorization heuristics face limitations due to their reliance on predefined rules and neglect of energy consumption, particularly for complex program structures and cross-platform adaptation. This paper proposes an energy-efficient auto-vectorization method using Relational Graph Convolutional Networks (RGCN) to address the limitations of heuristic compiler approaches in handling complex program structures and energy consumption optimization. By constructing code graph representations integrating control flow, data flow, and call flow, and training an RGCN model to predict Energy-Delay Product (EDP)-optimal vector widths, our method achieves significant improvements. Experimental results on two Intel Xeon platforms demonstrate EDP optimizations of 53.9% and 50.5% respectively compared to default configurations, outperforming rule-based models and validating its efficacy in handling complex code and cross-platform energy efficiency optimization.

articleTitle: Tomato planting environment monitoring and pest warning system based on Internet of Things and Huawei ModelArts
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the course of global agricultural modernization, smart agricultural systems have markedly enhanced crop production efficiency, minimized resource consumption, and advanced the development of environmentally friendly sustainable agriculture through precision perception, intelligent control, and remote management. This paper introduces a monitoring and early warning system for the tomato planting environment based on Internet of Things (IoT) technology and visual recognition technology. The system employs STM32 as the control core, integrates the ESP8266 communication module, OV7725 camera, and Huawei Cloud platform, and leverages deep learning technologies to achieve real-time monitoring of the tomato growing environment and intelligent early warning of insect pests. The system collects key parameters such as air temperature and humidity, light intensity, and soil moisture in real time via sensors, utilizes the Huawei ModelArts platform to train disease identification models, and provides remote data interaction and early warning services through WeChat mini programs. As a result, the system is capable of significantly mitigating yield losses caused by insect pests, thereby enhancing the productivity of tomato cultivation.

articleTitle: The application of edge artificial intelligence in the Internet of Battlefield Things
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper systematically discusses the indispensable role and technical pathways of edge artificial intelligence (AI) in the Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT). Considering the high real-time, dynamic, and security demands of the battlefield environment, a hierarchical collaborative architecture design based on “terminal layer - intelligent edge layer - cloud layer” is proposed, and its practical value is analyzed in scenarios such as real-time situational awareness, autonomous weapon control, and soldier health monitoring. By addressing core challenges like heterogeneous device management, low-latency response, and robustness assurance, solutions for dynamic resource allocation, lightweight model deployment, and intelligent spectrum management are provided. Lastly, the security threats and defense strategies of edge intelligence are analyzed, building an integrated military-grade security architecture of “detection-response-recovery”. This paper provides theoretical support and technical reference for the practical deployment of edge AI empowering the IoBT.

articleTitle: Time Synchronization Method for Wireless Sensor Networks Based on Adaptive Synchronization Period Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Clock synchronization is paramount in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) for critical applications such as data dissemination and network management. Inherent fabrication variances lead to disparate clock’s oscillator characteristics among sensor nodes. Consequently, real-time clock state tracking and compensation become imperative. To minimize communication overhead and optimize energy consumption, this paper introduces an Adaptive Synchronization Period Kalman Filter (ASP-KF), an innovative adaptive synchronization protocol leveraging Kalman filtering theory. The proposed algorithm implements a two-way message exchange mechanism for timestamp acquisition and employs an adaptive estimation filter for clock state tracking. By considering the time synchronization precision specifications outlined in the IEEE 802.15.4 standard, a synchronization interval adaptation function is formulated. Extensive simulation experiments corroborate that ASP-KF maintains superior performance under diverse initial conditions and dynamic operational scenarios.

articleTitle: Hospital Scene Object Detection with Integrated Lightweight Convolutions and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Object detection, a critical technology in robotic vision, has seen widespread adoption in various applications, especially in robot navigation and obstacle avoidance. Nevertheless, traditional algorithms struggle in dynamic hospital environments, exhibiting high rates of false positives, missed detections, and poor performance on small or occluded targets. The large model sizes further complicate deployment on mobile platforms, limiting real-world utility. To overcome these limitations, we present a hospital-specific pedestrian detection framework based on YOLOv11. Our methodology features three main contributions: First, we replace the C3k2 Bottleneck with GhostConv, significantly reducing model complexity. Second, we integrate GhostConv with ECA attention to form the GhostECA module, improving feature extraction capabilities without increasing parameters. Third, we introduce a dedicated small object detection layer and a CCAR module for enhanced multiscale feature handling. Extensive experiments on the HosSceneDet, KITTI, and SODA10M datasets validate our approach: the optimized S model achieves $94.8 \% \mathrm{mAP}\text{@} 0.5$ on KITTI $(1.7 \%$ improvement), while the N model reduces parameters by $32.1 \%$. These advancements demonstrate superior performance and practicality compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Improved Parameter Estimation Methods in the Post-Processing Phase of Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In the post-processing phase of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), a crucial step involves the parameter estimation of the initial key. Among various techniques, the group parity check method stands out as a prevalent approach for parameter estimation. This method operates by segmenting the received key into groups and applying parity checks within each group to estimate the bit error rate. Theoretically, this method can achieve high precision estimation with minimal information leakage compared to traditional random sampling methods. However, the practical efficiency and estimation accuracy of this method are contingent upon the group size and the statistical properties of the errors, which sometimes may not yield superior results relative to conventional methods. This paper introduces an enhanced group parity check method, which incorporates an additional parity code comparison and employs a dynamic group strategy, effectively reducing information leakage in subsequent error correction steps caused by erroneous estimations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed parameter estimation method can more accurately estimate and correct errors occurring during the QKD physical process and dynamically optimize the key generation process according to actual communication conditions.

articleTitle: EIED: A Curated Dataset for Knowledge Extraction in Electronic Information Equipment Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As a core task in web data mining, knowledge extraction holds significant application value in knowledge graph construction. Addressing the lack of domain-specific features in existing public datasets for electronic information equipment applications, this study proposes a domain-specific dataset construction methodology based on a collaborative framework of “multi-source collection, heterogeneous processing, and semantic annotation.” We successfully developed EIED, a specialized dataset for electronic information equipment. This dataset integrates multi-modal heterogeneous data sources, including technical literature, documentation, equipment parameters, and industry reports, forming a structured corpus of $200,000-$ character scale after semantic cleansing and expert annotation. Experimental validation employed a bidirectional comparative mechanism: BERT, BERT-LSTM, and BERT-BiLSTM hybrid models were tested on both EIED and generic datasets for named entity recognition and relation extraction tasks. Results demonstrate that models trained with EIED significantly outperform those using generic datasets in both entity recognition and relation extraction. This research establishes a high-quality data foundation for subsequent knowledge extraction and graph-based development in electronic information equipment applications.

articleTitle: Research on College Students' Mental Health Issues Based on an Improved BiLSTM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rise in concerns about the declining mental health of college students, the traditional methods used for evaluation are proving to be unreliable and time-consuming when it comes to providing accurate results. The work revolves around a novel bidirectional long short-term memory neural network (BiLSTM), which is aimed at creating a robust model for the early detection of mental health problems. In this study, we present the BiLSTM+AM model where the attention mechanism is included and different parameter optimization techniques are used to make the model more sensitive to the mood of the emotional text. Besides, we tried to work with data normalization and feature selection as the direct ways of model enhancements. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that the enhanced model outclasses ordinary models in the aspects of accuracy, recall, and F1 score, which are instrumental in the identification of potential mental illness risks and offer a surviving ground for mental health interventions in higher education. Furthermore, the paper provides advances in the method of intelligent psychiatric evaluation and college student studies, and it also presents prospects for future research in relevant fields.

articleTitle: Porting C++containers based on domestic heterogeneous platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the development of the times, the demand for high-performance computing power is also increasing, and heterogeneous computing collaborative parallel computing has become an important development direction of computing technology. In recent years, domestic heterogeneous platforms have flourished, and it is of great significance to transplant and develop suitable algorithms and software for the architecture of domestic heterogeneous platforms. The C++Standard Template Library (STL) is an important component of the C++programming language, providing a series of universal and reusable template classes and functions that can help developers better develop software. In terms of STL heterogeneous porting, the progress of domestic heterogeneous platforms lags far behind NVIDIA, which hinders the development of heterogeneous computing in China. Therefore, this article migrates commonly used containers in STL to broaden the adaptation range of domestic heterogeneous software. By porting several iconic containers, a solution for container heterogeneous porting is proposed, providing a reference method for STL heterogeneous porting. The final experiment showed that compared to non heterogeneous operations, this scheme significantly improves the performance of heterogeneous porting of containers in large data volumes. At the same time, it also has a huge improvement in the performance of internal operation functions of containers compared to the original STL parallel operation method.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor MRI Clustering Algorithm Based on Nearest Neighbor Prior Variational Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate detection of brain tumors is crucial for early diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the high-dimensional complexity of medical images, intra-tumor heterogeneity, and imaging noise limit the effectiveness of traditional clustering methods in MRI analysis. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an improved Variational Autoencoder (VAE)-based clustering algorithm that integrates knowledge self-distillation and a nearest neighbor prior to enhance feature learning and clustering semantic consistency. Additionally, we design medical image-specific data augmentation strategies to improve model robustness. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing deep clustering algorithm based VAE in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and clustering accuracy for brain tumor MRI images. This work holds promise for applications in brain tumor detection and related medical tasks.

articleTitle: Analysis of User Satisfaction of The SAP Application Using the PIECES Framework Method : Case Study of PT Domas Agrointi Prima
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the level of user satisfaction with SAP applications at PT Domas Agrointi Prima using the PIECES (Performance, Information, Economics, Control, Efficiency, and Services) methodology. In addition to technological advancements, the SAP application used in product procurement in this organization is plagued by various problems, including slow period opening and closing processes and its dependence on a reliable internet connection. This motivated management to assess the efficacy of the system in facilitating product procurement transactions. This study used a quantitative methodology. This study used probability sampling to produce a total of 258 respondents as a sample. Using a questionnaire for data collection and Partial Least Square (SmartPls) for data analysis, the four hypotheses proposed in this study were tested. Performance, information, economy, control and security, efficiency, and services are factors that influence user satisfaction with SAP applications at PT. Domas Agrointi Prima, according to the research findings. In an effort to improve user satisfaction with SAP applications at PT Domas Agrointi Prima, optimizing application performance through technology updates and more structured system maintenance is the right choice. Furthermore, the quality of application information should be a primary concern. Companies can assess the application process and identify unnecessary steps. On the service side, it is necessary to offer solution-oriented and responsive technical support. With the ability to immediately resolve user issues, PT Domas Agrointi Prima can form a helpdesk team that can be accessed around the clock. And finally, it is important for organizations to involve consumers in the application development process.

articleTitle: A Time-Aware Mutual Information Feature Selection and LGA-Driven Approach for ICMPv6 DDoS Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As the IPv6 protocol gains extensive deployment, ICMPv6—its core element in network configuration and route discovery—has emerged as a high-risk target for distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. Conventional ICMPv6 DDoS detection strategies often fail to balance precision and timeliness when faced with high-dimensional traffic and intricate temporal patterns. In response, we propose a detection framework integrating Time-Aware Mutual Information (TMI) feature selection with an LSTM-GRU-Attention (LGA) hybrid model for ICMPv6 DDoS attacks. By applying TMI within sliding windows, we compute and average the mutual information between features and attack labels, effectively reducing feature dimensionality while preserving temporal correlations. The resulting subset of critical features is then input into the LGA model, which leverages LSTM and GRU in parallel to capture both long-and short-term dependencies, while a self-attention module provides enhanced global context. Our experiments indicate that, relative to conventional feature selection and detection approaches, the proposed method achieves substantial gains in accuracy and F1 score, with a marked decrease in inference delay, thus satisfying the real-time defense requirements in IPv6 network environments.

articleTitle: Measuring Nozzle Image Area Using Deep Learning and Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Nozzle characteristics of aircraft engines are one of the important indicators for measuring their performance. It is necessary to conduct measurement and analysis in order to obtain the performance parameters of the nozzle. This paper proposes a measurement method for nozzle images. This method is based on YOLO V11 object detection and GrabCut image segmentation techniques, and mainly includes the following points: To enhance the YOLO V11 model, we utilize the re-parameterization module, RepConv, to improve its C3k2 module, and thus propose the RepC3k2 module. This allows the model to have better feature representation capabilities during the training process. A loss function based on MPDIoU with better convergence properties is introduced to optimize the model’s training process. A dual attention mechanism, CBAM, is added to the backbone network of the model to improve its accuracy and robustness during detection. A novel method for measuring the area of a nozzle image is proposed: utilizing GrabCut image segmentation and image processing techniques to segment the nozzle image, and then obtaining the area based on the proportion of image pixels. Finally, experiments were conducted to verify the reliability and accuracy of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: KPI Anomaly Detection Method for Multi-Scale Feature Fusion in Time-Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: KPI anomaly detection is a key task in the field of intelligent operation and maintenance. Existing methods are based on time series anomaly detection, which have the problem of weak feature extraction ability in operation and maintenance scenarios, especially the insufficient utilization of frequency domain information. This paper proposes an unsupervised KPI anomaly detection method based on multi-scale feature fusion in timefrequency domain for intelligent operation and maintenance of data center. In this method, the one-dimensional convolutional neural network with different scales convolution kernels is configured to extract the multi-scale features in time domain and frequency domain respectively, and the cross-domain attention fusion module is used to realize the dynamic weighted interaction of time-frequency features, so as to enhance the feature expression ability. The variational autoencoder is used to reconstruct the time series data, and anomalies are determined by the reconstruction probability. Experimental results on three real server KPI datasets show that the proposed method achieves the best recall rate and F1 value compared with other baseline methods, and the F1 value is $0.95,0.97$ and 0.94, respectively. It is worth noting that the introduction of frequency domain features significantly improves the recall rate, which is $0.98,0.96$ and 0.96, respectively, which verifies the key role of frequency domain information in KPI anomaly detection, and provides an effective solution to the problem of weak feature extraction ability of existing methods.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Respiratory Waveform Recovery Based on Millimetre-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Respiratory signs, as key vital signs, play an essential role in long-term monitoring for the diagnosis of respiratory-related diseases. In respiratory sign monitoring, which recovers fine-grained respiratory waveforms rather than just predicting respiratory rate, this fine-grained respiratory volume data provides valuable insights into disease physiology. However, conventional signal processing methods can only obtain coarse respiratory waveforms, and recent methods using variational encoder-decoder architectures suffer from training instability, leading to pattern collapse. To address these issues, we propose an encoder-decoder architecture based on residual adaptive multi-scale LSTM, which enables more stable training, generates finer respiratory waveforms, and further improves the accuracy of predicting respiratory rate. Experimental results show that the method in this paper outperforms the baseline when compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: ADKG-LLM: Construction of Agricultural Disease Knowledge Graph with Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The transformation of information storage methods has prompted the construction of targeted knowledge bases to become crucial. Traditional knowledge management suffers from low efficiency and poor scalability. With the development of agricultural intelligence, a disease detection and prevention Q&A system based on knowledge graphs has emerged. Knowledge graphs can structurally store heterogeneous data and construct semantic connections of diseases. The construction methods of knowledge graphs have become a hotspot in natural language processing, but they require a large amount of manually annotated data. The emergence of LLMs(Large Language Models) provides new ideas for the construction of knowledge graphs, reducing the dependence on manual annotation. This study proposes the ADKG-LLM(Agricultural Disease Knowledge Graph) method, which utilizes LLMs to analyze agricultural disease texts, automatically extract entities and relationships to construct knowledge graphs, and perfects them through Lora fine-tuning. In the experiments, data from professional literature were collected using web crawlers and character recognition, cleaned, and then used for few-shot prompting and fine-tuning of LLMs. The results show that GPT-4 performs best in the named entity recognition task, followed by GPT-3.5, and Llama3-8B outperforms Llama2-7B, indicating that GPT series models outperform the LLAMA series in the construction of Chinese agricultural pest and disease knowledge graphs. Compared with traditional models, LLMs perform better in Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Relation Extraction (RE) tasks. Moreover, this method is not only applicable to the field of agricultural pests and diseases, but can also be extended to the construction of knowledge graphs in other fields, saving human effort and time.

articleTitle: Towards Informative Text Compression: A Linguistically guided Self-Information Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Though Large Language Models (LLMs) have proven effective in the realm of Natural Language Processing (NLP), their application on long text has been hindered by huge computation cost. To meet this challenge, text compression reduce the input length by selectively removing text units, serving as a promising solution. However, current text compression methods suffer from ignoring linguistic information, resulting in missing linguistically important text units and degraded downstream task performance. To solve this problem, we introduce a novel text compression method based on linguistically guided self-information, where the self-information of text units are rescaled as importance score by linguistic features. Then, the text units with low importance score are removed, allowing LLMs to process the most linguistically and semantically important sequence. Experimental results on Natural Questions and Trivia QA datasets show our method outperforms competitive Selective Context and LLMLingua methods in terms of EM scores, balancing compression and retention well with strong performance and adaptability.

articleTitle: DSBU-Net: Dual-stream branch union network for Image manipulation localization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Image manipulation detection and localization is a hot topic in the field of computer forensics, but with the development of image editing technology, it is easier to tamper with images. Although previous work has attempted to capture features from the noise views to explore the noise inconsistency between authentic and forgery regions with some success, more efficient fusion methods are still being explored. To address this problem, a dual-stream branch union network (DSBU-Net) for image forgery localization is proposed. Firstly, an end-to-end DSBU-Net network structure is designed to jointly capture the features of both RGB view and noise view. Secondly, in order to make the network model focus on the inconsistency between the authentic and forgery regions, as well as to suppress the impact of semantic information on localization, the extracted noise is encoded by the noise branch encoder to obtain noise features. Next, the RGB features processed by the RGB branch encoder are input into the designed dual-stream fusion module based on the selfattention mechanism to obtain the fused features. Finally, the forgery regions are localized by inputting through the skip connection into the RGB decoder. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms current popular methods on datasets such as CASIA, COVERAGE, and NIST16. At the same time, the effectiveness of the dual-stream fusion module has been proven through ablation experiments.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning: Cryptographic Techniques and Development Frontiers
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The rapid evolution of data privacy regulations and the growing demand for secure machine learning (ML) deployments have driven significant advancements in privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML) methodologies. This paper provides a systematic review of cryptographic techniques and architectural innovations. We categorize state-of-the-art approaches into three domains: traditional ML algorithms (e.g., linear regression, k-means clustering, SVMs), two-party/multi-party deep learning protocols, and hardware-accelerated secure inference frameworks. A key focus lies on the integration of quantized neural networks (QNNs), particularly binarized neural networks (BNNs), with secure multi-party computation (SMPC) to optimize computational and communication efficiency. Experimental evaluations on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that tripartite BNN protocols achieve up to 43% latency reduction and 62% lower communication overhead compared to full-precision baselines, albeit with accuracy tradeoffs proportional to quantization intensity. Hardware optimizations, including CUDA-accelerated cryptographic primitives and modular GPU platforms like Piranha, further enhance scalability for complex models. Our analysis underscores the viability of hybrid solutions combining quantization, SMPC, and hardware acceleration to balance privacy guarantees with practical performance in edge computing and distributed intelligence scenarios.

articleTitle: Efficient Additive 3D Modeling from Single Images via Layered Morphing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: A novel technique for single-image-driven rapid additive 3D modeling is presented, integrating principles of 3D printing with topological relationships between adjacent layers. By incorporating innovative curve morphing techniques, efficient transformation from a single image to complex three-dimensional models is achieved. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that superior performance in modeling efficiency, geometric accuracy, and visual fidelity is attained, particularly for regular geometric shapes and transitional forms. While potential for refinement in detailed reconstruction of complex cultural artifacts is noted, competitive overall results are still observed. Compared to traditional manual modeling, significant enhancements in speed are realized, while high levels of accuracy and appearance similarity are maintained, and data requirements along with computational complexity are substantially reduced. Practical solutions for rapid product design, digital heritage preservation, and augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR) applications are provided, with optimized layer structuring and topological control addressing precision limitations inherent in deep learning approaches. This research advances the field of 3D modeling by offering a robust, efficient framework with broad theoretical and practical implications.

articleTitle: Pose-Depth Joint Optimization and Adaptive Sampling for Self-Supervised Multi-Frame Depth Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Self-supervised multi-frame depth estimation encodes geometric information of different depths by constructing a Cost Volume and provides geometric priors for multi-frame depth estimation by minimizing the matching cost. However, existing methods overlook the potential impact of inter-view pose estimation errors and depth sampling ranges on the quality of geometric priors, which limits matching accuracy. In this paper, we propose an optimization strategy that combines the wide-baseline constraint in monocular depth estimation with the cyclic consistency constraint in visual odometry to alleviate the issue of cumulative errors between views and improve the matching quality of the multi-frame Cost Volume. Additionally, to address the limitations of traditional fixed-range sampling, this paper adaptively adjusts the sampling width of the Cost Volume based on the uncertainty of monocular depth estimation, reducing the interference from similarly textured regions. The experimental results show that on the KITTI dataset, our method achieves significant improvements: compared to ManyDepth and MoveDepth, our method improves the Abs Rel metric by 14.3% and 5.4%.

articleTitle: Deep learning Based Topology Optimization of Marine Satellite-to-Ground Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Network topology affects important network performance metrics including link utilization, reliability, high energy consumption and delay. In this paper, we propose a deep learning based and with the assistance of MEC to optimize the topology of marine satellite-to-ground network. By combining graph neural network (GAT) and multi-objective optimization strategies, the key issues in the design of marine network topology are addressed. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods in terms of reduced network latency, reduced energy consumption and improved reliability.

articleTitle: Generative Prediction of Severe Convection Events Using Satellite Imagery and Diffusion-U-Net Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Severe convection events pose significant hazards and demand accurate prediction for effective mitigation. Traditional forecasting methods often struggle with the high resolution and specificity required for such phenomena. This study leverages generative modeling to enhance the prediction of severe convection using satellite imagery. In this work, we purpose an Integrated Convection Events Prediction Framework (ICEPF) that leverages advanced satellite imagery and cutting-edge machine learning techniques to enhance the prediction and analysis of severe weather phenomena. The ICEPF combines a diffusion-based generative model for predicting future satellite imagery, a fine-tuned ESRGAN model for enhancing image resolution, and a MobileNet-SegNet-based semantic segmentation model for identifying cumulus clouds. By integrating these models, our framework offers a powerful tool for forecasting severe convection with improved accuracy and detail. Our results indicate that combining generative diffusion models with advanced segmentation techniques can provide a robust framework for forecasting severe weather conditions, offering potential enhancements over traditional meteorological methods.

articleTitle: Automated penetration testing based on action clipping and decomposition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the continuous development of network technologies, an increasing number of network devices are facing severe security threats, making it imperative to enhance the stability and reliability of network infrastructure. Automated penetration testing, which evaluates network security from the perspective of an attacker, faces challenges such as excessively large action spaces and insufficient utilization of historical information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Algorithm based on Action Decomposition and Clipping (HRLCD) to tackle the problem of poor decision-making performance in large-scale network environments. Firstly, HRLCD combines historical state representation with a curiosity-driven mechanism to optimize action selection strategies and improve the performance of the agent in penetration testing tasks. Secondly, the HRLCD algorithm employs an action clipping mechanism, which eliminates inefficient actions based on historical rewards, thus reducing the agent’s action space and enhancing decision-making efficiency. Finally, HRLCD introduces a hierarchical strategy framework that divides the decision-making process into highlevel and low-level strategies, with the former responsible for global decisions and the latter for specific action execution. This hierarchical structure not only improves task processing efficiency but also enhances the system’s adaptability and flexibility. In the POMDP-based decision model for penetration testing, this method effectively accelerates the training process and improves the accuracy of the policy. Experimental results show that the HRLCD algorithm significantly outperforms traditional methods in decision-making performance in penetration testing tasks, providing new insights for the application of reinforcement learning in the field of network security.

articleTitle: Multilevel Dual Attention Residual Network for Scene Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In this paper, we harness the self-attention mechanism and the integration of multi-scale features to efectively capture rich contextual information, aiming to address the challenge of dense classification. We introduce a novel multi-level dual-attention residual network (MDARNet). This network is designed to adaptively combine local and global features, as well as low-level texture features and high-level semantic features. Specifically, we adopt the U-net as the fundamental model infrastructure. Then, we incorporate spatial attention modules and channel attention modules within the ResNet structure. This enables the selective aggregation of features at every position and across every channel. Notably, we manage to preserve the learned spatial attention matrix (PAM) and channel attention matrix (CAM) of the two attention modules with an extremely negligible storage cost. We not only carry out feature fusion via skip connections to capture contextual information comprehensively, but also utilize the attention matrix derived from low-level texture features to guide and supervise the attention calculation of high-level semantic features. As a result, we are able to obtain more precise segmentation outcomes. We conduct simulation experiments on the Cityscapes dataset, PASCAL VOC2012, and PASCAL Context datasets, and achieve state-of-the-art segmentation results.

articleTitle: Quantum Neutrino Optimization Algorithm and Its Application in Fault Diagnosis of All-Electric Trawler Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The all-electric trawler power system exhibits complex characteristics such as multi-device coupling, multitimescale dynamic responses, and extensive heterogeneous data processing. Traditional fault diagnosis methods face challenges including slow convergence and susceptibility to local optima. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Quantum Neutrino Optimization Algorithm (QNOA) that integrates quantum computing and neutrino entanglement characteristics, aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of fault diagnosis. QNOA employs quantum state array encoding to represent the solution space, leveraging quantum superposition states for parallel searches of high-dimensional data. By incorporating a neutrino spin regulation factor to dynamically adjust qubit probability amplitudes, the algorithm simulates the global entanglement behavior of neutrino weak interactions, thereby strengthening its global search capability and effectively balancing exploration and exploitation. Experimental results demonstrate that QNOA achieves over $30 \%$ reduction in average fitness values and more than $25 \%$ improvement in average convergence speed compared to traditional algorithms (e.g., Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization) on benchmark functions such as Sphere and Rosenbrock, particularly excelling in multimodal function optimization. Further application to fault diagnosis in all-electric trawler power systems-through equipment state encoding, objective function modeling, and simulation case studiesvalidates that QNOA can accurately locate diverse faults, including transformer short circuits, circuit breaker failures, and load overcurrents, with convergence to the optimal solution within 20-30 iterations. The findings confirm the high efficiency and robustness of QNOA in complex power system fault diagnosis, providing innovative technical support for intelligent ship operation and maintenance.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization Algorithm for Position Adjustment and Sub-band Allocation of UAV-BSs Based on Clustering and Graph Coloring
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) as aerial base stations capitalizes on their inherent advantages of low deployment costs and high operational flexibility, thereby addressing diverse networking communication requirements in various emergency situations. Within the scenario of UAV base station (UAV-BS) communication networks, optimal UAV-BSs distribution and sub-band allocation can fully exploit the flexibility of UAV-BSs while mitigating dynamic strong interference, significantly improving network coverage and service performance. This study decouples the problems of UAV-BS position optimization and sub-band allocation, introducing an algorithm based on user clustering and graph coloring problem for position adjustment and sub-band allocation. The objective is to improve both the extent of user coverage and the average user transmission rates. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves extensive and uniform user coverage while effectively enhancing the average user transmission rate.

articleTitle: TOOA-DDPG: A Joint Optimization Method of Task Offloading and Obstacle Avoidance Strategy for Autonomous Driving Vehicles Based on DDPG
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Autonomous driving systems use online path planning with global information to determine optimal routes. However, during movement between adjacent nodes, vehicle dynamics and kinematic constraints must be considered for effective obstacle avoidance. This paper proposes an online optimization algorithm for task offloading and obstacle avoidance, named TOOA-DDPG, based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient network (DDPG). This algorithm jointly optimizes task offloading and obstacle avoidance, enhancing both avoidance efficiency and overall travel performance. The optimization problem involves a complex action space with continuous and discrete variables, further complicated by dynamic traffic and fluctuating wireless conditions. TOOADDPG efficiently handles high-dimensional continuous action spaces by directly outputting deterministic actions, avoiding exhaustive search. Simulations confirm its accuracy and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A General Optimization Method for SpMV Based on Graph Partitioning and Matrix Reordering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rising demand for the performance of sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) in various fields, traditional optimization approaches for SpMV computation, which are designed specifically for certain domains, encounter the issue of limited data applicability. Moreover, as SpMV computation is memory-access intensive, the inefficiency of vector memory access emerges as a significant performance bottleneck. This paper proposes a comprehensive optimization scheme integrating graph partitioning and matrix reordering techniques. By transforming the sparse matrix into a graph and performing partitioning and reordering, the distribution of nonzero elements is effectively changed, the memory access order is adjusted, and the data locality is significantly improved, thereby enhancing the memory access efficiency and overall computational performance. Experimental results show that this method successfully increases the sparsity within the diagonal range by an average of 9.51 times, and the average speedup ratio of the overall SpMV computation on the CPU reaches 1.26, demonstrating strong versatility and laying a solid foundation for the efficient application of SpMV in multiple fields.

articleTitle: Research on Cross-Project Vulnerability Detection Method for Open Source Software
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper centers on applying and advancing Embedding models within open-source software for cross-project vulnerability detection. It reviews relevant studies and delves into how Embedding technology captures open-source software features from multiple angles, such as code structure, community activity, and developer behavior. By transforming high-dimensional sparse data into low-dimensional dense vectors, it enhances the accuracy and reliability of feature representation. Moreover, it comprehensively examines the strengths, limitations, and future research directions of current methods, aiming to offer comprehensive theoretical and practical guidance for the intelligent analysis and security enhancement of open-source software.

articleTitle: Automatic control of unmanned vehicles using DPSN-DDPG
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm (DDPG) is a classical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method that is particularly suitable for solving continuous control problems and has been widely used in autonomous driving. However, the traditional DDPG algorithm suffers from inefficient and ineffective exploration. To solve this problem, an improved DDPG algorithm with dynamic parameter space noise (DPSN) is proposed. In this paper, a framework that incorporates a variational autoencoder (VAE) and hierarchical normalized neural network with DPSN is constructed to achieve automatic control of unmanned vehicles. The experimental results on the Carla platform illustrate the DPSN-DDPG algorithm achieves significant improvements in exploration capability and training efficiency. The unmanned vehicles controlled by DPSN-DDPG can overcome local optimums, achieving higher rewards and completion rates.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv11n-Based Small Object Detection Algorithm from UAV Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, drone technology is playing an increasingly important role in various fields such as environmental monitoring, agricultural protection, and emergency rescue. Aerial images captured by drones provide valuable data resources due to their unique perspectives and wide coverage. However, small object detection in drone aerial images remains a major technological bottleneck due to challenges such as small target sizes, inconspicuous features, and complex backgrounds. To address this issue, this study proposes an improved YOLOv11n-based small object detection algorithm to enhance detection accuracy from the UAV perspective. First, we introduce the C3k2-AD module, which enhances feature extraction through local perception, attention mechanisms, and multilayer perceptrons (MLP) to better capture object shape features at different viewing distances in UAV imagery. Second, to improve the model’s ability to detect small objects, we incorporate the SBA module in the Neck part of the model and add a P2 small object detection head in the Head section, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to distinguish and accurately detect targets in different regions. Experimental results on the VisDrone2019 dataset demonstrate that the improved YOLOv11n algorithm outperforms other models in small object detection accuracy. Specifically, the proposed model achieves an $\mathrm{mAP} \text{@} 0.5$ of $39.4 \%$, a precision of $48.8 \%$, and a recall of $38.6 \%$, representing improvements of $6.7 \%, 4.8 \%$, and $5.8 \%$, respectively, compared to the baseline model.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Cigarette Demand Forecasting: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study puts forward a framework driven by AI, aimed at forecasting cigarette sales through combining various machine learning and deep learning models in a bid to enhance the precision and interpretability of forecasts. Different algorithms are evaluated, which includes models like Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Trees, XGBoost, LightGBM, Support Vector Machine, and Artificial Neural Networks, to make predictions about cigarette demand. It is indicated that models such as RF, GBT, XGBoost, and LightGBM offer forecasts that are quite accurate overall, displaying low RMSE and high $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ values, hence they become the selected models for this forecasting endeavor. Analysis surrounding feature importance indicates that economic factors, including aspects like product category, income, and GDP, are significant to consider when predicting cigarette sales. The benefits of employing an ensemble-based approach are emphasized, which combines different model strengths in pursuit of greater robustness and adaptability, particularly in rapidly changing market situations. This framework holds insights that might be of value to stakeholders involved in the tobacco industry, potentially assisting in the refinement of marketing and distribution strategies that they use. There could be future research that thinks about integrating real-time data along with enhancements in deep learning methods for better accommodating the complexities of the market.

articleTitle: A Review of Research on Attention Mechanisms in Sentiment Analysis of Focused Texts
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, society and the explosive growth of the number of texts in today’s society, text sentiment analysis is becoming more and more important in various fields such as business, culture and entertainment, medical treatment, and public opinion monitoring, etc., and the attention mechanism, as an essential and key analyzing mechanism in sentiment analysis, is more worthy of this research’s in-depth study. This thesis mainly investigates the research status, mechanism application and development prospect of attention mechanism in the field of sentiment analysis, aiming to provide a more comprehensive introduction and overview of the attention mechanism, hoping to help people understand the attention mechanism in sentiment analysis in a more systematic way, while providing valuable ideas and directions for the development of the field. Studies have shown that attention mechanisms have flourished in the field of sentiment analysis in recent years, deriving many valuable, high-level, and complex modeling applications, which have greatly promoted and facilitated the processing and computation of sentiment analysis. Currently, the attention mechanism still struggles with processing highly complex texts, lacks sufficient interpretability in weight assignments, and faces challenges in efficiently integrating multimodal information.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization Design of Process Parameters for Organics Removal from Industrial Waste Salt by Pyrolysis-Oxidation Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Efficient removal of organic impurities is essential for the resourceful utilization of industrial waste salt. Low-temperature pyrolysis-high-temperature oxidation is an effective approach; However, issues such as suboptimal parameter matching, low removal efficiency, and high energy consumption remain. This study employs machine learning and multi-objective optimization algorithms to enhance process efficiency and reduce energy consumption. Organic removal rate and energy consumption per gram are set as optimization objectives, while pyrolysis temperature, pyrolysis time, oxidation temperature, oxidation time, and air flow rate are considered optimization variables. A BP neural network combined with an improved Tuna Swarm Optimization algorithm (TSO-BPNN) is developed based on experimental data. NSGA-II is applied to obtain Pareto-optimal solutions, which are further refined using the CRITIC-TOPSIS evaluation model. Results indicate that the improved TSO-optimized BP neural network improves prediction accuracy with lower error metrics, achieving an average optimization improvement of $19.81 \%$ in organic removal rate and $17.21 \%$ in energy consumption per gram. The optimized process parameters are pyrolysis temperature of $279^{\circ} \text{C}$, pyrolysis time of 30 min, oxidation temperature of $552^{\circ} \text{C}$, oxidation time of 16 min, and air flow rate of $215 \text{ml} / \text{min}$, leading to an increase in organic removal rate to $91.2 \%$ and a reduction in energy consumption per gram to $1.865 \text{kW} / \text{g}$, representing improvements of $6.29 \%$ and $8.04 \%$, respectively.

articleTitle: MolBFN: Equivariant Bayesian Flow Networks for 3D Molecule Generation
