publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This work introduces MolBFN, a new generative SE(3)-equivariant model utilizing Bayesian Flow Networks (BFNs), which models the parameters of molecule distribution in a continuous and differentiable way. Unlike most of previous models adding chemical bonds via predefined rules, MolBFN integrates dynamic interactions between atom and chemical bonds by utilizing an innovative graph neural network which updates both atom and bond representations during message passing simultaneously. MolBFN unifies the probabilistic distribution modeling across various modalities of atoms and bonds by maintaining a coherent and continuous representation between atoms and bonds while preserving SE(3)-equivariance. Experimental results demonstrate that MolBFN can generate molecules with significantly better validity and stability scores.

articleTitle: Fault identification of optical communication network based on machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: In order to accurately diagnose optical communication system faults and ensure the stable operation of optical communication system, the fault diagnosis method of optical communication system based on Gaussian weighted KNN is studied. This method is developed with the aim of enhancing the precision and reliability of fault detection within optical networks. By leveraging the Gaussian weighted KNN algorithm, which is a machine learning technique, the system is able to classify optical communication faults more effectively. The Gaussian weighted KNN algorithm is particularly useful in this context because it assigns weights to the neighboring data points based on their distance from the query point, which in this case is the fault to be diagnosed. This allows the algorithm to give more importance to the faults that are more similar to the one being analyzed, thus improving the accuracy of the classification process. Based on the analysis of the module composition of optical communication system, Gaussian weighted KNN algorithm is used to classify optical communication faults. This involves breaking down the optical communication system into its constituent modules and analyzing each module’s role and potential points of failure. By understanding the system at this granular level, the fault diagnosis method can be tailored to the specific characteristics of each module, thereby enhancing the overall diagnostic capability. Experimental results show that the accuracy of this method is 98.92%. This high level of accuracy indicates that the Gaussian weighted KNN-based fault diagnosis method is highly effective in identifying and classifying faults within optical communication systems.

articleTitle: An Improved Discrete Marine Predator Algorithm for Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) is a classic discrete optimization problem that finds widespread application in logistics, route planning, and other fields. Although traditional optimization methods have performed well in solving TSP, their computational complexity often limits their applicability to large-scale problems. This paper proposes an Improved Discrete Marine Predator Algorithm (IDMPA) to address the TSP. By introducing concepts such as rank-based encoding, equidistant decoding, and sliding alignment, this work extends the continuous optimization capabilities of the original Marine Predator Algorithm(MPA) into the discrete domain. Additionally, the method integrates a 2-Opt algorithm for local search optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the IDMPA exhibits superior performance across multiple instances in the TSPLIB library, significantly enhancing both solution efficiency and quality. These findings suggest that the IDMPA not only effectively addresses the TSP but also offers a promising approach for tackling other discrete optimization problems.

articleTitle: Personalized Federated Learning Privacy with Adaptive Distillation and Robust Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Federated learning has been shown to alleviate the “data silo” problem; however, it is still vulnerable to threats such as gradient leakage and Byzantine attacks. To address these concerns, a personalized federation privacy protection scheme based on adaptive distillation and robust aggregation has been proposed. This scheme involves the construction of a learnable temperature parameter training strategy in the distillation process, which involves the participation of the local model in the gradient update of the global model. This approach enables the personalization of the local model while ensuring the privacy of the local client. Second, a short-term history gradient is introduced in the aggregation phase to filter low-quality clients, and a paradigm-based adaptive gradient filtering dynamically adjusts the threshold to filter malicious gradients to improve the global model accuracy. Finally, the security analysis shows that honest and curious servers cannot recover data from gradients, and the aggregation phase effectively reduces the impact of unreliable and malicious clients on the global model. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly enhances the global model accuracy under various types of attacks, including both typical and complex attacks, under both IID and Non-IID conditions.

articleTitle: A lightweight drift sensing method for UASN based on sliding window-LSTM cooperative strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: As the rapid growth in marine resource development and underwater national defense security demands, the large-scale deployment of underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASN) has made them critical information infrastructure, with dynamic detection of node vulnerabilities becoming a core challenge for ensuring network reliability. In complex underwater environments, the time-varying nature of acoustic channels, equipment performance degradation, and the continuous evolution of new network attacks lead to significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity in node behavior data. Traditional static detection models struggle to distinguish between environmental noise interference and malicious attack behaviors, leading to severe misjudgments and missed detections. To address the challenges of intrusion detection in dynamic environments within underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASN), this paper proposes a hybrid mechanism based on sliding window dynamic threshold adjustment and LSTM drift trend prediction. By statistically analyzing recent data distribution characteristics, it dynamically adjusts the drift detection threshold to balance sensitivity and stability. At the same time, a lightweight LSTM model is used to learn historical drift patterns, predict future drift trends, and trigger model updates in advance. The prediction results are combined with the sliding window threshold to achieve “prediction-response” collaborative decision-making, significantly reducing detection latency. This enhances the real-time performance and robustness of the Adaptive Intrusion Detection System (AIDPS).

articleTitle: Electronic Control Unit Authentication Mechanism Based on Endogenous Security
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent Internet-connected vehicles, the electronic control unit (ECU), as a core component of the automotive electronic system, plays a key role in the control and monitoring of vehicle sub systems. The ECU mainly relies on the controller local area network (LAN) bus ID for identification and communication, and an attacker can realize an attack on the ECU communication system by tampering with the ID, which has a certain security risk. Aiming at the problem of ECU trusted authentication, this study proposes an ECU authentication mechanism based on endogenous security theory. The mechanism adopts a dual authentication architecture: the first one is access authentication, and the second one is message authentication based on dynamic heterogeneous redundancy (DHR) architecture. By constructing the dual authentication system, the security of ECU authentication and message transmission is effectively improved. Simulation experiments show that the proposed authentication mechanism ensures the credibility and strong robustness of ECU authentication.

articleTitle: A Deepfake Detection Model Based on Xception and Self-Correcting Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the widespread use of AI technology, the cost of generating fake videos has decreased, and the realism of these fakes has significantly improved. This poses a serious threat to the authenticity of various fields such as social media, news dissemination, and film production. Furthermore, as video on many modern mobile devices is often compressed to reduce transmission bandwidth, low-quality fake videos are being widely circulated. Although detection techniques for high-quality videos have made progress, the technology for detecting fake low-quality videos remains lacking. Additionally, current fake detection methods perform well on single datasets, but their accuracy significantly drops when tested across different datasets. To address this issue, this paper proposes a deepfake detection model based on Xception and self-correcting convolutional networks. The model consists of a dual-branch structure: one branch is composed of a self-correcting convolutional network for extracting inconsistent feature information, while the other branch is based on an improved Xception network to capture deeper feature representations while reducing computational complexity and enhancing model efficiency. Finally, the extracted features are embedded into a Residual Network. To validate the effectiveness of the algorithm, the model was tested on the FaceForensics ++ and Celeb-DF datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed detection method outperforms other methods and demonstrates good detection performance across multiple datasets, further proving the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: STAE-APT: An APT Detection Method Based on Long-Term Behavioral Features from Provenance Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Due to the characteristics of long-term latency and multi-stage attacks, long-term behavioral features are crucial for Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) detection. Existing research struggles to effectively extract long-term behavioral features and suffers from slow detection speeds. To address these issues, we introduce STAE-APT, a novel APT detection method leveraging provenance graph analysis. This method utilizes a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN)-enhanced autoencoder (TCN-AE) to capture global temporal information. Simultaneously, a channel attention mechanism is introduced to highlight local critical behavioral features, thereby enhancing the feature representation capability for long-term behaviors. Furthermore, the parallel convolution characteristic of the TCN model is leveraged to significantly improve the detection speed. Evaluations on four public datasets, compared against methods like UNICORN and SeqNet, demonstrate STAE-APT’s superior performance, achieving accuracies of $99.88 \%, 99.5 \%, 99.1 \%$, and $98.38 \%$, respectively, alongside a $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$ reduction in detection time.

articleTitle: Research on Wind Power Prediction Based on RIME-CNN-LSTM-Attention Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the continuous growth of energy demand and the proposal of carbon emission reduction target in our country, wind power, as an important green renewable energy, has become a key way to achieve the target. However, the high volatility of wind power brings challenges to the deep integration and efficient utilization of green energy system, and also causes great pressure on the stable operation of the power system. In this paper, the wind power prediction method based on RIME-CNN-LSTM-Attention model is used. Firstly, the model combines CNN, LSTM and Attention mechanism, which can effectively extract local features, model timing dependencies and focus on key moment features, so as to optimize wind power prediction. Then, by introducing the frost ice optimization algorithm for global search, the hyperparameters of the model were adjusted to ensure the best configuration of the model, so as to improve the prediction accuracy and stability. Finally, compared with four groups of classical models, the results show that the evaluation index of the proposed model is more accurate and stable, and it has significant advantages in generalization ability. This method has broad application prospects in wind power generation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Cross-Modal Image-Text Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a improved deep learning-based multimodal information fusion method for cross-modal image-text retrieval. we investigate various fusion strategies, including early, intermediate, and late fusion, along with attention mechanisms, and analyze the role of batch normalization in stabilizing training. The proposed method enables direct learning of effective joint representations, minimizing manual feature engineering. Benchmarked against DCCA, Multi-DBN, and Deep-SM on four datasets derived from Flickr30k, our approach achieves an average retrieval accuracy of $91.08 \%$, outperforming the baselines by 7.58, 6.04, and 3.19 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the superior performance of our method in crossmodal image-text retrieval.

articleTitle: Accident LLM: A multimodal large language model of accident description based on Inter-Frame Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Addressing the technical bottlenecks in traffic accident video analysis and liability determination, this study proposes Accident LLM—a multi-modal large language model based on an inter-frame attention mechanism. This model generates interframe feature vectors by calculating the local correlation of adjacent frames, significantly reducing the complexity of spatial-temporal modeling, and optimizes the positional encoding strategy to enhance the recognition ability of spatial relationships such as traffic signs and vehicle trajectories. Experiments show that the model outperforms existing methods on various metrics (BLEU-4, METEOR, etc.) on the self-built accident datasets and demonstrates good generalization on general datasets (TVSum, MSRVTT). The research provides an efficient technical framework for intelligent liability determination systems, and future service closed-loop can be further optimized through legal knowledge injection and interactive dialogue.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv10 Algorithm for Kitchen Hygiene and Safety Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Food hygiene and safety is a critical issue in global public health, particularly in the operational environment of restaurant kitchens where hygiene and safety standards are crucial. With the rapid development of the food industry, traditional manual supervision methods are struggling to cope with the increasingly complex challenges of food hygiene and safety. To address the issue of food hygiene and safety monitoring in kitchen environments, an improved YOLOv10 model is proposed. By incorporating a Global Attention Mechanism (GAM), the model enhances its ability to capture spatial-channel interactions across the entire feature map, improving accuracy in detecting small objects. Additionally, the CIoU loss function is replaced with Wise-IoU (WIoU), which dynamically adjusts gradient gains to reduce the impact of low-quality samples on model training, further enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of kitchen hygiene and safety monitoring. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves high accuracy in complex backgrounds and diverse scenarios, particularly in identifying risk behaviors such as bare skin, unmasked individuals, and rodent activity, with a 2.2 percentage point increase in accuracy compared to the original YOLOv10.

articleTitle: ST3GAN: A Chinese Character Font Generation Model Combining Structural-Stroke Consistency Loss and Style Perception Loss
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning technologies, Chinese character font generation based on artificial intelligence has become a hot research topic. However, the core challenge in Chinese character font generation lies in how to simultaneously maintain structural rationality and style consistency during the generation process. Currently, many studies focus primarily on improving the overall quality of the generated images, with less attention given to the accurate preservation of the intrinsic structural features and writing style of Chinese characters. To address this challenge, a novel Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) model, ST3GAN, is proposed. This model introduces structural stroke consistency loss and style perception loss, aiming to enhance the generator’s deep understanding and expression of Chinese character structure and style. Specifically, the structural stroke consistency loss combines structural encoding and stroke encoding to ensure the accuracy of stroke count and layout in the generated characters, while the style perception loss uses the Gram matrix to measure the similarity between the generated image and the target style, thereby enhancing style consistency. Experimental results show that ST3GAN significantly improves the quality of generated images, especially in terms of structural rationality and style consistency, demonstrating a strong advantage over existing methods in generation performance.

articleTitle: FuDA-YOLO: Low-light Object Detection using Multi-scale Fusion Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Low-light Object Detection (LOD) is a significant research field in computer vision. In some application fields of automatic driving, security monitoring and so on, it has great value and broad prospect. Low-light conditions means that environment light is insufficient, the loss of image information is serious, and the noise increases. However, most of the traditional object detection methods consider only normal light conditions and their models are also trained that way, leading to a poor performance. A common solution is to use image enhancement technology to improve the brightness of an image and furthest restore its details, and then use a normal object detection network to complete the detection task. These methods cannot well meet the real-time requirements and the evaluation criteria of image enhancement are mostly based on human vision, not suitable for machine vision tasks. Moreover, one of the difficulties of LOD is the lack of annotation data, and it is difficult to collect or make new low-light datasets. To solve these problems, we propose FuDA-YOLO, a LOD method by introducing unsupervised domain adaptation into the YOLO network. The main structure of our FuDA-YOLO is a Multi-scale Fusion Domain Adaptation Module combined with YOLOv8n, to reduce the domain difference between source and target domains. We have carried out a series of experiments to prove that our method can significantly improve model’s detection accuracy, domain adaptation ability and inference speed.

articleTitle: An Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for Whole Process Open Channel in D2D
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Since IoT relies on wireless and shared networks, how to address security issues becomes a challenging problem as the number of devices increases. The most promising scenario in the IoT environment is device-to-device (D2D) communication, while existing security protocols on D2D communication rely on secure channels for the registration phase, which fails to fit real application scenarios. To solve this problem, an authentication and key agreement protocol (OC-AKA) for the whole process of D2D open channel is proposed: based on Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), a light-weight security protocol without the need of relying on the secure channel is designed to ensure that the device obtains key pairs and accomplishes authentication and key negotiation without relying on a secure channel. Finally, the security of the protocol is verified using the formal method BAN logic, the model detection tool Scyther, and the non-formal approach, and the analysis results show that the OC-AKA protocol can effectively resist man-in-the-middle attacks, replay attacks, and internal privilege attacks. In order to verify the performance of OC-AKA protocol.

articleTitle: SLCF: Security-Level-Aware Microarchitectural Cleaning for Efficient Time Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: The primary challenge in current microarchitectural security is that timing attacks can leak sensitive information across security domain boundaries, severely threatening system security. These attacks typically exploit microarchitectural features of shared processor resources (such as caches, branch predictors, etc.) to infer secret data in another security domain by measuring operation latency. While existing temporal partitioning techniques provide some protection, they generally adopt coarse-grained “one-size-fits-all” cleaning strategies that indiscriminately clear all microarchitectural states, causing significant performance degradation in high-performance out-of-order processors. This paper proposes a Security-LevelAware Cleaning Fence mechanism (SLCF) that dynamically selects the cleaning scope based on the processor’s security level: in user mode, only the L1 data cache is cleaned, while in supervisor mode, comprehensive microarchitectural state cleaning is performed. Experimental results on the OpenC910 RISC-V processor demonstrate that this mechanism effectively defends against microarchitectural timing channel attacks while controlling performance overhead to an extremely low level. The user mode SLCF successfully closes the L1D cache timing channel with an average performance overhead of only $0.53 \%$, while the supervisor mode SLCF provides comprehensive protection by closing all microarchitectural timing channels with a performance overhead of $1.18 \%$. This mechanism ensures system security while minimizing the impact of defensive measures on system performance.

articleTitle: Study on the Distribution Characteristics and Dynamic Evolution of Green Buildings in China Based on the K-means Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the concept of green and sustainable development, the gap of green building growth among provinces in China is becoming increasingly obvious. Based on the data of wastewater discharge, air pollution and urban environmental infrastructure investment in China Statistical Yearbook, K-means clustering algorithm is used to classify the distribution of green buildings, and the key influencing factors and dynamic evolution trend are analyzed. At the same time, focusing on the energy consumption of each region, PCA main city analysis is used to study the main indicators affecting the green performance of buildings, and the differences and connections of these analysis methods are analyzed in depth. The results show that: (1) There are obvious regional differences. Green building development in eastern coastal and highly urbanized areas is faster (such as Yangtze River Delta and Pearl River Delta), while that in northwest and underdeveloped areas is slower. (2) Industrial wastewater emission, sulfur dioxide emission, industrial smoke (dust) emission and population density are the main energy indicators affecting the green performance of buildings.(3) Economic development, policy support, environmental governance and market demand are key determinants of green building concentration. Efficient provinces (e.g. Beijing, Shanghai) benefit from strong economic fundamentals, policy incentives, advanced environmental management and high market demand, making them leaders in green building development. (4)The evolution of green building has experienced three stages: policy-driven, market-led and technology-driven. In the early stages, government policies play a crucial role; in the medium stage, market demand becomes the main driving force; in the later stage, technological innovation, resource recycling and green social system development become key factors for sustainable growth. In the future, provinces should adopt collaborative innovation, policy optimization and resource sharing strategies to promote the development of high-quality green buildings and contribute to carbon neutrality goals and ecological sustainability.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction of Complex Systems Based on Integrated Machine Learning: A Case Study of the Probability of Flood Occurrence
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: With the aggravation of global climate change and human activities, the frequency and intensity of flood disasters have been continuously increasing, causing huge losses to human society. Accurately predicting the probability of flood occurrence is crucial for flood prevention and disaster reduction. This paper focuses on the uncertainty prediction of complex systems, taking the prediction of flood occurrence probability as a specific case. Integrated machine learning methods, combined with techniques such as correlation analysis, hierarchical clustering, and the entropy-weight TOPSIS method, are used to deeply analyze flood disaster data and construct an efficient prediction model. The research results show that the integrated machine learning model performs remarkably well in predicting the probability of flood occurrence, providing a scientific basis for the prevention and response to flood disasters. It also offers useful references for research in the field of uncertainty prediction of complex systems.
